deals.body:
Best Japanese food brand openings in Singapore in 2026
Our little red dot is home to a variety of cuisines from all over the world, yet in the midst of it all, Japanese food seems to steal our hearts time and time again. With Japan being one of Singaporeans’ go-to travel destinations, it’s no surprise that there’s been a recent wave of Japanese brands making their debut here. From famous gyudon to matcha desserts and Ginza-famous sandos, here’s our compilation of the best new Japanese eateries in 2026 .
1. Matsuya
Image credit: u/kccz123 via Reddit
If you’re a frequent Japan-goer, you’d know that Matsuya is one of Japan’s most popular gyudon chains. Now, you can save your flight to Japan, as they’re set to make their arrival at Suntec City sometime in November 2026 . This would mark the completion of the ‘big 3’ gyudon chains in SG, alongside Sukiya and Yoshinoya.
Image credit: Japan Journeys
While we still don’t know much about the Singapore outlet, Matsuya is well-loved and known for its affordable gyudon bowls. A full meal in Japan costs roughly between ¥400 and ¥1000 , which converts to about S$3.25 to S$8.10 . The top pick here is the classic Beef Bowl (¥480) that’s stewed with onions in a sweet soy sauce. For a heartier option, go for their selection of curry bowls, such as Beef Curry and Rice (¥680) or Beef Curry with Cheese (¥950) .
Read our Matsuya feature .
Address: 3 Temasek Boulevard, #B1-125 (Tower 2), Singapore 038983
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Matsuya is not halal-certified.
Popular Japanese Gyudon Chain To Open At Suntec In Nov 2026
2. I’m Donut
Image credit: The New Yorker
Adding to the line-up of Japanese doughnut chains, I’m Donut will be making its debut in Singapore at ION Orchard , set to open in December 2026 . The brand has over 10 outlets across Japan and is best known for their fluffy nama doughnuts. What sets them apart is their brioche dough, made with pumpkin and fermented at low temperatures before it gets fried at high heat.
Image credit: I’m Donut
Though their Singapore menu is still unconfirmed, we presume that their best-selling powdered sugar doughnut, the I’m Donut? Original (price TBD) , will make an appearance. Another top pick would be the Custard Cream (price TBD) , filled generously with Diplomat cream. The I’m Donut? Matcha (price TBD) would be perfect for fellow matcha fans, starring a kneaded dough coated in Yame matcha powder from Fukuoka. FYI: everything here is made handmade in-house, from the dough to the fillings and even the toppings!
Check out our I’m Donut coverage .
Address: 2 Orchard Turn, #B2-19, ION Orchard, Singapore 238801
Opening hours: TBD
Website
I’m Donut is not halal-certified.
Viral Japanese Chain I’m Donut To Open At ION Orchard
3. Age.3
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
Another Japanese eatery landing at ION Orchard in mid-November 2026 is Age.3 , a fried sando shop hailing all the way from Ginza. The brand rose to fame for its crispy golden sando boasting a soft and chewy centre, with locals braving the queues of up to two hours just to try them.
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
Going all-out for their debut, the Singapore menu will feature a whopping 34 flavours. For something sweet and classic, opt for the Whipped Cream Sando (price TBD) that’s made with low-sugar cream that’s whipped by hand. Other interesting flavours include the Creme Brulee Sando (price TBD) , Mont Blanc (price TBD) , and Chocolate Strawberry (price TBD) . Their savoury choices are just as extensive, including the Beef Short Rib Yakiniku Sando (price TBD) served with barbecue sauce and a soft-cooked egg, Grilled Keema Curry (price TBD) , and Grilled Cheese with Smoked Salmon (price TBD) .
Read our Age.3 feature .
Address: ION Orchard, Singapore 238801
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Age.3 is not halal-certified.
Viral Japanese Fried Sando Shop Age.3 To Open At ION Orchard With 34 Flavours
4. O/sio
Image credit: O/sio
Following our review of Sio Pasta —an Italian-inspired pasta concept helmed by Michelin-approved Japanese chef Shusaku Toba—earlier this year, its sister eatery, O/Sio , is set to launch its first overseas eatery in Tanjong Pagar on 4 November 2026 . O/Sio offers hearty Italian fare with a Japanese twist, from fresh pasta to charcoal-grilled meats, alongside a complementary wine programme curated by Chef Toba himself.
Image credit: O/sio
Look forward to mains starting from $18.80 . Special offerings include the Singapore-exclusive Smoked Truffle Carbonara (price TBD) for a decadent pairing of creamy pasta and earthy black truffle shavings. If you enjoy seafood, the Seafood Pomodoro (price TBD) would be right up your alley. They also have the fan-favourite Charcoal-grilled Angus Beef Steak (price TBD) that’s served with a side of crispy fries.
Read our O/sio feature .
Address: 38 Tanjong Pagar Road, Singapore 088461
Opening hours: TBD
Tel: 8072 9512
Website
O/Sio is not halal-certified.

Pasta Bar on Keong Saik Road launches a five-course November Experience Menu on 5 November at S$88++ a person, with a minimum of two diners, on Pasta Bar’s website . The menu moves through regional Italian dishes, from the Amalfi Coast to Emilia-Romagna and Sicily.
Handmade pasta at Pasta Bar. Photo: Pasta Bar
Starters
The meal opens with three stuzzichini. A uni toast puts bafun uni on brioche with whipped brown butter and chives. Arancini come with pear mostarda and prosciutto, and gnocco fritto, the fried Italian dough, is paired with whipped feta and hot honey.
The pasta courses
• Pasta al limone: bronze die-cut eggless maccheroni with preserved lemon and pecorino romano, served in a pecorino wheel
• Tortellini in brodo: guinea fowl tortellini in consommé with pickled chayote, charred pearl onions, Thai basil, coriander and chilli sauce, a nod to Vietnamese pho
• Scoglio nero: squid ink linguine with seafood sofrito, clam jus, cockles and bincho-grilled barramundi
• Ossobuco: saffron sfoglia sheets with braised beef cheeks, bone marrow relish, shaved parmigiano and red wine jus
Pasta dishes at Pasta Bar on Keong Saik Road. Photo: Pasta Bar
The ossobuco is the kitchen’s take on the Milanese classic, with the usual saffron risotto swapped for fresh saffron pasta sheets. The pasta al limone is finished in the cheese wheel, a nod to the Amalfi Coast, where fresh lemons sit at the centre of the cooking. Scoglio, the restaurant explains, is a Southern Italian seafood dish rooted in the coastal kitchens of Campania, Puglia and Sicily.
Dessert
The fifth course is DIY cannoli. Diners fill homemade shells with sheep’s ricotta and top them with chocolate sauce, cocoa nibs, crushed pistachios and amarena cherries. Cannoli trace their origins to Sicily under Arab rule, between the 9th and 11th centuries.
A seafood pasta at Pasta Bar. Photo: Pasta Bar
Booking
Pasta Bar is at 55 Keong Saik Road, #01-05. It opens for dinner daily from 6pm to 10.30pm and for lunch from Tuesday to Saturday, 12pm to 3pm. Reservations go through the restaurant’s website, and the menu starts on 5 November.

A Hot Hideout and PlayMade launch mala pearls
When people online joked about the ultimate Orchard Central itinerary, it went something like this: mala at Yang Guo Fu Mala Tang, a sweet treat at Yo-Chi , and a drink to cool down at Molly Tea or CHAGEE. Now, two brands, A Hot Hideout and PlayMade , are taking things a step further by combining mala and bubble tea into one unlikely creation.
A Hot Hideout Review: Is This Famous SG-Born Mala Chain Still Worth The Hype?
From now till 6 November 2026 , fans can try the new Mala Pearls , available at selected PlayMade and A Hot Hideout outlets. Get them at PlayMade outlets for $1.40 or $1.60 for a medium or large size , respectively, or at A Hot Hideout for $0.60 with drinks and $1.20 with food.
Don’t knock it before you try it; the pearls are perfectly QQ with a slight sweetness, paired with the familiar kick of mala.
Drench them in your mala tang so the pearls soak up all of their collagen goodness and, in turn, lend a hint of sweetness to the broth.
Or if you’re a purist, get them in PlayMade’s signature Taiwan Milk Tea with Mala Pearls for a spicy rendition of the beloved drink. The rich creaminess of the milk tea mellows out the fiery kick of the mala pearls, resulting in an addictive sweet-and-spicy combination.
PlayMade is also bringing back their fan-favourite Pomelo Blossom Milk Tea ($4.90++) —a blend of their smooth milk tea and tangy, refreshing pomelo. You can get it with the new Mala Pearls, or with the brand’s signature Pink Cactus Pearls .
That’s not all: PlayMade is also adding their aforementioned Pink Cactus Pearls to A Hot Hideout’s signature Thai Milk Tea , in both red and green milk tea flavours for just $0.60 . Alternatively, you can also pair the Pink Cactus Pearls with food for just $1.20 .
If you’re unimpressed with the size of the Mala Pearls, go biiig with their Mega Mala Boba (price TBD) , a Halloween-exclusive special that’s only available on 31 October 2026 at selected PlayMade outlets: Tampines 1 , 313@Somerset , Northpoint City , and Westgate .
Imagine a scaled-up version of the same Mala Pearls, with the same chewiness and punchy mala flavours. There are only 10 servings per outlet, so be sure to set your alarms to get there early.
Head down to your nearest A Hot Hideout and Playmade outlet to give this collab a go before it’s too late!
Watch our Instagram coverage .
View this post on Instagram
For more spicy collaborations, check out KFC x Samyang’s new Buldak Carbonara menu item . In other exciting news, read our guide to the best Japanese food brand openings .

PlayMade is not halal-certified.

Chipotle Mexican Grill will open in Singapore in 2027
Image credit: @chipotle
Chipotle fans, here’s an update on that Singapore opening we told you about last year: the timeline’s officially been pushed back. Chipotle Mexican Grill has confirmed that its first Singapore restaurant will now open in 2027 , a year later than the 2026 date we first reported.
Jewel Changi Food Guide: 40 Best Spots For Truffle Gyudon, Mochi Donuts and More
Here’s the latest update: The burrito chain will open at Jewel Changi Airport !
View this post on Instagram
The delay comes as Chipotle finally kicks off its actual Asia debut, and Singapore, it turns out, isn’t first in line after all.
Image credit: @chipotle
Chipotle opened its first-ever Asia outlet on 2 September 2026 , located along Gangnam-daero in Seoul’s Seocho-gu district. The restaurant runs through a joint venture named S&C Restaurants Holdings, formed with South Korean operator Sangmidang Holdings (formerly SPC Group), the same group behind Shake Shack, Paris Baguette, and Eggslut’s presence in Singapore.
For the uninitiated, Chipotle is a fast-casual Mexican chain known for its customisable burritos, tacos, and rice bowls. It began in 1993 as a lone restaurant in Denver, and has since expanded to include more than 4,200 outlets across the world.
Their menu is slated to be identical to those in the US and internationally. You can expect endless customisability with their build-your-own-meal concept, where they use fresh, responsibly sourced ingredients.
Image credit: @chipotle
You can get fully-stuffed Burritos as well as loaded Burrito Bowls , or if you like your meal light on carbs, you can choose to get their Salads, as well as their Tacos .
All their meats are responsibly raised, including Chicken , Pork Carnitas , Steak , and Barbacoa (braised beef) . They even have plant-based options, including the Sofritas , a plant-based protein, and Veggie , which comes with guacamole and beans.
Image credit: Chipotle
Chipotle will face stiff competition from existing fast-casual Mexican chains in Singapore, such as Australian-born Guzman Y Gomez, and homegrown brand Stuff’d. We’ll update this article once we get more information!
In the meantime, you can follow Chipotle Singapore for the latest updates.
Craving tacos and burritos now? Our round-up of the best Mexican restaurants in Singapore has some solid picks to tide you over.
For more new international openings in Singapore, check out our guide to new Chinese F&B brands in Singapore for 2026 !
Address: TBD
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Chipotle is not halal-certified.

Woksta has wok hei pasta from $7 in Bukit Merah
You’d typically expect pasta with bold flavours and bougie plating to only be found at atas Italian restaurants , but Woksta proves otherwise. This hawker stall at ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre in Bukit Merah has gone viral for its wok-fried pasta that blends the beloved noodle dish with local flavours.
The stall is run by Chef Henry Yong, who used to work at Michelin-approved Scandinavian restaurant Dill. He swapped out the fine dining life for a hawker stall where he can spend more time with his family and return to his first love: cooking with a wok. Despite opening only about a month ago, Woksta has gained traction for their unique local take on pasta, and we had to see if the food was worth the hype.
Woksta’s menu is straightforward, with only three choices available , each plated beautifully and paired with their signature coconut sauce that’s made in-store.
Living up to their name, all their pasta is fried with a wok to achieve wok hei, AKA that char and smoky depth of flavour.
We started our pasta feast with the Curry Fried Chicken ($7) , which was served with generous chunks of fried chicken and a medley of vegetables, including capsicum, zucchini, and onions.
Initially, I was sceptical about how the coconut sauce would pair with the various noodle dishes, but it actually blended well with the curry flavour from the noodles. The sauce was silky smooth and added a lemak touch to the dish, reminiscent of coconut milk.
This dish had the strongest wok hei, as you can see from the char on each strand of pasta.
Each chicken chunk was generously coated with curry powder, adding a subtly spicy kick in each crunchy bite.
Next we tried the Fish & Coconut ($9) . Unlike the other two variations where the coconut sauce is plated on the side, the noodles here were completely doused in the sauce. The sauce was creamy and had a strong coconut taste that was not too cloying. I liked how the onions added a nice crunch to cut through the richness, while also adding a natural sweetness.
In terms of wok hei, this dish didn’t quite have a strong char as it was creamier than the rest, but it was still pleasant to eat.
Though it looks a bit like batang fish at first glance, the fish used here is seabass, fried until golden brown for a crispy exterior. The fish itself was flaky, though it did taste a tad fishy.
Last but not least is the Laksa Seafood ($10) , which turned out to be my favourite of the lot. Though it didn’t taste entirely like laksa, I enjoyed the subtle floral note from the laksa leaves on top and the crunch from the veggies.
The sauce also had a hint of spiciness from the chilli oil. I recommend mixing it all up to marry the flavours.
As a seafood lover, I appreciated the generous portions of both prawns and sotong, which were plump and QQ, giving the dish more texture and mouthfeel.
Overall, I’d say that the food did live up to the hype. I could taste Chef Henry’s heart in each dish, and it’s definitely worth heading down to give it a try for yourself. Do note that they’re only open for three hours per day, so it’s best to come early to beat the lunch crowd.
Check out our Dirty Pasta feature on a home-based pasta store located in Bukit Batok. In other noodle news, our Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee feature has the scoop on their upcoming Century Square outlet.
Address: 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, #01-113, ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, Singapore 150006
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 2pm
Website
Woksta is not halal-certified.
Popular Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee To Open At Century Square This Nov
Photos taken by Genecia Tan.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.

deals.body:
My first visit to Matsuya in Sapporo, Hokkaido, in 2019 was an unforgettable one. Just outside the entrance, my phone flashed an earthquake alert, and seconds later, the ground began shaking furiously beneath my feet. While the locals barely batted an eyelid, I froze in shock.
Thankfully, the piping-hot beef rice bowl waiting for me soon brought me back to my senses. Who knew that 7 years later, I’d be reunited with Matsuya, this time at Suntec City ’s basement in Singapore?
Located directly opposite Fish & Co., the eatery features self-service booths and spacious seating. The menu offerings mimic the ones you’ll find in Japan — an assortment of rice bowls including Unagi and Japanese curry .
Of course, we had to give the classic Gyumeshi Beef Bowl (S$5.50 for small) a try. There are also other sizes available – – – from Medium (S$5.90) to Double (S$10.90) . Savoury and tasty, the thin beef slices went well with the sweet onions and rice. Compared to its competitors, the beef at Matsuya offered a meatier bite with a leaner ratio of fat. We also added a Soft-Boiled Egg (+S$1.50) for maximum indulgence. Trust me, its worth it!
Our favourite was the Gyumeshi topped w/ Green Onion & Mentaiko Mayonnaise (S$8.50 for small) . Don’t be fooled by the intimidating sight of the green onion; it actually works! The combination of spring onions, creamy mentaiko , beef slices, and seaweed had multi layers of flavour that danced in my mouth.
We also tried the Soft Boiled Egg & Hamburg Steak with Tomato Sauce Set (S$13.50) which is known to be very popular in Japan. The meat was juicy and hearty, pairing perfectly with the tomato sauce and runny egg. The set comes with rice, miso soup, and a salad with mashed potato. To switch up the flavour, you can help yourself to the condiments on the table: Ponzu Citrus Sauce , Garlic Flavoured BBQ Sauce , Sesame Sauce , and more!
Come savour 60 years of hard work and dedication at Matsuya. For the best experience, we recommend ordering one variety of beef bowl each to share amongst your dining party.
Do note on the following:
• The restaurant is currently at its soft launch phase and will be operating from 11am to 3pm and 5pm to 11pm only
• The restaurant will be closed on Fri, 30 Oct 2026
• Chicken dishes will not be available during the soft launch and grand opening week
• Grand opening will be on Sat, 31 Oct 2026

Christmas log cakes for 2026 are now on sale at three Singapore hotels, with voco Orchard’s D9 Cakery opening pre-orders on 2 November for a S$115 Strawberry Yuzu Log, on voco Orchard Singapore ‘s festive menu. The Fullerton Hotel has cut its Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log to S$66, and Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium has a new calamansi log at an early-bird S$78.40.
The Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log. Photo: The Fullerton Hotel Singapore
The Fullerton Hotel Singapore
The Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log weighs 900g and comes in red and green. It is built from pistachio joconde, raspberry marmalade and Opalys namelaka. It costs S$66 in the online shop, down from S$88.
Orders need at least four days’ notice, and the last day to order is 21 December. Collection and delivery run from 20 November to 27 December.
Collection is daily from 10am to 7pm at The Fullerton Cake Boutique in the hotel lobby, except on 24 and 25 December, when it moves to the TDB Function Room on B1. Delivery is S$50 nett per location, and free for single orders above S$500 nett.
voco Orchard Singapore
D9 Cakery has two logs this year:
• Strawberry Yuzu Log, S$115: strawberry Bavarian mousse, yuzu curd and Valrhona Manjari ganache
• Mango Lime Gula Melaka Log, S$105: mango and kaffir lime mousse, gula melaka curd, apricot compote and dark chocolate ganache
Pre-orders run from 2 November to 18 December, with collection and delivery from 24 November to 28 December. There is no delivery on 24 and 25 December.
Citibank and OCBC cardholders and IHG One Rewards members get 15 per cent off. The festive menu also has Panettone at S$65, Christmas Stollen at S$40 and Christmas Fruit Cake at S$60. Enquiries go to +65 6730 3392.
The D9 Cakery Christmas menu. Photo: voco Orchard Singapore
Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium
The new Calamansi & Caramel Miso Log Cake weighs 1kg and serves eight to 10. It pairs calamansi with caramel miso.
The regular price is S$98, and the early-bird price on the hotel’s online store is S$78.40.
The Calamansi & Caramel Miso Log Cake. Photo: Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium

Thai Seng Fish Soup opens second outlet in Bugis
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
Fish soup fans are probably well familiar with Thai Seng Fish Soup , which has consistently drawn hour-long queues at Ubi. After more than 20 years, the brand finally expanded to a second location in Bugis in July 2026, so heartlanders in central Singapore can get in on the hype.
https://eatbook.sg/best-fish-soup-singapore/
We also heard that a third location is in the works, so keep your eyes peeled for more information!
Do note that this is not to be confused with Tai Seng Fish Soup , another well-known fish soup stall with a nearly identical name.
Image credit: foodpanda
Thai Seng’s fish soup is popular for its strong umami flavour, which sets it apart from the more traditional, lighter versions of fish soup. They’re also known for using freshly sliced batang fish for a superior taste.
Image credit: foodpanda
The menu is pretty standard, with options including Sliced Fish Soup (from $6), Seafood Soup (from $8), and Fried Fish Bee Hoon Soup (from $6).
Image credit: foodpanda
For a spicy option, the Tom Yum Seafood Soup (from $8.50) is a crowd favourite, thanks to its punchy flavour and balance of sweet, sour, and spicy notes. Other options include Fish Head Bee Hoon (from $6), Fish Belly Soup ($10), Fish Porridge (from $6), Double Fish Soup (from $6), and Sliced Fish Mee Sua (from $6).
Many regulars recommend getting the soup with ee mian and the “egg bomb”—deep-fried egg floss strip— which adds another layer of flavour and depth to the broth.
For more good eats in Bugis, here is a Bugis food guide for $1.80 boat noodles, mala tang and more. And on the topic of popular local stores, the beloved Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee is opening an outlet in Tampines!
Ubi outlet
Address: 3026 Ubi Road 1, #01-146 Industrial Estate, Singapore 408719
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 9:30am to 6:30pm, Sun 9:30am to 2:30pm
Bugis outlet
Address: 269B Queen Street, #01-235 Stall 4, Singapore 182269
Opening hours: Daily 9:30am to 8pm
Website
Thai Seng Fish Soup is not halal-certified.

deals.body:
Nomad Kitchen is a new stall at Taman Jurong
Finding quality Middle Eastern fare in Singapore isn’t always easy. But a stall serving dishes from Iran, Turkey, Italy, Greece, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, and Afghanistan? That’s even harder to come by. So when we came across Nomad Kitchen , we knew we had to check it out.
Located in Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre , the new stall has already earned itself a solid reputation, reportedly selling out daily. Its founder, Fuad Salim, a self-professed F&B nomad, picked up the recipes throughout his 30-year career in hospitality, where he worked as an F&B and hotel manager.
Food at Nomad Kitchen
The menu consists of Afghan Chicken (from $6) from Afghanistan, Saffron Jujeh ($8) from Iran, Iskender ($12) from Turkey, Shakshuka ($7) from Morocco, Lasagna ($8.50) from Italy, Moussaka ($8) from Greece, and finally, rotisserie chicken and street wraps inspired by Saudi Arabia.
Chef Fuad prepares everything from scratch daily, including handmade Lavash flatbreads, grilled meats, kabuli rice, saffron rice, and lasagna.
We started with the $6 portion of Afghan Chicken. For an extra $2.50 , you can get another quarter of the rotisserie chicken, which we thought was extremely generous in this economy.
While I tend to find roast chicken too dry for my liking, this one was juicy, moist, and expertly cooked. The seasoning was flavourful too, with a blend of spices that added depth without being overly salty. However, we found the white meat slightly bland, as most of the seasoning was concentrated on the skin and hadn’t penetrated the meat.
According to the chef, raisins and carrots are integral to an Afghan kabuli rice dish. I could see why: they added a burst of sweetness to the aromatic rice, making for a complex and layered flavour profile.
The Saffron Jujeh was probably my favourite dish—it came with two chunky grilled chicken kebabs, saffron rice, roasted tomatoes and peppers, and a yoghurt sauce. Again, the generous portion size was a pleasant surprise.
The kebabs had a similarly intense spice blend to the rotisserie; however, they were thoroughly marinated, so every bite was full of flavour. The yoghurt-based sauce was tangy and refreshing, but more subtle, which worked well to highlight the kebab rather than overpower it.
The roasted vegetables were smoky and juicy, and good enough to stand alone as a side dish. Traditionally, though, Persians would mash the juicy tomatoes into saffron rice, turning them into a flavourful “sauce”.
Lastly, we tried the lasagna. Most faux-Italian places I know of put an ungodly amount of cheese on their lasagna (I’m not complaining). This one was more well-balanced, with all the elements complementing each other rather than overpowering the dish.
The pasta sheets were quite thick and satisfyingly chewy. They made for a great vessel for the layers of beef ragu, Neapolitan sauce, and bechamel. The dish was savoury and hearty, with hints of sweetness and acidity to balance it out.
Ambience at Nomad Kitchen
Nomad Kitchen is tucked away in the corner of Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre. We arrived around 12:30pm to a short queue and a steady stream of customers.
The market itself was huge and happening, with three stories worth of food and retail stalls. It was relatively well-ventilated, with multiple fans working overtime to combat the Singapore stuffiness.
The market is a 10-minute bus ride or 18-minute walk from Lakeside MRT Station.
Nomad Kitchen – Eatbook Review
I visited Nomad Kitchen with high expectations, knowing Chef Fuad Salim’s hospitality background, and was still pleasantly surprised. Every element of the food was well-cooked and flavourful. The dishes also seemed to stay true to their cultural roots, with ingredients and flavours recreated as authentically as possible.
As a Westie, I will definitely be revisiting to try the rest of the menu.
View this post on Instagram
Check out our Instagram Reel for the full scoop!
If you’re on a hunt for more unique hawkers, check out our pork rib prawn mee review , which features a 90-year-old hawker. And while you’re in the area, here are the best Jurong East food places to visit.
Address: Yung Sheng Road, #02-109 Taman Jurong Market & Food Centre, Singapore 618499
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 10am to 3pm
Website
Nomad Kitchen is Muslim-owned.

Photos taken by Marcus Neo.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.

Messina x Queic cheesecake gelato collab runs till 8 Nov 2026
Image credit: Messina x Queic
PSA: Messina and Queic by Olivia have joined forces on a limited-edition collab with two cheesecake gelato flavours and a pair of ice cream sandwiches, running from 26 October to 8 November 2026 , while stocks last.
Popular Aussie Chain Gelato Messina Opens In Chinatown With Singapore Exclusive Flavours
Queic started as a single shop on Kreta Ayer Road in 2021, spun off from Olivia Restaurant & Lounge, and has since grown to four outlets. Messina, meanwhile, is the Australian gelato chain that landed on Club Street in 2025 and is known for its experimental rotating specials, so the two make a pretty natural pairing.
Image credit: Messina x Queic
First up is BBC (Buttery Blue Cheese) (from $7.50) . The base is a butter pecan gelato with blue cheese worked in, then loaded with chunks of Olivia’s Signature Cheesecake and candied pecans. Expect a salty, savoury edge from the blue cheese, softened by the toasty sweetness of the nuts. If you’re already a fan of Queic’s original cheesecake, this is basically that in scoop form.
Image credit: Messina x Queic
The second flavour, Eazy Brie-zy (from $7.50) , takes its cue from the brie, honey, and fig combo you’d normally find on a cheese board. Australian honey goes into the gelato, which carries a strong brie flavour, with Queic’s Brie Cheesecake chunks, candied walnuts, and swirls of fig jam mixed through. Blue cheese sceptics might find this the easier entry point of the two.
Both gelato flavours are sold by the scoop and in take-home tubs, and only at Messina’s Club Street shop.
Image credit: Messina x Queic
Can’t make it down to Club Street? Queic has its own spin on the collab. The Buttery Blue Cheese Ice Cream Sandwich and Eazy Brie-zy Ice Cream Sandwich feature the matching gelato between two house-made brown butter hazelnut sablé cookies, with a layer of honey lemon caramel. They go for $12 each in-store at the Kreta Ayer , Scotts Square , and JEM outlets.
With only two weeks on the clock, we’d suggest heading down sooner rather than later, especially if you want a tub to bring home.
For more scoops worth the calories, read our guide to the best ice cream cafes in Singapore . Otherwise, read our 12-hour Bugis and CBD itinerary for more food options in the area!

Address: 1 Club Street, Singapore 069400
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 10pm
Website
Gelato Messina is not halal-certified.

Xiao Jiao Tian opens second outlet at Wisma Atria
Image credit: @foodieteng
2026 has seen new Chinese food brands popping up all over Singapore, and the latest to join the lineup is Xiao Jiao Tian . The Sichuan-inspired restaurant has opened its second outlet on the third floor of Wisma Atria , just a short walk from Orchard MRT Station . Their first outlet is located at City Square Mall .
Are Chinese F&B Brands Really “Taking Over Singapore”? Here’s What We Think
Image credit: @op3creative
Xiao Jiao Tian was founded in Fujian in 2013 and has more than 80 kitchens and outlets across China and Singapore to date. While their food is Sichuan-inspired, the flavours are toned down to suit a wider range of tastes. According to the brand, every dish is cooked to order, with no reheating or overnight prep. Customers can even get the dish for free if it doesn’t meet the restaurant’s standards.
Their most well-known dish is the Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli ($39.90++) , where tender bullfrog is simmered in a spicy, tangy pickled chilli broth. Other best sellers include the Crispy Roast Chicken ($45.90++) and Shrimp with Garlic Vermicelli (TBD) —the latter features juicy shrimp baked on a bed of fragrant garlic vermicelli.
Image credit: @gracenomz
If you can handle the spice, we recommend ordering the Chinese Sauerkraut Fish ($29.90++) , which gets you sliced fish poached in a spicy, sour sauerkraut broth. This dish also lets you adjust the spice level according to your preferences.
Image credit: @foodieteng
For something milder, there’s the classic Sweet & Sour Pork ($24.90++) , comprising crispy pork chunks coated in a sweet and tangy sauce.
Image credit: @gracenomz
If that’s not enticing enough, Xiao Jiao Tian has an opening deal for you: get free-flow tea, ice cream, snacks, and rice for just $1.50++ per person , down from the usual price of $3++. You can also sign up for their free membership to get slashed prices on selected dishes.
In more exciting food news, Tiong Bahru Bakery has just launched a giant croissant that’s a whopping 28cm long. If you’re a fan of bubble tea, read our feature on the Playmade x A Hot Hideout collab , which has new mala pearls for a limited time.
Address: 435 Orchard Road, #03-32/33/34, Wisma Atria, Singapore 238877
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 10pm
Website
Xiao Jiao Tian is not halal-certified.
PlayMade Has New Mala Pearls In Collab With A Hot Hideout For A Limited Time

Side Quest – Creative studio & art cafe in Joo Chiat
Joo Chiat is known for its colourful shophouses, heritage spots, and trendy haunts tucked along its streets, from the Museum of Food to a dedicated Samoyed dog cafe .
Joining the neighbourhood’s list of places to check out is Side Quest , a newly reopened art jamming studio that sits atop one of Joo Chiat’s many shophouses, offering a cosy space to let your creative juices flow and design a masterpiece at your own pace.
What is Side Quest?
View this post on Instagram
Founded in 2025, Side Quest was started by 23-year-old Jessica Tay to share her love for art with others and inspire them to explore creativity through craft activities . It began as a mobile business hosting DIY workshops for private birthdays and events all around Singapore, before she decided to open her own studio in Joo Chiat.
Instead of serving food, the art cafe’s menu features a variety of hands-on art projects made for all ages . The space is also designed for visitors to slow down and enjoy creating their own keepsakes without expecting it to be flawless. There are also no formal instructors , so you can work on your crafts without any pressure and let your creativity take the lead.
Image credit: Side Quest via Google Maps
Since reopening on 13th October 2026, Side Quest has introduced a refreshed menu with beginner-friendly workshops and activities , aiming to be a creative third space where you can unwind with friends while trying something new.
What to expect at Side Quest
Unleash your inner artist with painting sessions
Image credit: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
Side Quest offers 6 painting activities , all with materials fully provided, and zero prior art experience needed. Pick up a brush and paint whatever’s on your mind on a blank canvas with the Canvas Painting ($38 for 2 hours) workshop.
Image adapted from: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
For beginners, Figurine Painting ($28 for 1.5 hours) or the crowd-favourite Trinket Tray Painting ($20/hour) will give you an easy starting point. You’ll get to choose from a selection of hand-cast figurines and trinket trays, then personalise them with your own designs.
There’s also the Colour Stories Coaster Painting ($35 for 2 hours) workshop, which lets you paint a pair of coasters with pre-drawn designs inspired by the Peranakan tiles found all over Joo Chiat.
Image adapted from: @sidequest.sg via Instagram
For something more practical, try Tote Bag Painting ($35 for 2 hours) and decorate an art piece that can be carried around wherever you go. Plant parents will want to check out Plant Pot Painting ($32 for 2 hours) , where you’ll get to customise your own flower pot and bring it back to spruce up your home garden.
Find your creative spark with DIY loop charms & postcards
Image adapted from: Side Quest
Painting is not all that you’ll find at Side Quest; those looking to explore other crafts or personalise mini tokens for friends and family can do so at the postcard and charm-making stations.
You’ll be given up to 2 postcards per session for you to write a heartfelt message to your loved ones and decorate them at the Snail Mail Postcard Bar ($25/hour) ; Side Quest will even help you mail it out for free .
At the Ling Long Loop Charm Bar ($18 for 30 minutes) , participants will get unlimited access to the cafe’s collection of beads and charms to create their own accessory. Make one for yourself or put together a little keepsake for someone special.
Celebrate birthdays with arts & crafts
View this post on Instagram
Skip the usual birthday dinner and celebrate your special day with a hands-on craft party hosted entirely by Side Quest. Starting at $60/pax , the Basic Birthday Party Package includes a 2-hour private celebration and your choice of any of the painting activities offered at the studio.
For more crafty fun, upgrade to the Bespoke Birthday Party Package at $90/pax . You’ll get an extra 30 minutes of party time , access to the Ling Long Loop Charm Bar , and curated goodie bags for each guest to take home.
Image credit: Side Quest
Parents can also leave the cleanup to Side Quest, so you can spend more time celebrating the special occasion with the little ones. The party can be hosted at the studio in Joo Chiat, or have the team bring the celebrations to your preferred venue at no extra charge.
Are food & drinks allowed at Side Quest?
While Side Quest does not serve any food or drinks as of yet, feel free to bring along non-alcoholic beverages from the cafes in Joo Chiat to sip on while working on your artworks.
How to get to Side Quest
View this post on Instagram
The art studio is a 7-minute walk from Marine Parade MRT Station . You’ll find Side Quest on the 2nd level of the 7-Eleven directly opposite i12 Katong .
Visit Side Quest for fun workshops at wallet-friendly prices

deals.body:
Tablescape Restaurant & Bar at Grand Park City Hall has unveiled its Christmas 2026 collection, a mix of a four-course dinner in its neoclassical dining room, two reimagined log cakes and Festive Celebration Sets for gatherings at home. The festive dinner runs from 2 December to 1 January, from 6.30pm to 9pm.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
The Festive Four-Course Dinner
The dinner costs S$98++ per guest. Each diner picks two starters, one main course and one dessert from a contemporary European menu.
The starters are Burrata with heirloom tomatoes and shaved melon, a Foie Gras Duo of pan-seared foie gras and mousse with beetroot, cocoa and salted chocolate, and Boston Lobster with charred onion, garden leaves and Avruga caviar.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Mains include Sea Perch, cooked sous-vide and wrapped in savoy cabbage with charred leeks, mussels and a bonito-onion emulsion, and a Roasted Turkey Roulade with potato mousseline, smoked bacon and asparagus. There is also a Josper-grilled Wagyu Beef Tenderloin with shallot confit, pumpkin fondant and tenderstem broccoli, and a vegetarian Truffle Courgette Risotto.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Dessert is the Coffee & Coconut Cloud, a coffee-coconut mousse with crisp meringue and candy floss, finished tableside with a spray of gold dust.
Two log cakes and a cheese board
The takeaway range includes two log cakes, each 1kg and serving 8 to 10 people:
• Santa’s Secret Rum & Kunafa Log, S$98, takes its cue from Dubai chocolate with crisp chocolate kunafa layered against moist chocolate sponge and a rum note
• Frosty’s Osmanthus & Yam Log, S$88, pairs osmanthus pear confiture with vanilla sponge, white chocolate mousse and Japanese yam filling
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Completing The Sweet Bar is the Charcuterie Cheese Yuletide Board at S$68, with cured hams, mortadella and salami, bleu, Asiago and Brie cheeses, marmalade and candy canes.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Festive Celebration Sets for home
Two sets are available. The S$228 set serves 6 to 8 people and includes two starters, one main, two sides and one log cake. The S$280 set serves 8 to 10 people and has three starters, one main, three sides and one log cake.
Starters include the Charcuterie Cheese Yuletide Platter, Snowy Burrata & Prosciutto di Parma, Rudolph’s Savoury Beef Meatballs made with Wagyu beef, and Golden Crown King Prawns with mango-spiced salsa and chickpeas. Mains are Roasted Festive Turkey, Holly Jolly Salmon Wellington, Honey-Glazed Gammon Ham and Prime Angus Beef Roast in striploin or ribeye, at about 2.5kg.
Image: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar
Sides include Mac & Cheese, oven-roasted ratte potatoes, glazed chestnuts with pecans, grilled vegetables with almonds, edamame with bacon and buttery Brussels sprouts. Each set comes with a choice of either log cake. Takeaway orders can be placed on the restaurant’s online store.
Key details
• Festive dinner: 2 December 2026 to 1 January 2027, 6.30pm to 9pm, S$98++ per guest
• Venue: Tablescape Restaurant & Bar, Level 3, Grand Park City Hall, 10 Coleman Street, Singapore 179809
More Christmas food to plan for
Comparing options? See our guide to Christmas log cakes 2026 at voco Orchard, Fullerton and Holiday Inn Atrium , and the list of hotel Christmas turkey takeaways with early-bird discounts . Tablescape also featured in our Tablescape mooncakes 2026 guide .

Singapore Coffee Week 2026 is back at Marina Bay Sands
Image credit: Singapore Coffee Week
As a country filled with workaholics, our coffee culture is booming, and something’s brewing that’ll get us all excited— Singapore Coffee Week 2026 is back from 5 November to 8 November 2026 . Better yet, entry to the highly anticipated event is free of charge.
Get excited for exhibits by various coffee brands, both local and international, games, activities, and even live competitions. Read on for a sneak peek of what’s at the event.
Expect around 50 exhibitors, including popular brands such as Suzuki Coffee , one of Singapore’s oldest artisanal roasters, and Baristart Coffee , known for its signature creamy lattes. Cowpresso Coffee Roasters is well known among home baristas for its high-end home espresso gear, on top of specialty coffee beans.
Image credit: Singapore Coffee Week
Beyond the mainstream brands, here are some unique roasters worth seeking out. Shinkirou Coffee from Tokyo will be featured at the Japan coffee pavilion. You’ll find their Ethiopia Sidama Dembi #2 , known for its vibrant fruity flavour, and Colombia Granja Paraíso 92—Ombligon , with more intense fruity and acidic notes. Prices are TBD.
Image credit: Yorz Coffee
Another highlight is Yorz Coffee, a Singapore-based organic grower with cultivation grounds in Yunnan, China. Its specialties include Ou Yang Natural , Wine Natural , and YORZ Espresso Blend. Meanwhile, KenntaRoast is a Singaporean boutique micro-roastery that makes experimental specialty coffees in small batches.
You can also look forward to events happening throughout the three days, including social media giveaways, interactive board games, passport trail adventures, and a bean discovery bar.
That’s not all: Fans can learn more about coffee roasting at the Singapore Coffee Roasting Team Championship 2026, where teams will compete for the chance to represent Singapore at the upcoming ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027.
While I have the coffee addicts’ attention, check out these best coffee cafes in Singapore . And here are some Marina Bay Sands restaurants with meals under $50 that you can visit after you attend the coffee festival.
Address: 10 Bayfront Ave, Singapore 018956, Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Hall C, Level 1
Event hours: 10am to 8pm
Website

deals.body:
We’ve got the intel on new bars in Singapore! The bar scene is buzzing with fresh energy, from swanky cocktail bars in Singapore to bold menus that’ll make your taste buds do a happy dance. Some even double as live music bars in Singapore , where you can sip, dine, and groove the night away. We’ve also been busy checking out the new restaurants in Singapore making waves across the city. Ready to drink your way through the crème de la crème with us?
Why trust this guide
When it comes to bars, I’m one of the city’s biggest fans. I’m always on the hunt for the next cool spot that opens up, and I follow it religiously till I can visit for myself to tell you all about it. I’m also very grateful to the bartenders I’ve met along the way who give me the honour of visiting their spaces before they’re open to the public.
Hot new bars in Singapore: November 2026
New bar: Earworm
Photography: Earworm via Instagram
We already know and love Offtrack for its fabulous music choices and even better taste in drinks. So it’s no surprise the group’s second concept is just as musically driven! Aptly named Earworm, this fluid space is a fun mix of bar, restaurant, and live music spot all rolled into one. The music programme champions local artists, and you’ll catch them performing live every Wednesday night. On the weekends, though? You’ll get bass-thumping soundtracks from DJs.
Drinks-wise, the menu is decently extensive with zero-proof picks, beers, wine (red, white, and even orange!), and cocktails. My heart is immediately drawn to the Pimm’s Cup mixed with Another Hendrick’s Gin, and I can never say no to an espresso martini riff, especially if it comes with salted cacao cream like the Caffe Mole!
Must-try drinks: Pimm’s Cup; Caffe Mole; New York Sour; Shakerato
Expect to spend: Cocktails start from $25
Opening hours: Tuesday to Thursday, 6pm to 1am; Friday to Saturday, 6pm to 2am
Address : Earworm , 16 North Canal Road, Singapore 048828
New bar: Sohaus
Photography: Sohaus
From the minds that brought you Nutmeg & Clove, let’s welcome Sohaus, the newest rooftop bar in Singapore . Situated on the roof of the newly opened Moutai House , this new bar in Singapore is a social space made for gathering, unwinding, and soaking in the city vibe. It also boasts one of the most breathtaking views of Singapore’s skyline. According to the team, the bar also gets a fabulous view of the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix ! As if we needed any more incentive to visit this spot.
Naturally, you can expect plenty of Moutai in Sohaus’s cocktails, inspired by cultural moments that have shaped Asia – from what we eat and drink to what we collect, wear, and do. If you’re looking for a seat, you’ll be directed to the alfresco area. But for those who prefer air conditioning, we recommend staying indoors. However, the inside bar area is standing only, and can be a bit of a tight squeeze. We say come in small groups to make the most of the experience.
Must-try drinks: Blind Box Fizz; Coffee Run Martini; Sohaus Highball
Expect to spend: Cocktails start from $28
Opening hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 5pm to 12am
Address : Sohaus , Level 4, Moutai House, 3 Fullerton Road, Singapore 049215
New bar: The Choya Ginza Bar
Photography: The Choya Ginza Bar via Instagram
A century of Choya’s craft and heritage has been distilled into a new establishment: the Choya Ginza Bar. The first-ever bar dedicated to all things Choya, you’ll get to see more than 12 Choya editions and specially curated tasting flights. And this is on top of the Choya serves, classic cocktails, and original concoctions. This is also one of the most affordable cocktail menus I’ve seen in a long time. You won’t find drinks over $22 at this bar, and you can even have a tasting flight of five Choyas for just $20!
Must-try drinks: Anything from the seasonal drinks menu; Choya tasting flights
Expect to spend: Drinks start from $16
Opening hours: Monday to Thursday, 4pm to 11pm; Friday to Saturday, 4pm to 11pm
Address : The Choya Ginza Bar , #02-06, Millenia Walk, 9 Raffles Boulevard, Singapore 039596
Hot new bars in Singapore: October 2026
New bar: Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar
Photography: Sufyan Saad
If you haven’t already caught up with our Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar review , this is your sign to read up, stat. Decked out in red, this new fried chicken spot dishes out nostalgic plates inspired by childhood. Pick between the original or duck fat mala fried chicken to line your stomach. Drinks-wise, we’d recommend the kaya daiquiri ($20) that comes with a little buttermilk waffle garnish. And if you’re going zero-proof, order the virgin smoky yuzu mocktail ($15).
Must-try drinks: Kaya daiquiri; virgin smoky yuzu mocktail
Expect to spend: Drinks start from $20; fried chicken starts from $12
Opening hours: Daily, 5.30pm to 1am (opens till 2am on Fridays & Saturdays)
Address : Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar , #02-15, 1 Liang Seah Street, Singapore 189022
New bar: A Bar Called Bar

deals.body:
Mollie Makes is a new Chinese dessert cafe in Johor Bahru
One of my favourite things to do in JB is to go dessert cafe hopping . I love travelling from matcha cafes to artisanal bakeries in search of sweet treats to satisfy my sweet tooth. Recently, I discovered Mollie Makes , a new cafe near customs serving Chinese desserts with a contemporary twist. If you’re looking for another spot to add to your JB itinerary, this one’s worth checking out.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 27 October 2026.
15 Best Dessert Spots In JB For Matcha Cakes, Black Sesame Shaved Ice And More
The cafe boasts a rustic Chinese look with traditional motifs and wooden furniture that’ll send you back to Season One of The Rise of Phoenixes . There are plenty of photo spots, so be sure to get your camera ready.
As aesthetic as the spot may be, they didn’t skimp on the quality of the desserts either. You can expect a wide variety of Chinese desserts, ranging from traditional classics to modern variants.
As a pistachio fanatic , their Pistachio Beancurd Mochi (RM15.90) was basically calling my name. Imagine a bowl filled generously with pistachio-flavoured tau huay, topped with stretchy mochi and cheese foam, then garnished with chopped pistachios.
This bowl met my rather high standards for pistachio desserts: it had prominent earthy, umami pistachio flavours, without being too sweet. The mochi also added a nice textural contrast—soft and stretchy with an indulgent milky taste. The cheese foam tied the whole dessert together, adding a subtle saltiness that offset the sweetness.
My dining companion preferred the Oh Yeah! Mollie (RM14.90) , comprising a base of coconut jelly piled high with toppings, including coconut milk he fen AKA Chinese wide noodles, rose-infused chestnuts, and fresh mango cubes. It’s then finished with a heaping scoop of coconut ice cream and a sprinkle of toasted coconut.
This dessert can be described in one word: refreshing. The coconut jelly is QQ and jiggly, and reminded me of the Chinese dessert bing fen.
The coconut ice cream, on the other hand, was soft and creamy. The fragrant coconut flavour was further accentuated by the coconut he fen, which tasted very similar to actual coconut meat.
The fresh mangoes were also slightly sour, cutting through the richness of the dessert, while the rose-infused chestnuts provided a nice crunch.
To wash everything down, we ordered the Taro Milk Tea With Mochi (RM15.80) , comprising Assam milk tea zhnged up with taro paste and handmade mochi, finished with a layer of cheese foam.
If you’re an orh nee lover , this drink is basically tailor-made for you. The Assam milk tea base was quite light and fragrant, allowing the stronger-tasting yam paste to come through. The mochi also added a nice bite: it was soft and slightly chewy, making it feel more like a dessert than a drink.
Interestingly, the dessert cafe offers a lineup of fresh shio pan. We ordered their Mentaiko Shio Pan (RM8.90) , and surprisingly, it could rival my favourite salt breads. It had a crunchy, buttery base, with a soft and chewy middle, and was garnished with mentaiko mayo, seaweed, and a slab of creamy Kewpie mayonnaise.
That’s not all: the bread is split lengthwise and slathered with more creamy mentaiko mayo for added umami.
Mollie Makes is located a seven-minute drive away from CIQ Jalan Jim Quee .
For more places to tick off your JB cafe checklist, read our guide to the best cafes in Johor Bahru . Alternatively, if you have no idea on where to start, our JB food itinerary might lead you in the right direction.
Address: 30 Jalan Dhoby, Bandar Johor Bahru, 80000 Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 8pm
Website
Mollie Makes is not halal-certified.

Photos taken by Nivian Chiang.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.

deals.body:
Nook Coffee is a new coffee kiosk in Bedok
Image credit: Nook.57 Coffee
An adorable hole-in-the-wall coffee spot has just opened in the East: Nook Coffee , Bedok’s latest addition, serving specialty coffee and matcha. It boasts an artsy concept, with hand-painted store signage and hand-drawn designs on its coffee cups.
Image credit: @NookcoffeeSG
FYI: This Halloween, the team has drawn up spooky graphics on their cups to give your daily coffee a twist. Keep an eye out if you want to score one of these special cups!
Image credit: @NookcoffeeSG
They offer the standard cafe-style options, such as Black (from $3.40++) , White (from $3.90++) , and Cappuccino ($3.90++) .
For something a little fancier, get the flavoured lattes, including Mocha , Spanish Latte , Vanilla Latte , and Caramel Latte , well-priced from $4.40++ each —a steal in this economy.
Image credit: Nayae from Google Maps
We’re eyeing the three signature drinks: a Tiramisu Latte ($5.80++) that’s made with homemade cream, a Mint Cocoa Latte ($5.60++) , and a Coconut with Coffee Foam ($5.80++) .
Lastly, matcha fans can choose from four matcha options, including a regular Matcha Latte ($4.50++) and a Strawberry Matcha Latte ($5.20++) . If you’re feeling more adventurous, consider the Coconut with Matcha Foam ($5.80++) and the Cocoa Latte with Matcha Foam ($6.20++) .

deals.body:
Zermatt Neo opens OVER restaurant in Tanjong Pagar
Best known for taking on massive amounts of food in one go, competitive eater and content creator Zermatt Neo has started his very first F&B venture: OVER , which just opened along Tras Street .
The new concept brings larger-than-life portions and crazy food challenges, in partnership with The Wolfpack Investment Holdings. They’ve already gotten an overwhelming response for their soft-launch reservations, so we had to visit and see what the commotion is about.
Fans can expect three portion sizes on the menu: Lesser for solo diners, Standard for sharing, and Challenge , featuring the largest servings, typical of Zermatt Neo.
We kick-started our feast with the Rolling Over Wakame in the Lesser portion for $10++ . This featured spring rolls doused in a house-made glaze and topped with wakame salad.
The dish tasted just as interesting as it looked. The spring rolls were crispy and paired well with the briny wakame and subtly sweet glaze, making for a great start to our mukbang-like meal.
Up next we had the Shroyu-Clams! (from $35++) . As a huge lala fan, this starter lived up to all my expectations. Though it came in the smallest size, the clams were anything but. Each one boasted a huge portion of meat, making it worth every penny.
The white clams were simmered and served in a buttery and garlicky shoyu sauce that was finger-licking good. It also came with slices of toasted sourdough to soak up every last drop of the rich sauce.
Moving on to the mains: what really stole the show for us was the Curry Me Over (from $23++) . My colleague and I marvelled at the sheer size of this dish, which Zermatt himself said was originally twice as big.
Atop the bed of rice lies a massive, tender, juicy cut of chicken drowned in nanban sauce that added a pleasant creaminess.
Portions aside, we were impressed with how fragrant the Hainanese-style curry was. Each grain of rice was slathered in the decadent curry zhup, leaving me wanting more after every bite. Despite looking extremely heavy, it was a well-balanced dish that ended up being our favourite of the evening.
On the topic of chicken, we also had the Wing Me Over (from $10++) . Each wing was tender and fried to maximum crunch. While the rub on the skin tasted a tad too salty for me, the teriyaki-like sauce on the side helped cut through the richness.
On top of OVER’s regular menu, the restaurant will also be introducing a rotation of collaborations with various local chefs and businesses. Marking their debut collab with viral local barbecue brand Jett Barbecue, the Over Jett (from $28++) features a burger stacked with Jett BBQ’s signature beef cheeks, crispy onion rings, fried eggs, and a creamy mayo dressing.
Much like how Jett BBQ only makes special appearances now and then, the Over Jett will only be available until 30 November 2026, so grab it while you still can.
Their drinks alone deserve a special shout-out—all of them come in oversized portions. We ordered the Japanese Highball ($13.80++) and Shochu Sour (from $12.80++) , both of which came in extra-tall glasses and were refreshing thirst quenchers.
End your meal on a sweet note with their “secret menu” Mom’s Pie (price TBD) . The pie flavour rotates every month, with this month’s being Apple Pie . The gooey filling within the buttery crust had a woody cinnamon flavour, and the frosting on top was light and airy, marking the perfect end to our meal.
If you’re game, go for the Ultimate Food Challenge (from $239++) , where you take on an entire 8kg platter in one hour. Diners can give it a shot alone or in groups of up to four. Succeed and win a free meal, a spot on the Hall of Fame, a cash prize, as well as bragging rights.
OVER has a bar-like vibe, with high chairs and tables, dim lighting, neon signs, and a curated soundtrack—perfect for a casual night out with pals over some good food and drinks.
The restaurant is located conveniently in the CBD, just a short five-minute walk from Tanjong Pagar MRT Station or Maxwell MRT Station .
In other news, Singapore Coffee Week is back with free entry from 5 to 8 November. If you’re craving a sweet treat in the area, our Messina x Queic feature gives you the latest scoop on their limited-time collab.
Address: 54 Tras Street, Singapore 078993
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 11am to 12am
Website
OVER is not halal-certified.
Singapore Coffee Week 2026 Returns From 5 To 8 Nov, Entry Is Free
Photos taken by Zi Xuan Chan .
This was a media tasting at OVER.

Remember the massive waterfront mall we told you about in Penang ? The Waterfront Shoppes is finally opening on 29 Oct 2026 , bringing over 300 retail and dining outlets plus a seafront promenade with views of the Penang Bridge .
Credit – The Light City
Located within The Light City , the sprawling lifestyle destination covers over 1.5 million sq ft across two phases, combining shopping, dining, and entertainment in one coastal precinct. Its waterfront setting also gives shoppers a scenic spot to take a breather between browsing stores and grabbing a bite.
Credit – The Light City
The line-up is set to span everything from familiar local eats and international brands to casual cafes and waterfront dining spots. As more tenants join the mix, there’ll be even more reasons to drop by beyond the usual shopping run, especially if you fancy a meal with a view of the sea.
Credit – Zus, Bakestone, Skechers & XVenture
The confirmed tenant line-up includes Mercato , Parkson , Decathlon , Skechers , Watsons , ZUS Coffee , CU Mart , Loud Speaker , ParaThai , Tai Ho Jiak , Mr. Wu Taiwanese Cuisine , 65c Ondo , Bakestone , and Ningji Lemon Tea . You’ll also find lifestyle and entertainment options such as XVenture , CMC Theatre by Mega Cineplex , and Dreame , alongside fashion, beauty, and tech retailers.
Note that the information provided is accurate at the time of writing and may be subject to change.
Credit – The Light City
The Waterfront Shoppes is part of the wider The Light City integrated development, which will also feature luxury residences, office towers, international hotels , and the upcoming Penang Waterfront Convention Centre (PWCC) . The larger project aims to bring shopping, business, hospitality, and entertainment together in one destination.
The Waterfront Shoppes begins its soft opening on 29 Oct 2026 , so keep it on your radar if you’re planning to visit Penang soon!

deals.body:
Best omakase restaurants in Singapore
Omakase, synonymous with fancy Japanese fare, actually means: I leave it up to you. The “you” here refers to the chef, who would present a series of dishes centred around the season’s best produce. Fancy it may be, it doesn’t always mean that you have to spend a bomb and then some—with that, here’s a list of the best omakase restaurants in Singapore for all budgets, with prices from less than $40++ a person.
1. Tentsuru
Image credit: @tentsurusg
At most omakase experiences, tempura might be but one of many courses. At Tentsuru , however, tempura takes centre stage on their chef’s choice menus—a decision founded on Master Chef Daiki Kawaguchi ’s love for the deep-fried Japanese dish.
There are four omakase menus at Tentsuru, each with progressively more courses. These are Tsuzumi ($188++), Uguisu ($280++) , and Tsuru ($380++) . Whatever your choice, be certain that a fine-dining tempura and omakase experience awaits, built upon fresh ingredients air-flown from the Toyosu Fish Market and various parts of Japan. Typically, the experience involves an appetiser, a seafood and vegetable tempura medley, a tendon or a tencha, and a dessert. All courses are enjoyed on a Japanese bar counter, with front-row seats to Chef Kawaguchi in action.
Image credit: @tentsurusg
If you’re in the mood for a splurge, order the Tsuru. The meal starts with a seasonal appetiser and dish of the day, before segueing into eight different tempura offerings. Of the lot are two Tentsuru signatures: the Sea Urchin Tempura , where uni roe is served raw on a deep-fried shiso leaf, with a dollop of caviar. Also of note is the Miyazaki A5 Wagyu Beef tempura, topped with earthy black truffle shavings and a house-made komi sauce. During the winter season, diners can also expect Hokkaido wild king crab to make an appearance on their plates.
A selection of premium sake—including an exclusive Tentsuru Kura No Hana Junmai Daiginjo (from $55++) —along with a curated range of fine wines, is also available for pairing.
Address: 29 Tanglin Road, Level 2, The St. Regis Singapore, Singapore 247911
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 12pm to 2:30pm, 6pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 8113 3612
Website
Tentsuru is not halal-certified.
2. Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Cuppage Plaza is known for being a haven for authentic Japanese restaurants. Among them is Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu , often regarded as one of the best omakase spots in the area . Tucked away on the plaza’s sixth floor, it is an intimate reservations-only eight-seater omakase restaurant run by Chef Masa. Diners get a front-row seat as the chef prepares his dishes of the day, spanning appetisers to sushi and sashimi, as well as cooked dishes.
The pace of the meal is leisurely, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa has only one seating each night. Expect to spend two to three hours feasting on Chef Masa’s creations, all made with seasonal ingredients air-flown daily from Tokyo’s Toyosu Market.
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Currently on the menu are highlights like the Grilled Ankimo with Deep-Fried Sweet Onion , where monkfish liver is grilled in a manner similar to foie gras, and topped with a sweet onion garnish for added texture. There’s the Monaka , Sushi Masa’s spin on the negitoro sushi, comprising chopped fatty tuna and uni served on a crisp Japanese wafer, with a zingy housemade shiso pesto and sansho pepper sauce.
For sushi, the Flame-Grilled Otoro Nigiri with Leek is a memorable reinterpretation of an aburi course. Fatty tuna grilled directly over an open flame to develop a lightly charred crust that enhances the fish’s butteriness, finished with leek for freshness.
Prices start at $230+ for their 16-course Syuugetsu Dinner menu—a more reasonable price than omakase experiences of a similar calibre, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa isn’t housed in a hotel or an expensive shophouse.
Reservations open 60 days in advance, and can be made via their website .
Address: 5 Koek Road, #06-03, Singapore 228796
Opening hours: Tue-Sat 7:15pm to 10pm, Sun for private bookings only
Tel: 9752 5851
Website
Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu is not halal-certified.
3. AN Omakase
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Located near Maxwell MRT Station is AN Omakase , a casual Japanese dining restaurant serving up both lunch and dinner omakase.
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Prices start at $13 8++ for the Himitsu menu, which comes with five courses—an appetiser, a steamed dish , nigiri sushi , soup , and dessert . Vegan-friendly options are available too.

members.body:
Best omakase restaurants in Singapore
Omakase, synonymous with fancy Japanese fare, actually means: I leave it up to you. The “you” here refers to the chef, who would present a series of dishes centred around the season’s best produce. Fancy it may be, it doesn’t always mean that you have to spend a bomb and then some—with that, here’s a list of the best omakase restaurants in Singapore for all budgets, with prices from less than $40++ a person.
1. Tentsuru
Image credit: @tentsurusg
At most omakase experiences, tempura might be but one of many courses. At Tentsuru , however, tempura takes centre stage on their chef’s choice menus—a decision founded on Master Chef Daiki Kawaguchi ’s love for the deep-fried Japanese dish.
There are four omakase menus at Tentsuru, each with progressively more courses. These are Tsuzumi ($188++), Uguisu ($280++) , and Tsuru ($380++) . Whatever your choice, be certain that a fine-dining tempura and omakase experience awaits, built upon fresh ingredients air-flown from the Toyosu Fish Market and various parts of Japan. Typically, the experience involves an appetiser, a seafood and vegetable tempura medley, a tendon or a tencha, and a dessert. All courses are enjoyed on a Japanese bar counter, with front-row seats to Chef Kawaguchi in action.
Image credit: @tentsurusg
If you’re in the mood for a splurge, order the Tsuru. The meal starts with a seasonal appetiser and dish of the day, before segueing into eight different tempura offerings. Of the lot are two Tentsuru signatures: the Sea Urchin Tempura , where uni roe is served raw on a deep-fried shiso leaf, with a dollop of caviar. Also of note is the Miyazaki A5 Wagyu Beef tempura, topped with earthy black truffle shavings and a house-made komi sauce. During the winter season, diners can also expect Hokkaido wild king crab to make an appearance on their plates.
A selection of premium sake—including an exclusive Tentsuru Kura No Hana Junmai Daiginjo (from $55++) —along with a curated range of fine wines, is also available for pairing.
Address: 29 Tanglin Road, Level 2, The St. Regis Singapore, Singapore 247911
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 12pm to 2:30pm, 6pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 8113 3612
Website
Tentsuru is not halal-certified.
2. Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Cuppage Plaza is known for being a haven for authentic Japanese restaurants. Among them is Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu , often regarded as one of the best omakase spots in the area . Tucked away on the plaza’s sixth floor, it is an intimate reservations-only eight-seater omakase restaurant run by Chef Masa. Diners get a front-row seat as the chef prepares his dishes of the day, spanning appetisers to sushi and sashimi, as well as cooked dishes.
The pace of the meal is leisurely, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa has only one seating each night. Expect to spend two to three hours feasting on Chef Masa’s creations, all made with seasonal ingredients air-flown daily from Tokyo’s Toyosu Market.
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Currently on the menu are highlights like the Grilled Ankimo with Deep-Fried Sweet Onion , where monkfish liver is grilled in a manner similar to foie gras, and topped with a sweet onion garnish for added texture. There’s the Monaka , Sushi Masa’s spin on the negitoro sushi, comprising chopped fatty tuna and uni served on a crisp Japanese wafer, with a zingy housemade shiso pesto and sansho pepper sauce.
For sushi, the Flame-Grilled Otoro Nigiri with Leek is a memorable reinterpretation of an aburi course. Fatty tuna grilled directly over an open flame to develop a lightly charred crust that enhances the fish’s butteriness, finished with leek for freshness.
Prices start at $230+ for their 16-course Syuugetsu Dinner menu—a more reasonable price than omakase experiences of a similar calibre, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa isn’t housed in a hotel or an expensive shophouse.
Reservations open 60 days in advance, and can be made via their website .
Address: 5 Koek Road, #06-03, Singapore 228796
Opening hours: Tue-Sat 7:15pm to 10pm, Sun for private bookings only
Tel: 9752 5851
Website
Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu is not halal-certified.
3. AN Omakase
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Located near Maxwell MRT Station is AN Omakase , a casual Japanese dining restaurant serving up both lunch and dinner omakase.
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Prices start at $13 8++ for the Himitsu menu, which comes with five courses—an appetiser, a steamed dish , nigiri sushi , soup , and dessert . Vegan-friendly options are available too.

Bukit Panjang finally has its own Sushiro. The Japanese conveyor-belt chain’s newest outlet sits on the second floor of Bukit Panjang Plaza, and it comes with two weeks of 1-for-1 sushi and S$6++ drinks to pull in the neighbourhood. If you live in the north-west and have been taking the bus to Lot One in Choa Chu Kang or Causeway Point in Woodlands for your salmon plates, this one is for you.
The grand opening deals run from 30 October to 12 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
What the grand opening deals cover
The opening promotion runs from 30 October to 12 November. Sushi goes 1-for-1, and the second portion arrives on the same plate rather than as a separate plate on the belt, so one plate carries double the sushi. Ask the staff which plates are in the deal on the day you go.
Three drinks drop to S$6++ each for the same two weeks:
• Lemon sour, usually S$8++
• Suntory The Premium Malt’s draught beer, usually S$10.50++
• Kaku highball, usually S$9++
The sure-win gachapon for diners spending S$50 or more was an opening-day special on 30 October only, so that one has come and gone.
The second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu runs until 3 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
The limited menu running alongside
Bukit Panjang opens in the middle of the second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu, which runs at every outlet until 3 November while stocks last. The headline plates are the Miyako salmon trout taste and compare from Japan’s Sanriku Rias coast at S$2.90++ and a fatty swordfish at S$2.90++.
The rest of the line-up leans on soy sauce koji, a fermented seasoning of soy sauce and koji, across four fish:
• Soy sauce koji fresh salmon, S$2.90++
• Soy sauce koji engawa, S$2.30++
• Soy sauce koji yellowtail, S$3.90++
• Soy sauce koji red snapper, S$4.90++
Pufferfish fans get two fugu plates at S$4.90++ each, and the bancha braised octopus uses Hokkaido mizudako at S$3.90++. Prices differ at the Digiro outlet in Mandai Wildlife Reserve.
Tuna, ikura, unagi and salmon from Sushiro’s regular menu. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Where Sushiro goes next
Bukit Panjang is the first of three new Sushiro outlets on the calendar. Great World follows at the end of November at #01-112/113/114, and Funan comes next in early December at #02-16. Taste Orchard, on the other hand, has closed for good, which leaves Wisma Atria, Isetan Scotts and Orchard Gateway as the Orchard Road options. Parkway Parade is temporarily closed.
App reservations for Bukit Panjang opened on 24 October, and booking ahead through the Sushiro app is the sensible move for a new outlet in its first weekends.
Sushiro Great World is due to open at the end of November. Image: Sushiro Singapore (artist’s impression)
Sushiro Bukit Panjang Plaza details
Address: 1 Jelebu Road, #02-17/17A/18/18A/19/19A, Bukit Panjang Plaza, Singapore 677743
Hours: 11am to 10pm daily, last order 9.30pm
Grand opening promotion: 30 October to 12 November 2026
Reservations: Sushiro Singapore app
Other outlets: Sushiro Singapore locations

deals.body:
Cheap food places in Orchard for $10 and less
Orchard may be dubbed as the area for the affluent, a place you should avoid at all costs if you are looking to dine on a budget. But we are here to prove you wrong—here is our list of the 15 cheap Orchard food places that will only cost you $10 or less! Whether you’re craving a piping hot bowl of Yong Tau Foo or the comfort of a home-cooked Korean meal, we’ve got you covered.
1. Korat Thai Cafe
The key to finding Orchard Road’s cheap fixes lies in the less fancy, less decorated places. One such spot is Korat Thai Cafe, a nondescript spot serving up affordable Thai cuisine. Plus, their menu is super extensive, with over 50 dishes to choose from!
Options here include Tom Yum Fried Rice ($8.50), Garlic Pepper ($7.50), Sweet and Sour ($7.50), Basil Leaf Pork ($7.50) . Otherwise, dig into a comforting bowl of Tom Yum Noodle Soup ($8.50 ) , which boasts spicy and sour flavours, or a bowl of flavourful Phad Thai ($8.50).
Check out our Korat Thai Cafe review.
Address: 400 Orchard Road, #03-28, Orchard Tower, Singapore 238875
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 10pm
Website
Korat Thai Cafe is not halal-certified.
Korat Thai Cafe Review: XXL Thai Pork Backbone, Tom Yum Mama And More At Orchard Towers
2. New Station Snack Bar
New Station Snack Bar is located in Far East Plaza. If you’re familiar with their sister joint, New Station Rice Bar in Bugis, you would know just how popular the OG joint is. They sell a range of zi char-style dishes, but the one that put them on the map is their salted egg rice.
This salted egg rice, which is a non-negotiable dish to order when you’re here, is easily one of the best around. We visited their sister outlet not too long ago, so we can attest to this claim. Their delicious Salted Egg Pork Rice ($8) features crispy, deep-fried pieces of pork drenched in a thick, savoury salted egg sauce. But if that doesn’t strike your fancy, go for dishes such as the Marmite Chicken Rice ($9), Sweet and Sour Fish Rice ($8), or Black Pepper Beef Rice ($8) , which are equally as popular!
Check out our New Station Rice Bar review.
Address: 14 Scotts Road, #05-95, Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 8:45pm
Tel: 8999 4064
Website
New Station Snack Bar is not halal-certified.
Far East Plaza’s Popular New Station Snack Bar Opens Outlet In Fortune Centre
3. Riverside Indonesian BBQ
Image credit: Ming Rong via Google Maps
Riverside Indonesian BBQ is known for its panggang AKA grilled meats. They have numerous outlets dotted across various Kopitiams on the island, including one in Plaza Singapura and 313 Somerset! Options here include the Ayam Panggang Set ($7.80), Sotong Panggang Set ($8.50), and Ikan Panggang Set ($7.80), among others.
Image credit: Jasmine Adams via Google Maps
Other than meat, each plate comes with rice doused in lemak curry, cabbage, a sunny-side-up, clear soup, and sambal. The grilled chicken is super raved about, known for not only being tender and juicy, but also well-marinated. Each piece is grilled to perfection over charcoal, so you know you’re getting that ultra-smoky flavour!
313 Somerset outlet
Address: 313 Orchard Road, #B3-44, Singapore 238895
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 10pm
Plaza Singapura outlet
Address: 68 Orchard Road, #06-15/17, Singapore 238839
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 10pm
Website
Riverside Indonesian BBQ is halal-certified.
4. Song Fa Bak Kut Teh
Song Fa Bak Kut Teh needs little to no introduction, with it being arguably Singapore’s most established BKT chain. Not to mention, the stall has also had a consistent spot on the Michelin Bib Gourmand for over seven years!
Though the prices of the BKT here are a leg-up compared to what you would find at more humble hawker stalls, most dishes on the menu here will still set you back less than $10. Must-order items here are the Pork Ribs Soup ($8.80++ ) and the Premium Loin Rib Soup ($9.80++).
The broth boasts a rich, distinctive flavour of pork bones, thanks to the long hours of simmering. It also isn’t overly peppery, which is great as it wouldn’t induce a coughing fit upon first sip. To better soak up more of that fragrant broth, order some Dough Fritters ($2.30++) AKA you tiao to dip on the side.
Check out our Song Fa Bak Kut Teh review .
Address: 176 Orchard Road, #02-29/30, The Centrepoint, Singapore 238843
Opening hours: Mon-Thurs 11am to 9am, Fri 11am to 9:30am, Sat 10:30am to 9:30pm, Sun 10: 30am to 9pm
Website
Song Fa Bak Kut Teh is not halal-certified.
Song Fa Bak Kut Teh Review: Singapore’s Famous Michelin-Approved Bak Kut Teh, Open Since 1969
5. Fiie’s Cafe
Image credit: Kai via Google Maps
Arguably one of the most well-known food joints in Lucky Plaza is Fiie’s Cafe , or you might better know the stall as the famous Mister Grumpy’s fried chicken. The nickname stems from the formidable expression the owner of the stall wears when serving customers. Though that hasn’t stopped the stall from racking up long queues of customers on the daily.

deals.body:
We all know the feeling of a brand new work week. You just had a great weekend, but now it’s time to get back to the Monday-to-Friday grind.
But there’s encouraging news for those of you working in the CBD area: another reason to look forward to going to the office on weekdays. 11Westside , a California-Mexican restaurant, recently launched 3 weekly promotions on Mondays , Tuesdays , and Wednesdays .
Credit: 11Westside
11Westside is located in Asia Square Tower 1 , so those of you who pass by frequently might find it familiar. The restaurant prides itself on delivering bold West Coast flavours and artisanal cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for after-work dinners or drinks .
Credit: 11Westside
Kicking things off on Mondays is Margarita Mondays , featuring free-flow handcrafted margaritas and bar snacks you can pair with your Mexican-inspired orders . This deal is available from 5.30pm–8pm , while stocks last. I guess it’s a nice way to beat the Monday blues for those of you who work nearby.
Taco Tuesdays then take over on the second day of the week, offering 50% off all tacos from 6pm onwards . Menu highlights include Baja Fish (S$8) , Mango Shrimp (S$8) , and Wagyu Beef Cheek Birria (S$18 for 2pcs) . Planning a Tuesday post-work hangout with colleagues and friends doesn’t seem like such a bad idea!
Credit: 11Westside
Ladies, there’s also something for you to look forward to when dreaded mid-week comes. Ladies’ Night Wednesdays at 11Westside invites you to a free-flow suckling pig taco live station , and house pours for just S$9.90 .
