members.title: Donate Blood, Get a Mixue, Messina or Yo-Chi Dessert Voucher: Singapore Red Cross, 2 Nov-6 Dec 2026

members.body:
Yo-Chi, Messina & Mixue vouchers at blood banks in Singapore
2026 is flying by, and if your New Year’s resolutions are still sitting on your Notes app untouched, there’s still time to tick something off the list. For those who have no idea where to begin, why not start by donating blood? It’s a simple way to do some good and help save lives.
Plus, you can score vouchers from Yo-Chi , Messina , and Mixue when you donate blood at participating blood banks in Singapore as part of the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign. Here’s how.
Donate blood at 1 of the 5 blood banks in Singapore
Image credit: Michael Chia via Google Maps
From 2nd November to 6th December 2026 , you’ll earn a voucher for a sweet treat when you donate blood at any of the 5 participating blood banks in Singapore.
Here are the 5 locations:
• Bloodbank@HSA
• Bloodbank@Dhoby Ghaut
• Bloodbank@Westgate Tower
• Bloodbank@One Punggol
• Bloodbank@Woodlands
Book your appointment according to the sweet treat you want
Image credit: Eatbook
Remember to book an appointment online before heading down. But something to take note of is that the vouchers are available during different periods , so you’ll want to time your blood donation according to the treat you’re eyeing.
Image credit: Messina via Google Maps
Here’s when you can snag each voucher:
Date
Voucher
2nd-15th Nov 2026
$5 Mixue discount voucher
16th-26th Nov 2026
Voucher for a free extra scoop of ice cream at Messina
27th Nov-6th Dec 2026
$5 Yo-Chi discount voucher
Remember to flash the campaign page or campaign-related visuals to be eligible
View this post on Instagram
Don’t forget to show the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign page or the campaign’s Instagram post to the staff at the registration counter when you arrive for your appointment.
This is an important step if you want to walk away with your voucher, as staff won’t prompt you about the promotion. You’ll have to flash the campaign visuals before your blood donation procedure begins to qualify.
Celebrate doing a good deed with a silent disco
Image credit: Singapore Red Cross Society
There’s more to look forward to after rolling up your sleeves. Pints & Beats is a 1-day silent disco specially organised for blood donors, happening at Another Bar on 6th December 2026 , from 2pm to 6pm .
It’s essentially a daytime party for donors to celebrate doing a good deed, with fun activities lined up. To be eligible, you’ll need to have successfully donated blood between 1st July and 30th November 2026 .
There are 2 ways to register your interest:
• Those who donated before 2nd November will receive an email by 9th November inviting you to register your interest. Take note that this is only for sign-ups and isn’t your event access confirmation.
• Those who just donated can look out for the QR code on the tent cards at any refreshment area in the blood banks and scan it to register your interest.
Successful applicants will receive a separate confirmation email by 4th December 2026 , with access details for themselves and a plus-one.
Image for illustrative purposes only.
Image credit: @mixuesyd via Instagram
As for what’s in store, expect free Mixue drinks, photo spots, a custom T-shirt station, and hourly sure-win lucky draws. There’s also a grand draw featuring 3 prizes, including a staycation!
Book your blood donation appointment soon
Image credit: @xt_lee via Instagram
If it’s your first time donating blood and you’re feeling anxious, check out our guide to donating blood in Singapore for everything you need to know before heading down.
Also, we can’t stress this enough: book your appointment early and remember to flash the campaign visuals at the registration counter before donating, or you might just miss out on your sweet treat voucher!
Find out more about the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign
More ways to give back to the community:
• Donate essentials to migrant workers at the inspIRRe store
• Places to volunteer in SG, sorted by region
• Guide to donations to The Salvation Army
Cover image adapted from: @xt_lee via Instagram, Eatbook, Messina via Google Maps

deals.body:
We all know and love Orchard Road as an iconic shopping destination in Singapore. But when the hunger pangs call, finding the perfect dining spot can leave us stumped – especially if you’re searching for a quiet restaurant away from the crowds that delivers on its ambience, food and drinks. Enter Slainte at Paragon, Orchard, a newly revamped sanctuary that hits all the marks. Made for intimate date nights and convivial group hangouts alike, Slainte might be that day-to-night spot you need on your radar.
Slainte at Orchard: Details at a glance
Best for: An inviting day-to-night spot with charcoal-grilled dishes and rare whiskies
Must-try dishes: Snow aging yukimuro full blood wagyu; miso-glazed Patagonian toothfish; salt-roasted carabinero; Iberico pluma
Price: Starters from $9; mains from $19; desserts from $19; drinks from $5
Opening hours: Daily, 11am to 10pm
Address: #04-09, Paragon Shopping Centre, 290 Orchard Road, Singapore 238859
Cosy up in a chic and inviting setting
Photography: Slainte
Step inside Slainte, and you’ll be instantly enveloped in a warm and welcoming ambience. From the cave-like stone walls to wooden furnishing and warm glow, every inch of the restaurant is designed to make you linger.
With a perfect balance of intimacy and luxury, it is a space that makes for easy and effortless conversations. Coupled with its quieter location away from the main shopping strip, Slainte is where you can finally take a breather from the hustle and bustle.
A smoky menu takes centre stage
Bold, smoky flavours and charcoal grilling anchor the menu at Slainte. The restaurant’s state-of-the-art Kopa oven is where all the grilling magic happens. Fired by charcoal and applewood, this showstopper reaches a blistering 600 degrees Celsius.
The results? An irresistible menu kissed by smoke, serving up unbeatable juiciness and deeply charred flavours that can’t be replicated at home.
Photography: Slainte
The flame-grilled selection beckons with signatures like black Angus porterhouse ($78), char siew Iberico pork jowl ($17) with a sweet-savoury glaze, Jack’s Creek wagyu hanger steak ($58), miso-glazed Patagonian toothfish ($38), and an 18-hour-marinated ayam bakar ($24).
And don’t miss the Iberico pork ($42) cooked to medium-well – we hear it’s one of the best in town. Enjoy these succulent meats and seafood with moreish sides ($9 each) like French onion mac and cheese, smashed crispy potatoes and charred asparagus.
Beyond these charcoal-grilled creations, we’re also eyeing starters like the scallop and prawn tartlets ($25) for a savoury pastry with fresh seafood, and hearty plates such as the signature yuzu kosho pasta ($29). With an extensive selection of pasta, vibrant salads and hearty mains, you’ll be left happily spoilt for choice from day through night.
Sip auctioned-sourced whiskies by the dram
Photography: Slainte
Curious about the world of whisky? Take a seat at Slainte to get started. The restaurant offers a collection of auction-sourced rare whisky that you can sip by the dram from just $15. Take it as your licence to try lesser seen whisky labels, each with its unique taste, history and craftsmanship.
Wines, champagne and creative cocktails are also available. We recommend trying the specially concocted cocktails, including the signature Slainte. An ode to the restaurant’s Irish roots, it is a blend of smoky Islay Scotch, sweet vermouth, Aperol and cinnamon.
Hello Slainte, our new go-to spot in Orchard
In an area known for glitz and sky-high prices, Slainte is where you can treat yourself to a well-crafted dining experience without the hefty price tags. On your next shopping spree in Orchard, swing by the restaurant to indulge in charcoal-grilled delicacies and sip fine whiskies and cocktails.
Curious about its allure? Visit Slainte at Paragon, Orchard, and you’ll understand why it is a dining destination that makes you linger a while longer.
This post is in partnership with Slainte.

links.title: Tokyo’s Cult-Favourite Mr.CHEESECAKE Pops Up at ION Orchard Until December 30
Tokyo’s cult-favourite Mr. Cheesecake makes its Singapore debut at Ion Orchard

members.body:
Cheesecakes in Singapore can be found just about anywhere, but they’re not quite the same as the silky delights from Tokyo’s Mr. Cheesecake. With over a million cheesecakes sold in Japan, these masterfully crafted desserts come from chef Koji Tamura. Through the art of Japanese precision, the humble cheesecake has been given a massive upgrade. But what makes Mr. Cheesecake’s desserts so worth the wait? Here’s the 411.
Mr. Cheesecake’s pop-up in Singapore: Details at a glance
When: 11 November to 30 December 2026
Price: TBC
Opening hours: TBC
Where: Mr. Cheesecake’s pop-up , Ion Orchard, opposite Hermes, Level 3, 2 Orchard Turn, Singapore 238801
What makes Mr. Cheesecake special
Photography: Mr. Cheesecake
From classic cheesecakes and burnt Basque cheesecakes to other dessert options like roll cakes, tiramisu, and financiers, Mr. Cheesecake’s offerings are nothing out of the ordinary. So what is it about these cakes that made this brand go insanely viral in Tokyo?
Part of Mr. Cheesecake’s uniqueness is in the method of serving. Its signature cheesecake has three different taste profiles, depending on the temperature you serve it. You can enjoy it frozen, where it’s extra tart and tastes like ice cream cake. Wait a little while for it to warm up and you get a contrast of textures with a smooth outer layer and frozen centre. Or have it fully thawed for a mouthfeel akin to creme brulee – the best way to enjoy the sweetness and aroma.
Mr. Cheesecake’s key flavours also read like a perfume list in the best way possible. Made with vanilla, white chocolate, tonka bean, and lemon, it’s skillfully balanced to create a rich but light cake.
And as Mr. Cheesecake says: it may not be the best in the world, but it might just be the best you’ll ever have in your life.
What to expect at the Singapore pop-up
Photography: Mr. Cheesecake
Very few details have been released about the brand’s upcoming Singapore pop-up. Given that it is the brand’s first-ever pop-up in Southeast Asia, we’re expecting minimalist displays that shine the spotlight on the main star – the cheesecakes.
We’re told to expect a curated line-up of five creations, brought together for the first time just for the Singapore debut. Flavours you can look forward to include the matcha and caramel Earl Grey cheesecakes and the rich tiramisu.
We’ll be back with more updates as more information rolls out, so stay tuned!
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Mr. Cheesecake?
It's a brand founded in 2018 by chef Koji Tamura. Mr. Cheesecake is best known for its (you guessed it) cheesecakes with rich and creamy flavour.
Why is it so popular?
Thanks to its distinct texture and layered flavours, Mr. Cheesecake is exceptionally popular in Japan. You can enjoy the cake at three different temperatures, and each has its unique texture and flavour.
Where is the Mr. Cheesecake pop-up?
It'll be located within Ion Orchard.
Is this Mr. Cheesecake's first pop-up?
Yes, this is the brand's inaugural pop-up in Southeast Asia.
Will this be permanent?
As far as we've heard, Mr. Cheesecake has no plans on opening a permanent store in Singapore.
members.summary: Cheesecakes in Singapore can be found just about anywhere, but they’re not quite the same as the silky delights from Tokyo’s Mr. Cheesecake. With over a million cheesecakes sold in Japan, these masterfully crafted desserts come from chef Koji Tamura. Through the art of Japanese precision, the humble cheesecake has been given a massive upgrade.

A short ferry ride, a change of scenery, and perhaps a long lunch by the water ? Batam is welcoming a new waterfront destination this December , as Opus Bay begins its phased opening with the promise of leisurely island stays, waterfront dining, and a little retail therapy along the way.
Credit – Opus Bay
Just 45 minutes by ferry from Singapore , the integrated resort will make its debut with Marina Bay Ferry Cove , its own ferry terminal, and Residence on Opus Bay , home to the 493-room Balmoral Tower hotel . The best part: the hotel is only a 3-minute walk from the terminal — so less walking, more vacationing!
Credit – Opus Bay
Getting there is as easy as a breeze. The upgraded Marina Bay Ferry Cove will offer direct access to the resort, with ferry connections from Singapore’s HarbourFront and Singapore Cruise Centre . Guests can also look forward to a VIP lounge, dedicated priority lanes, and buggy services to assist with luggage.
Credit – Opus Bay
Beyond checking into your room, there will be more to explore as the resort develops. Bay Boulevard Marina Promenade , opening in a later phase, is planned to bring together waterfront restaurants, a food hall serving local favourites, specialty boutiques, and a supermarket.
Expect a leisurely mix of shopping and dining, with Indonesian designers, locally crafted souvenirs, and resortwear adding a distinctly island-inspired touch.
Credit – Opus Bay
For something to get your blood pumping between meals, Opus Bay will also feature 3 padel courts — including one built to competition standards — alongside 4 pickleball courts . Hotel guests will enjoy complimentary access, so you can work up an appetite before settling in for another meal.
Credit – Opus Bay
While the full line-up of facilities will arrive in stages, Opus Bay is already shaping up to be an appealing addition to Batam’s growing leisure scene . Think an easy island escape without the fuss of a long-haul journey, with the prospect of sea views, unhurried afternoons, and plenty to discover as the resort takes shape.
Planning a year-end getaway? Keep Opus Bay Batam on your radar, and check which facilities are open before making your reservation.

Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup , the Geylang shop that has sold turtle soup since 1946, has opened its first mall outlet at Great World this month, in the year the family business turns 80.
The new restaurant sits at #B1-106/107, 1 Kim Seng Promenade. It opens daily from 11am to 10pm, with last order at 9.30pm, and closes only for Chinese New Year. Great World MRT on the Thomson-East Coast Line (TE15) is the easy way in: Exit 6 leads into the mall at Basement 2, and the restaurant is one floor up.
Claypot Turtle Soup, the house signature since 1986. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
From a shoulder pole to Lorong Bachok
The family traces its roots to Fengtang Xiang in Chao’an. Tan Ah Sai arrived in Singapore in 1927, aged 11, and after the war cooked herbal turtle soup for workers rebuilding the city, selling it bowl by bowl from a shoulder-pole pushcart before saving for a tricycle. He founded the business in 1946.
His son Tan Khar Seng took over the fire in 1973, at 20, while supporting eight siblings, and his wife Tay Ah Lek cooked through the night. In 1986 the shop moved to individual claypots, which the family bills as Singapore’s first claypot turtle soup. It settled at 29 Lorong Bachok in 1992, and the third generation, Vivian and Allan, joined in the 2000s.
The Tan family, photographed in a Singapore studio in the 1960s. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
What a bowl costs
The family publishes dine-in prices for the Geylang shop and has not posted a separate Great World menu, so treat these as the reference point rather than a promise for Kim Seng Promenade.
• Claypot Turtle Soup: S$28 small, S$50 medium, S$78 large
• Double Boiled Turtle Soup: S$16 small, S$21 medium
• Premier Fish Maw and Abalone Soup: S$30
• Ginseng Black Chicken Soup and Cordyceps Chicken Soup: S$15 each
• Sugarcane, Water Chestnut and Imperatae Root Soup: S$9.90
The double-boiled small bowl is the cheapest way into the turtle soups. Sides run from S$6 for cucumber in vinaigrette to S$16.90 for steamed seabass with Teochew olive vegetable, and a bowl of Fragrant Yam Rice is S$2.50. The menu does not state whether service charge or GST applies. Prices on GrabFood, foodpanda and Oddle run higher than in the shop.
Double Boiled Turtle Soup, from S$16 at the Geylang shop. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
Cordyceps Chicken Soup, S$15 at the Geylang shop. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
Before you go
There are no table reservations at either branch. Seating is walk-in, first come, first served. The Great World outlet takes WhatsApp messages only, on 8997 0368. Pick-up orders and food reservations go through a separate WhatsApp line, 8737 2929, and food is set aside once paid.
Tan Ser Seng is not halal-certified. It serves pork dishes, and some soups carry a splash of house herbal wine. The family describes its soups in traditional terms and is clear that the descriptions are not medical advice.
The original shop at 29 Lorong Bachok keeps shorter hours, 11am to 8.30pm daily with last order at 8pm, a five-minute walk from Aljunied MRT.
The Lorong Bachok shop in Geylang, home to the family since 1992. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup

Hi friends, I’ve returned once again to share 5 brand-new eating places across Singapore that have opened recently. If you’ve been following this series (my sincere thanks), you know that I try my utmost best to include 5 vastly different destinations with differing price points to suit various budgets and occasions. And with that, I present to you my list of the 5 new hawker stalls , rosti spots and restaurants that opened in Singapore in Oct 2026 .
Warmhouse Nasi Lemak
Nestled in the blue zone of Chinatown Complex , Warmhouse Nasi Lemak is opened by Singaporean Kenneth and his Taiwanese wife, Cindy, whose dreams were to experience being hawkers in Singapore. This photographer and make-up artist couple decided to combine the food cultures of Taiwan and Singapore onto their plates of coconut rice.
I’m still salivating over the Set B Taiwanese Salt & Pepper Popcorn Chicken Nasi Lemak (S$5.50) . The mini orbs of salt and pepper chicken were plump and juicy, garnished with fried basil leaves. The fluffy coconut rice possesses a strong but not overpowering coconut flavour. The unique, flowy ramen egg won me over. I couldn’t help but wonder why nobody had thought of this pairing sooner because it was soooooo GOOD! I also adored the house-made dried shrimp-laden sambal that wasn’t so sweet and had texture. You can also try the Set A Warmhouse Nasi Lemak (S$5) that comes with chicken wing and luncheon meat.
335 Smith Street, Chinatown Complex, #02-223, Singapore 050335
Petra
Petra is the newest Mediterranean spot at Dempsey by Executive Chef Anas Shami that delivers a fresh perspective of Eastern Mediterranean dining to our shores, paying homage to the region’s culinary traditions, exuberant flavours, and the culture of gathering together to enjoy a meal. The space is romantic and even comes with a pet-friendly outdoor terrace.
Some dishes that remain etched in our memory are the house-baked Barbari w/ Sesame Seeds (S$12) paired with the Mezze Dip Trio (S$32) — hummus , marbukham and taramasalata . The Crispy Falafel (S$18) with ponzu edamame and the thin, crispy Eggplant & Zucchini Chips (S$22) served with tzatziki , saffron honey, and dukkah nuts were great. Seafood lovers will love the Chargrilled Japanese mackerel (S$56) with fennel drizzled in sumac vinaigrette , while the Chicken Shawarma Skewer (S$32) is marinated with hawaij spices and slathered with capsicum sauce.
40C Harding Road, Dempsey Road, Level 1, Singapore 249548
Hippopotato
Thank goodness for Hippopotato , a new addition to the lacklustre food scene at Punggol’s Northshore Plaza . If I’m being brutally honest, there’s hardly anything left to entice me to swing by, especially since Sixth Floor Oyster Cake and Little Caesar have vacated the mall. Hippopotato is run by a pair of brothers, who were previously making rosti as a home-based business at Tampines with raving reviews on Google . Oh, and one of them used to be an ex-chef at Marche dishing out rosti .
There are a total of 9 varieties to choose from starting with the Golden Classic Rosti (S$8) that’s served with just sour cream. The O konomirosti (S$10.50) is perfect for Japanese fans who love a touch of umami with bonito flakes, zingy okonomiyaki sauce, and Japanese mayo crowning the rosti . There’s also other decadent options like Salted Egg Chicken Schnitzel Rosti (S$12.50) and Smokin’ Salmon Rosti (S$13.50) .
407 Northshore Drive, Northshore Plaza I, #02-41 , Singapore 820407
Matsuya
60-year-old Japanese beef bowl chain, Matsuya , has stepped into Singapore’s food scene with its first Singapore outlet landing at the basement of Suntec City . The menu offerings are exactly the same as the ones in Japan, featuring a range of Rice Bowls , Unagi , Japanese curry , as well as Hamburg .
If you’re clueless on what to order, the classic Gyumeshi Beef Bowl (S$5.50 for small) is a good introduction. Enjoy tasty beef slices coupled with sweet onions over fluffy Japanese rice — it doesn’t get more comforting than that. Those with larger appetites can check out their other sizes — from Medium (S$5.90) to Double (S$10.90) . My personal recommendation would be the Gyumeshi topped w/ Green Onion & Mentaiko Mayonnaise (S$8.50 for small) . The combination of spring onions, creamy mentaiko , beef slices, and seaweed had multi layers of flavour that danced in my mouth. Remember to add a Soft-Boiled Egg (+S$1.50) to hit that sweet spot!
3 Temasek Boulevard, Suntec City Mall, #B1-149/149A, Singapore 038983

60-year-old Japanese beef bowl chain, Matsuya , has stepped into Singapore’s food scene with its first Singapore outlet landing at the basement of Suntec City . The menu offerings are exactly the same as the ones in Japan, featuring a range of Rice Bowls , Unagi , Japanese curry , as well as Hamburg .
If you’re clueless on what to order, the classic Gyumeshi Beef Bowl (S$5.50 for small) is a good introduction. Enjoy tasty beef slices coupled with sweet onions over fluffy Japanese rice — it doesn’t get more comforting than that. Those with larger appetites can check out their other sizes — from Medium (S$5.90) to Double (S$10.90) . My personal recommendation would be the Gyumeshi topped w/ Green Onion & Mentaiko Mayonnaise (S$8.50 for small) . The combination of spring onions, creamy mentaiko , beef slices, and seaweed had multi layers of flavour that danced in my mouth. Remember to add a Soft-Boiled Egg (+S$1.50) to hit that sweet spot!
3 Temasek Boulevard, Suntec City Mall, #B1-149/149A, Singapore 038983

Chaleur Atelier Patisserie in JB sells hyper-realistic cakes
Cake lovers heading across the Causeway, here’s one for your JB itinerary . Just a 15-minute drive from JB CIQ , Chaleur Atelier Patisserie makes hyper-realistic, fruit-shaped cakes that look almost too cute to be eat.
2-Day JB Itinerary: Affordable Desserts, Famous Zi Char, Thrifting And More
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.32 as of 30 October 2026.
Chaleur is a modern French cake shop on the ground floor of Zennith Suites Service Apartments .
The whole menu is free of pork, lard, and alcohol. We tried three of its fruit cakes.
First up is the Mango Serai (RM29.80) . Its chocolate coating encases vanilla mousse, vanilla sponge, and a mango serai compote. For those who don’t know, serai is the Malay word for lemongrass, though we couldn’t discern a distinct lemongrass flavour.
Mango lovers will be happy to know there are real mango chunks inside. It’s a little on the sweet side, though, especially with the chocolate shell, so it’s a good one to share.
Next up, the Yuzu Pear (RM29.80) , shaped to look like a green pear.
This cake comprises vanilla pear parfait and a yuzu pear compote on a vanilla genoise, all wrapped in chocolate.
It was the most refreshing of the three, and less sweet than we expected. The yuzu was a nice touch, though we’d have liked it to come through stronger.
Our favourite was the Coconut Gula Melaka (RM29.80) .
Under the chocolate coating are coconut mousse, a Hawaiian pandan coconut layer, and gula melaka pain de Gênes, a French almond sponge. The best part was the real young coconut shreds in the middle. The sponge was a little dry, but the moist, creamy coconut mousse made up for it.
The shop itself is simple, with only a few seats, but it’s clean and works well for a quick dessert stop.
Overall, Chaleur is worth the detour for something unique in JB. Each cake comes to about S$9.20, which is reasonable for this level of workmanship. The shop isn’t far from the checkpoint, so you can dabao a box back to your hotel or even home to SG. Just get them into a fridge as soon as you can, because ours started melting quite fast.
For more cross-border sweet treats, check out our comprehensive JB cafe guide . If you’d rather stay on this side of the Causeway, read our master guide to the best bakeries in Singapore .
Address: Jalan Kebun Teh 2, #01-03, Zennith Suites Service Apartments, Larkin, 80250 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 7pm
Tel: +60 14-665 0928
Website
Chaleur Atelier Patisserie is not halal-certified but uses no pork or lard.

China-famous Yee3 is opening in Singapore this November
Image credit: Yee3
ION Orchard has been popping off lately, with the newly revamped Food Opera and a plethora of new international F&B brands. Now, it’s about to get even more exciting: China’s viral coconut drink brand Yee3 is set to make its debut in the mall in mid-November 2026 , giving competitors a run for their money.
Image credit: Yee3
For the uninitiated, Yee3 is a Shanghai-born brand, best known for its unique spin on coconut drinks. It’s since expanded to more than 500 outlets globally, drawing long queues in Kuala Lumpur and even in Sydney.
The brand prides itself on creating lighter and healthier drinks, using fresh Thai coconut water and no excessive sweeteners in all its products.
Image credit: Yee3
Look forward to an extensive menu of interesting coconut-based flavours and concoctions. The must-order here would be the Pistachio Cloud Coconut Water (price TBD) , with over five million cups sold worldwide. Other drinks in the Cloud Coconut Water Series (price TBD) include Salt Cheese Cloud Coconut (price TBD) and Oreo Storm Coconut (price TBD) .
Image credit: Yee3
Another highlight would be Yee3’s Coconut Frost Shake Series (price TBD) , marking Singapore’s first “frost fried” coconut drink. Made fresh to order daily, every cup comprises flash-iced coconut for a frosty texture and finish, churned with a gelato machine for maximum creaminess.
Choose from a variety of flavours, including Original , Matcha , and fruity options such as Grape , Watermelon , and Mango .
Image credit: Yee3
For mint fans, the Mint Coconut Water (price TBD) is an ultra-refreshing and cooling pick. On top of that, Yee3 also has a Coconut Sticky Rice Series (price TBD) in its line-up, with flavours such as Mango , Pistachio , and Taro .
While we don’t have prices for the upcoming SG outlet, the drinks usually cost between ¥13 and ¥28 in China, which works out to roughly $2.50 to $5.40 at current exchange rates. Do note that prices here may differ.
Although an official launch date has yet to be announced, we’ll keep this article updated with more information once we have it.
In more food news, Singaporean competitive eater Zermatt Neo has just opened Restaurant OVER in Tanjong Pagar. If you’re looking for more Japanese food spots, read our guide to the best new Japanese F&B openings in 2026 .
Address: 2 Orchard Turn, #B4-70, ION Orchard, Singapore 238001
Opening hours: TBD

Yee3 is not halal-certified.

McDonald’s and Pokémon fans, here’s something to look forward to: the Pokémon Happy Meal collaboration is heading to Singapore and Malaysia in December 2026 , following its US launch on 10 Nov .
Credit – @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The collection is said to feature 15 collectible mini box toys and 15 Pokémon trading cards . Each mini box is designed around a different Pokémon , including familiar favourites such as Pikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Bulbasaur, Umbreon and Piplup, alongside other recognisable characters.
Credit – @ModernNotoriety & @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The mini boxes are arguably one of the more interesting parts of the collection. They can reportedly be turned into little charms that you can clip onto your keys, bags or even your trousers.
I don’t know about you, but the idea of having a tiny Pokémon companion from a Happy Meal tagging along on everyday errands, rather than leaving the collectibles at home is actually quite genius!
Credit – @pokehuntdotfun via X (formerly Twitter)
As for the trading cards , leaked photos suggest that the collection could include 15 designs , 7 of which feature a holofoil finish . The alleged line-up includes Jirachi, Tyranitar, Absol, Decidueye, Hawlucha, Pikachu, Palafin, Lucario, Snorlax, Eevee, Metagross, Mimikyu, Chandelure and Wooloo.
However, some reports have listed only 14 stamped cards , so the final selection remains unclear .
Each Happy Meal is also reportedly expected to include 2 Pokémon trading cards , though this detail has yet to be confirmed for Singapore and Malaysia.
The meals may come in special Pokémon-themed packaging , too, with 3 reported box designs featuring Pikachu, Umbreon and Torchic. The exact selection of toys and cards, as well as how they will be distributed, could vary by market.
The McDonald’s x Pokémon collaboration is expected to reach Singapore and Malaysia in Dec 2026, though local prices, exact launch dates and the final selection of toys and cards have yet to be confirmed.
For now, I’m curious to see which Pokémon make it into the local collection, especially if the mini box charms turn out to be as adorable as they sound (and practical, of course)!

Credit – @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The collection is said to feature 15 collectible mini box toys and 15 Pokémon trading cards . Each mini box is designed around a different Pokémon , including familiar favourites such as Pikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Bulbasaur, Umbreon and Piplup, alongside other recognisable characters.
Credit – @ModernNotoriety & @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The mini boxes are arguably one of the more interesting parts of the collection. They can reportedly be turned into little charms that you can clip onto your keys, bags or even your trousers.
I don’t know about you, but the idea of having a tiny Pokémon companion from a Happy Meal tagging along on everyday errands, rather than leaving the collectibles at home is actually quite genius!
Credit – @pokehuntdotfun via X (formerly Twitter)
As for the trading cards , leaked photos suggest that the collection could include 15 designs , 7 of which feature a holofoil finish . The alleged line-up includes Jirachi, Tyranitar, Absol, Decidueye, Hawlucha, Pikachu, Palafin, Lucario, Snorlax, Eevee, Metagross, Mimikyu, Chandelure and Wooloo.
However, some reports have listed only 14 stamped cards , so the final selection remains unclear .
Each Happy Meal is also reportedly expected to include 2 Pokémon trading cards , though this detail has yet to be confirmed for Singapore and Malaysia.
The meals may come in special Pokémon-themed packaging , too, with 3 reported box designs featuring Pikachu, Umbreon and Torchic. The exact selection of toys and cards, as well as how they will be distributed, could vary by market.
The McDonald’s x Pokémon collaboration is expected to reach Singapore and Malaysia in Dec 2026, though local prices, exact launch dates and the final selection of toys and cards have yet to be confirmed.
For now, I’m curious to see which Pokémon make it into the local collection, especially if the mini box charms turn out to be as adorable as they sound (and practical, of course)!
Batam’s new waterfront resort Opus Bay opens this December, just 45 minutes from Singapore

Pokémon fans can look forward to clip-on box charms and possible holofoil cards, although local prices, launch dates, final designs and distribution details remain unconfirmed.

members.body:
McDonald’s x Pokémon Happy Meal
Pokémon fans, rejoice! This December is looking extra exciting, as you’ll soon have another reason to flock to McDonald’s . The fast food chain is bringing its limited-time Pokémon Happy Meals to Singapore, giving local fans a chance to get their hands on some Pokémon collectibles.
What’s in the Pokémon Happy Meal?
Image adapted from: Pokémon & @cop_o_clock via Instagram
Beyond the burger, side, and drink, the toy that comes with the Happy Meal is often the biggest draw. But this time, it could be an even bigger hit than usual. Pokémon has maintained a massive global following for decades, and recent years have shown that the franchise still has an incredible chokehold on fans.
So forget the usual red box with the golden arches. McDonald’s is giving its iconic Happy Meal packaging a Pokémon makeover, with 3 different box designs featuring fan favourites Pikachu, Umbreon, and Torchic.
Image credit: Pokémon
Inside each Happy Meal, you’ll find 1 of 15 collectible mini box charms , featuring adorable designs modelled after Pokémon such as Pikachu, Eevee, Bulbasaur, Popplio, Rowlet, and Sprigatito, among other familiar faces.
Here’s the full list of collectible mini box designs:
• Bulbasaur
• Charmander
• Squirtle
• Cubone
• Pikachu
• Eevee
• Umbreon
• Torchic
• Piplup
• Oshawott
• Minccino
• Espurr
• Rowlet
• Sobble
• Sprigatito
Image credit: Pokémon
But these mini boxes aren’t just meant to sit on your shelf. They can also be converted into adorable charms, so you can take your favourite Pokémon everywhere by clipping them onto your backpack or using them as keychains.
Image credit: @mcdonalds via Instagram
And if the mini box toys aren’t enough to get collectors excited, there’s more. Each Happy Meal also comes with 2 Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) cards , adding to the collecting frenzy that has swept the world in recent years. With 15 cards to collect in total, including 7 foil variants , there’s plenty to hunt down.
Here’s the full list of Pokémon TCG cards you can find:
• Zoroark
• Metagross
• Jirachi
• Eevee
• Snorlax
• Wooloo
• Decidueye
• Chandelure
• Palafin
• Pikachu
• Mimikyu
• Lucario
• Hawlucha
• Tyranitar
• Absol
When will the Pokémon Happy Meal be released in Singapore?
Image credit: Pokémon
According to an official announcement by McDonald’s , the Pokémon Happy Meal will be rolling out in different countries at different times, and the rest of us in Singapore can get our hands on it in December 2026 .
An exact launch date has yet to be confirmed, so we recommend you keep a close eye on McDonald’s Singapore’s Instagram page so you don’t miss out!
Start counting down to the launch of McDonald’s limited-time Pokémon Happy Meal
We can already imagine queues snaking around McDonald’s outlets as Pokémon fans and collectors descend on their nearest branches to snag these limited-edition goodies. Now, the only question is how many Happy Meals it’ll take before you finally catch ’em all!
Other collaborations to check out:
• Starbucks x Winnie the Pooh
• JisuLife x POPMART’s Twinkle Twinkle
• Stanley 1913 x ZO&FRIENDS
Cover image adapted from: McDonald’s & Pokémon
members.summary: No official launch date has been announced yet, but stay tuned for more updates.

A barista at a plant milk booth during the 2025 edition of Singapore Coffee Week. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Singapore Coffee Week returns for its third edition from 5 to 8 November, filling Hall C on Level 1 of Sands Expo and Convention Centre from 10am to 8pm daily. Entry is free and you can simply walk in. Before the doors open, public voting for the Singapore People’s Choice Café Award of the Year 2026 starts tomorrow, 1 November, at 10am.
The event is run by the Singapore Coffee Association, the trade body for the local coffee industry. Its members span coffee traders, roasters, café owners, equipment suppliers and baristas.
How the café vote works
Café entries closed on 20 October, and approved cafés sit on the Singapore Café Map and the official voting platform. Each person gets one ballot tied to a verified Singapore mobile number and can pick up to three different café brands, with each pick counting as one equal vote.
• Online voting runs from 1 November, 10am, to 8 November, 6pm.
• Onsite voting at Sands Expo runs from 10am to 8pm on 5 to 7 November, and from 10am to 6pm on 8 November.
• Cafés are not allowed to offer payments, gifts or discounts in exchange for votes.
The café with the highest verified total is named the Singapore People’s Choice Café Winner of the Year 2026 and gets a trophy, a certificate, a digital badge and a free individual booth at the 2027 edition. The rest of the top ten receive a trophy or certificate and a counter in a shared café pavilion next year.
The interactive coffee map traces coffee’s journey around the world and into Singapore. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
What you can do in Hall C
The Bean Discovery Bar gathers beans from different roasters in one spot, so it suits anyone hunting for a new bag to brew at home. An interactive coffee map traces how coffee spread around the world and how Singapore built its own coffee habits, with trivia along the way.
Sip and Stamp is a coffee discovery trail, and finishing selected activities earns a turn at Spin and Win for coffee goodies and merchandise. There is also a Golden Bean Hunt for 24K golden beans worth S$10,000 in total. Collect any eight stickers on the pre-event Café Hopping Adventure and you receive a location hint for the hunt.
An oat milk exhibitor booth at Singapore Coffee Week 2025. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Exhibitors include A.muse Tea and Co, Addison Institute, Asia Supply Trading, Balance Coffee, Baristart Coffee and Bettr.
Competitions on the floor
Teams in the Singapore Coffee Roasting Team Championship 2026 compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a chance to represent Singapore at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. The Singapore Home Roasting Championship also runs during the four days.
Roasting teams compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a place at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
The Singapore Fashion Drinks Competition takes place on 5 and 6 November, and its top three go on to the 2027 World Fashion Drinks Competition at HOTELEX Shanghai. People’s Choice winners are named on the association’s and the event’s social media channels on 8 November, once the votes are verified.

Little Farms is putting on a one-night Italian dinner at Little Farms Table in Tanglin Mall on Friday, 6 November, with a five-course menu at S$88 per person, and the same weekend brings two free Italian farmers’ markets at its Serangoon Gardens and Tanglin Mall stores. Both sit inside A Taste of Italy , the grocer’s month-long Italian produce and wine programme with the Italian Trade Agency, which runs until 18 November.
Chilled angel hair pasta with buffalo burrata, one of the dinner’s pasta courses. Image: Little Farms
The dinner starts from 5pm. The Little Farms culinary team has built the menu around Italian ingredients that the grocer stocks, and you can take the full five courses or order your favourite dishes à la carte.
On the list are a beef carpaccio and an heirloom tomato salad to start, then a creamy wild mushroom risotto with truffle or chilled angel hair pasta with buffalo burrata. Mains cover a golden Pollo alla Milanese, pan-seared seabass with salsa verde, and grilled O’Connor beef striploin with rosemary jus. Nonna’s Tiramisu, made with espresso and mascarpone, closes the meal. Bookings are open now for what is a single evening, so a Friday table for a group is worth sorting early.
Grilled O’Connor beef striploin with rosemary jus. Image: Little Farms
Free markets on 7 and 8 November
The Italian Farmers Market comes to Little Farms Market at Serangoon Gardens on Saturday, 7 November, and moves to Little Farms Market at Tanglin Mall on Sunday, 8 November. Both days run from 10am to 3pm, and entry is free with online registration.
Expect regional specialities and pantry staples, from olive oil and cheese to pasta and wine, with samples to try and representatives from the participating Italian brands on hand to explain how the products are made. It is the easier way into the programme if you would rather graze and stock up than commit to a full dinner, and since both stores host the same market, pick whichever is closer to home.
The Italian Farmers Market runs 10am to 3pm on 7 November at Serangoon Gardens and 8 November at Tanglin Mall. Image: Little Farms
A wine and cheese class at the Botanic Gardens
The third event lands on the same Friday as the dinner. The Bloomhouse by Little Farms, in Ginger Garden at the Singapore Botanic Gardens, holds an Italian Wine and Cheese Masterclass from 6pm to 8pm on 6 November at S$65 per person.
The guided tasting moves through five Italian wines, from a crisp Vermentino to Chianti and Brunello di Montalcino, each paired with artisan cheeses, with notes on how the pairings work. It has sold out on Little Farms’ own Eventbrite listing, so the Tanglin Mall dinner is the Friday plan still open.
The masterclass at The Bloomhouse by Little Farms pairs five Italian wines with artisan cheeses. Image: Little Farms
Outside the three events, Little Farms stores carry a selection of Italian products through to 18 November.

Grilled O’Connor beef striploin with rosemary jus. Image: Little Farms
Free markets on 7 and 8 November
The Italian Farmers Market comes to Little Farms Market at Serangoon Gardens on Saturday, 7 November, and moves to Little Farms Market at Tanglin Mall on Sunday, 8 November. Both days run from 10am to 3pm, and entry is free with online registration.
Expect regional specialities and pantry staples, from olive oil and cheese to pasta and wine, with samples to try and representatives from the participating Italian brands on hand to explain how the products are made. It is the easier way into the programme if you would rather graze and stock up than commit to a full dinner, and since both stores host the same market, pick whichever is closer to home.
The Italian Farmers Market runs 10am to 3pm on 7 November at Serangoon Gardens and 8 November at Tanglin Mall. Image: Little Farms
A wine and cheese class at the Botanic Gardens
The third event lands on the same Friday as the dinner. The Bloomhouse by Little Farms, in Ginger Garden at the Singapore Botanic Gardens, holds an Italian Wine and Cheese Masterclass from 6pm to 8pm on 6 November at S$65 per person.
The guided tasting moves through five Italian wines, from a crisp Vermentino to Chianti and Brunello di Montalcino, each paired with artisan cheeses, with notes on how the pairings work. It has sold out on Little Farms’ own Eventbrite listing, so the Tanglin Mall dinner is the Friday plan still open.
The masterclass at The Bloomhouse by Little Farms pairs five Italian wines with artisan cheeses. Image: Little Farms
Outside the three events, Little Farms stores carry a selection of Italian products through to 18 November.

Sake Matsuri, which bills itself as Southeast Asia’s largest sake festival, moves to Marina Bay Sands for its 13th edition on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026, with regular tickets at S$60 for a three-hour tasting session . The festival takes over Hall C of the Sands Expo and Convention Centre, and tickets are on sale now.
The organiser puts the pour list at more than 500 sakes, shochu and artisanal spirits from over 100 breweries and distilleries. A craft beer festival, Japan HopFest SJ60 Edition, runs alongside on the same weekend.
The move follows a March 2026 edition at the F1 Pit Building and a November 2025 edition at Jewel Changi Airport, beside the Rain Vortex.
Guests at a past Sake Matsuri edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
How the sessions work
Each day has two sessions: 11am to 2pm and 4pm to 7pm. The halls close from 2pm to 4pm while the organiser turns them over, so tasting stops completely in that gap.
A regular ticket covers one session only. You cannot stay on into the next one. If you want a longer day, you buy a second session or go VIP. Late arrivals still get in, but the session ends on time, so a 6pm arrival for the 4pm slot gets an hour.
An exhibitor booth at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
What a regular ticket gets you
The S$60 regular ticket includes a complimentary Sake Matsuri tasting glass, unlimited sampling across the 500-plus labels and entry to every festival zone, including a dedicated Spirits and Liquor Zone for Japanese gins, whiskies and shochu.
Masterclasses run by sake and shochu educators are included too. Seats are limited and you sign up in person at the Masterclass Lounge on the day. Bottles are on sale at the booths at festival prices.
There is also a food hall. Dishes there are priced separately from the ticket.
Tasting tables at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Bundles and VIP tickets
Groups get bundle pricing on regular tickets: five tickets for S$275, or eight for S$400.
VIP tickets cost S$128 for one person or S$248 for a couple. They cover the full day, both sessions, on your chosen date. On top of everything in the regular ticket, VIP holders get priority for masterclasses, a VIP Lounge for seating through the day and two-day access to Japan HopFest. The lounge stays open during the 2pm to 4pm break, but no food or drinks are served there.
All prices include GST.
A group at the Omu Nomu Craft Sake and Raw Bar booth at a past edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Before you buy
Tickets are final and non-refundable. They can be transferred to someone else if you contact the organiser’s support team at least 48 hours before the event with the new guest’s details.
The organiser strongly recommends buying online in advance and warns that past editions sold out before the festival weekend. Limited tickets might be available at the door.
Alcohol is served only to guests aged 18 and over, and staff can ask for photo ID at registration. Under-18s enter free with an adult but get no wristband or tasting glass. Designated drivers can enter with the ticketed guests they are driving, again without a wristband or glass. Paid parking is available at Marina Bay Sands.
An exhibitor at a past Sake Matsuri edition. Photo: Sake Matsuri Singapore
Details
• What: Sake Matsuri 13th Edition, with Japan HopFest SJ60 Edition alongside (ticketed separately)
• When: Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026; sessions 11am to 2pm and 4pm to 7pm
• Where: Hall C, Sands Expo and Convention Centre, Marina Bay Sands; nearest MRT is Bayfront (Downtown and Circle lines)
• Price: Regular S$60 per session; five for S$275; eight for S$400; VIP full day S$128, or S$248 for two (GST inclusive)
• Age: Alcohol served to guests 18 and over only

deals.body:
Island Penang Kitchen at 721 Clementi West Street 2 was an accidental discovery when I visited the West Coast neighbourhood. The eatery seemed popular, judging from the long line that had formed, so I made a mental note to visit them in the near future.
I also texted my relatives who live in the neighbourhood, and found out that they found the food to be quite good. Since it has been a while since I last had Penang food , I decided to pay them a visit at 11.30am before the lunch crowd arrived. True enough, it was relatively empty— hooray!
What I tried at Island Penang Kitchen
I started with one of my favourite appetisers, the Penang Rojak (Fruits & You Tiao ) for S$7 . I was more inclined on this although they had another variation that had you tiao only at the same price.
My first impression— the generous sprinkling of peanuts— a plus for someone like me who loves nuts in all forms ( ahem … don’t let your imagination run wild).
As for the ingredients, there were pieces of Japanese cucumber, turnip, you tiao and pineapple. But wait, is pineapple the only fruit ? I was a little confused since the combination was similar to a typical local rendition, except for the missing tau pok . I was expecting fruits like jambu to appear.
Nonetheless, I decided to go for it. The pieces of you tiao were super crispy and, most importantly, not hard. The pineapple was sweet and the turnip and cucumber gave varying levels of texture and crunch.
The hei ko sauce was seasoned to perfection and coated the ingredients evenly. Overall, I was pretty satisfied. This was a good start!
Instead of getting the iconic Penang Fried Kway Teow (S$7.80) , I decided to switch things up and ordered the Penang Fried Mi Tai Mak (S$7.80) instead. When the dish arrived, we were immediately captivated by its smoky fragrance.
The ‘rat tails’ were stir fried with slices of Chinese sausage, 2 peeled prawns, bean sprouts, fish cake slices and chives.
The noodles tasted as delicious as they smelled, each strand possessing a robust punch of wok hei smokiness. Although the chilli packed some heat, it still allowed me to taste the other components of the dish without numbing my tongue.
18 best street foods in Penang to uncover [Jan 2025 update]
The prawns were decent and firm, while the strands of tau geh retained a satisfying crunch. We also found mini golden nuggets of pork lard, hiding like bats hibernating in a cave. My only gripe? They were inconsistent— some were crispy and delicious, while others were slightly chewy and soft.
My favourite component of the Penang Fried Mi Tai Mak was the red slices of lap cheong , which injected subtly sweet and savoury notes throughout the dish.
We then shifted our attention to the bowl of Penang Assam Laksa (S$6.80) . The noodles were topped with bits of fish, sliced lettuce, mint leaves and chunks of pineapple.
The noodles used weren’t thick bee hoon but lai fun , which were slightly thicker and had a translucent appearance. It’s the same kind of noodles used in Penang, too— 100 points for authenticity!
The broth was gently tangy but I could hardly taste the umami -ness of the hei ko . Thankfully, we were given a bottle of shrimp paste sauce to enhance the flavour. I added about a full tablespoon of it, and that really helped to redeem the dish.
Initially, we debated whether the fish bits were ikan kembung (mackerel) or sardines, but we leaned towards the former due to its taste and texture. It added a depth of richness to the bowl of laksa .
The slices of pineapple gave the dish a mild sweetness while the mint leaves made things more herby and aromatic.
Since we always reserve a small compartment in our bellies for dessert , we shared a bowl of Penang Homemade Chendol (S$3.50) . Instead of red beans, kidney beans were used alongside the quintessential pandan jelly strands.
After giving it a good mix, the gula melaka at the bottom gradually turned everything a light brown hue. The taste was decent and satisfying, but it was similar to any other chendo l we had tried before— nothing to shout about.
Final thoughts
Overall, we were quite satisfied with the Penang dishes served at Island Penang Kitchen. Although there were some hits and misses, the positives outweigh the negatives.
With a decent menu, reasonable prices, and tasty dishes, I finally understood the appeal and popularity of this eatery, even though it’s tucked away in the back of the heartland neighbourhood where many might overlook it.
I guess from now on, if I’m craving Penang food, this place will be one of my top choices and recommendations.

Osteria Da SuA Korean-Italian restaurant on Telok Ayer Street, Osteria Da Su is an osteria built around the concept of authentic “Italian with a Korean Soul” — rooted in real Italian technique and craft, with Korean flavours woven in as an accent rather than a fusion. The menu specialises in handmade artisanal pasta, alongside Italian mains, small plates and desserts, all served in a warm, osteria-style setting. The restaurant is helmed by Chef Suji Park, who brings close to two decades of culinary experience across Korea and Italy, including three years at three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio in Bergamo and nearly five years on the opening team of Gucci Osteria in Seoul.

deals.body:
New restaurants and cafes in Singapore for November 2026
November is when most of us are already mentally on leave, with year-end dinners filling the calendar. But Singapore’s food scene isn’t slowing down. This month brings a competitive eater’s first restaurant, a Japanese beef bowl chain taking on Sukiya and Yoshinoya, and an ex-fine-dining chef wok-frying pasta at a Bukit Merah hawker centre. Here are the best new restaurants and cafes to check out in November 2026 .
1. Matsuya
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Japan’s Matsuya is one of the country’s most popular gyudon chains, with about 1,200 outlets back home and over 1,500 worldwide. Its first Singapore outlet lands at Suntec City in November 2026 , setting up a three-way beef bowl showdown with Sukiya and Yoshinoya.
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Local prices are still TBD, but in Japan the classic Beef Bowl —thinly sliced beef stewed with onions in sweet soy sauce—goes for just ¥480, or about $3.90. Other bowls include the Beef Bowl with Tomato and Cheese and Beef Bowl with Grated Radish and Ponzu Citrus Soy Sauce , while the Beef Curry with Hamburg Steak ($TBD) is the heartier pick. Ordering and payment are done at a kiosk, so this is very much an in-and-out lunch.
Read our Matsuya feature .
Address: 3 Temasek Boulevard, #B1-125, Tower 2, Suntec City, Singapore 038983
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Matsuya is not halal-certified.
Popular Japanese Gyudon Chain To Open At Suntec In Nov 2026
2. OVER
Competitive eater Zermatt Neo has made his first F&B move with OVER , a Tras Street restaurant about a five-minute walk from Tanjong Pagar MRT Station and Maxwell MRT Station . As you’d expect, size is the whole point—most dishes come in Lesser, Standard, or Challenge portions.
The Curry Me Over (from $23++) was our favourite: a huge, juicy chicken cut in nanban sauce over fragrant Hainanese-style curry rice. The Shroyu-Clams! (from $35++) pack plenty of meat per clam in a buttery, garlicky shoyu sauce made for mopping up with sourdough. The Wing Me Over (from $10++) is shatteringly crispy, though the skin rub was a tad too salty for us.
Feeling brave? The Ultimate Food Challenge (from $239++) gives you an hour to finish an 8kg platter, solo or in a team of up to four, for a free meal, a cash prize, and a spot in the Hall of Fame.
Read our OVER feature .
Address: 54 Tras Street, Singapore 078993
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11.30am to 12am, Sat 3pm to 12am
Website
OVER is not halal-certified.
Zermatt Neo Opens Restaurant With 8kg Food Challenge And Jett Barbecue Collab
3. Xiao Jiao Tian
Image credit: @op3creative
Founded in Fujian in 2013, Xiao Jiao Tian now runs more than 80 kitchens across China and Singapore. After its City Square Mall debut, the Sichuan-inspired chain has opened a second outlet on the third floor of Wisma Atria , a short walk from Orchard MRT Station . The spice is dialled down for a wider range of palates, and every dish is cooked to order.
Image credit: @gracenomz
The signature Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli ($39.90++) is the one to order—tender bullfrog in a spicy, tangy pickled chilli broth. Heat-seekers should get the Chinese Sauerkraut Fish ($29.90++) , with adjustable spice levels, while the Sweet & Sour Pork ($24.90++) keeps things mild. For now, free-flow tea, ice cream, snacks, and rice go for just $1.50++ per person , down from $3++.
Read our Xiao Jiao Tian feature .
Address: 435 Orchard Road, #03-32/33/34, Wisma Atria, Singapore 238877
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 10pm
Website
Xiao Jiao Tian is not halal-certified.
4. Boost
Image credit: Kimberly Chong via Google Maps
Smoothie regulars, it might be time to look up from your usual order. Boost has launched Blends with Benefits , five new blends served in the brand’s first-ever clear cups, each with a functional booster built in.
Image credit: Boost
The All Nighter blends raspberries, mango, passionfruit, and orange with 100mg of Pure Energy, a natural caffeine from guarana. Gym-goers get the First Protein Date , a blueberry-chocolate blend with toasted muesli and 33g of whey protein, or the spirulina-blue Blue My Mind with 5g of creatine. The Green Flag acks 6g of fibre into a lychee, pineapple, and cucumber blend, while the dragon fruit-pink After Glow comes with 5g of collagen. Every purchase also comes with a free sticker sheet for decorating your cup, while stocks last. Prices are TBD.
Website | Full list of outlets
Boost is not halal-certified.
5. Tanica
Image credit: Tanica
Tanica , The Singapore EDITION ‘s signature restaurant, is built around herbs, spice, and live fire. Its name blends “botanical” and “tannins”, and nearly everything passes through a wok or Josper charcoal grill before reaching your table in the greenery-wrapped, arboretum-inspired dining room.
Image credit: Tanica

deals.body:
Best food deals in Singapore for November 2026
November is a tricky month for the wallet. 11.11 sales are already filling your cart, Christmas pre-orders are popping up in your feed, and year-end dinners haven’t even been booked yet. The good news is that dining deals are working just as hard as the online sales this month, from $11 steaks to a 1-for-1 buffet with Old Chang Kee. Here are the best food deals in Singapore for November 2026 .
1. Pepper Lunch: $11 striploin steak for 11.11
Image credit: Pepper Lunch
Skip the online cart this Singles’ Day. On 11 November , Pepper Lunch is serving a 150g Striploin Steak with a drink for just $11 , sizzling on the brand’s signature hotplate with vegetables and your choice of dipping sauce.
Miss the flash deal, and you still get a decent consolation prize: from 3 November to 30 November , the same steak-and-drink combo goes for $16.90 . Both deals are for dine-in at Pepper Lunch Restaurant outlets only, while stocks last, and selected drinks and add-ons cost extra.
Website | Full list of outlets
Pepper Lunch is halal-certified.
2. Barossa Steak & Grill: $12++ Wagyu steak
Image credit: Barossa Steak & Grill
After a $500,000 revamp, Barossa Steak & Grill has reopened at VivoCity with a new waterfront space and a menu from Chef Dylan Ong, formerly the chef-founder of The Masses . To celebrate, the Australian F1 Wagyu Oyster Blade goes for just $12++ from 2 November to 15 November , down from $68++ .
It’s a la carte with no sides, and only for the first 100 customers each day. The deal is walk-in only, with one steak per person and up to 10 people per table, so go early.
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #01-161/162, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Opening hours: Mon-Wed 11.30am to 3pm, 5pm to 10.30pm, Thurs 11.30am to 3pm, 5pm to 11pm, Fri 11.30am to 3pm, 5pm to 11.30pm, Sat 11.30am to 11.30pm, Sun 11.30am to 10.30pm Tel: 8303 1863
Website
Barossa Steak & Grill is not halal-certified.
3. SUSHIRO: Opening sushi deals at Bukit Panjang Plaza
SUSHIRO has opened its 26th Singapore outlet at Bukit Panjang Plaza , a short walk from Bukit Panjang MRT Station , and it’s running a different sushi special every few days until 12 November . Each promotional plate comes with two pieces.
Coming up are Big Red Shrimp ($2.30++) from 3 to 5 November , Big Cut Fresh Salmon ($2.90++) from 6 November to 7 November , Jumbo Scallop ($4.90++) from 8 November to 9 November , and Medium Fatty Tuna ($3.90++) from 1 November to 12 November . The Lemon Sour , Premium Malts , and Kaku Highball are also $6++ each until 12 November, down from as much as $10.50++.
Address: 1 Jelebu Road, #02-17/17A/18/18A/19/19A, Bukit Panjang Plaza, Singapore 677743
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 10pm
Website
SUSHIRO is not halal-certified.
4. Opus Bar & Grill: 1-for-1 Old Chang Kee lunch buffet
Image credit: Opus Bar & Grill
Opus Bar & Grill has teamed up with Old Chang Kee for the Curry On! Sunday Local Lunch Buffet , and adults dine 1-for-1 every Sunday until 29 November . That works out to $108++ for two , or $54++ per person .
The Old Chang Kee corner has a Laksa Infused Popiah and Nasi Lemak Lobster Kueh Pie Tee , alongside the brand’s Curry Chicken Potato Puff . There’s also a laksa station with rock lobster, live oyster omelette, satay, and DIY rojak. Kids aged six to 12 pay $28++ , and those aged five and below eat free.
Read our Opus Bar & Grill Old Chang Kee buffet feature .
Address: 581 Orchard Road, Singapore 238883 (a short walk from Orchard MRT Station)
Buffet hours: Sun 12pm to 2:30pm
Tel: 6730 3390
Website
Opus Bar & Grill is not halal-certified.
This 1-For-1 Hotel Buffet Has Old Chang Kee Dishes, Lobster Laksa And More
5. Pizza Hut: Two pizzas for $22
Pizza Hut ‘s two-pizza bundles are a wallet-friendly fix for a weeknight gathering, with two Regular pizzas for $22 , or two Large pizzas for $33 , until 11 November .
Each bundle pairs one Cheesy 7 pizza, in flavours such as Soy Garlic Chicken and Otah Laksa, with a Favourite pizza, Very Beefy and Cheese ‘N’ Chic among them. You can choose pan, sourdough, thin, or cheesy stuffed crust. It’s for delivery or self-collection via the Pizza Hut app or website, while stocks last. Classic and Specialty flavours cost extra.
Read our Pizza Hut bundle deal feature .
Website | Full list of outlets
Pizza Hut is not halal-certified.
Pizza Hut’s $4.90 Pizza Deal Is Back Till 27 Oct
6. Dian Xiao Er: $9.90 claypot pepper soup
Image credit: Dian Xiao Er
Rainy November evenings call for something hot and peppery. From 1 November , Emerald members of Dian Xiao Er can get the Claypot Pork Tripe & Pork Rib Pepper Soup for $9.90 nett, down from $15.90. It comes piping hot, with tender tripe and meaty ribs in a robust broth that’s generous enough to share.
Buy the eCoupon on the Dian Xiao Er app with no minimum spend. It’s valid for 90 days for dine-in at all outlets, one coupon per table per visit.
Website | Full list of outlets
Dian Xiao Er is not halal-certified.

members.body:
IKEA Singapore is bringing back their highly anticipated Christmas Buffet for its 2026 run, starting this Dec.
Priced at just S $29.90 for adults , S $15.90 for kids under 12 , and FREE for toddlers below 4 , it’s a fantastic option for anyone looking for a decadent Christmas feast that won’t break the bank.
Credit – IKEA Singapore
This year’s all-you-can-eat Swedish feast takes place on just 3 Fridays in Dec 2026, across Singapore’s 3 IKEA outlets. The dates, locations and seating times are as follows:
IKEA Jurong: 4 Dec (Tickets on sale 5 Nov)
• Seating: 7.30pm to 9pm
• Last order: 9pm
IKEA Alexandra: 11 Dec (Tickets on sale 12 Nov)
• First seating: 5pm to 6.30pm (last order at 6pm)
• Second seating: 7.30pm to 9pm (last order at 9pm)
IKEA Tampines: 18 Dec (Tickets on sale 17 Nov)
• First seating: 5pm to 6.30pm (last order at 6pm)
• Second seating: 7.30pm to 9pm (last order at 9pm)
Tickets will be sold in-person only at Swedish Restaurant cashier counters of each respective store on a first-come, first-served basis while stocks last. Make sure your IKEA Family membership is active before queuing up at the counters to snag your tickets!
Credit – IKEA Japan
Diners can look forward to an array of Scandinavian classics like the one and only Swedish meatballs with cream sauce and ASC-certified salmon with hollandaise sauce . Other hearty hot dishes include Beef goulash with carrots and potatoes and Organic penne pasta with tomato sauce .
Credit – IKEA Singapore
The cold selection also comprises many Swedish staples, including ASC-certified smoked & marinated salmon , Swedish salmon salad and Swedish shrimp salad and MSC-certified assorted marinated herring .
Credit – IKEA Singapore
You’ll also find some exclusive festive additions, such as Sliced honey baked ham , and desserts with a Swedish twist like Lingonberry vanilla log cake and Swedish festive biscuits so you can close out your feast on a sweet note.
With tickets set to sell out fast, you’ll want to move quick if you plan to get your fill of unlimited meatballs and smoked salmon this holiday season!
members.summary: IKEA Singapore's Swedish Christmas Buffet returns on select Fridays in Dec 2026 across its Jurong, Alexandra, and Tampines outlets, serving unlimited Scandinavian cold starters, hot savouries, and festive desserts. Priced from S$29.90 for adults and S$15.90 for children under 12, the all-you-can-eat feast is available exclusively to IKEA Family members with tickets sold strictly in-person at restaurant cashier counters on designated release dates in Nov. It offers an affordable dining option best suited for families and budget-conscious diners seeking a festive meal.

Tanica, the modern Asian restaurant at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, has put prices to its first Christmas since opening: a four-course Christmas Eve set dinner at S$165++ per person, and a Christmas Brunch of unlimited small plates from S$128++. Both are taking reservations now.
Plated courses served at Tanica, the image the restaurant uses for its Christmas Eve dinner. Image: Tanica
The restaurant opened in September inside the hotel’s conservatory, a room of palms and green velvet banquettes, with a kitchen that leans on modern Asian flavours. Its regular calendar already runs a three-course weekday set lunch at S$48++, served in 60 minutes with complimentary hotel parking, and a Sunday Table spread from S$98++ with salads, charcuterie, cheeses and pastries. The two Christmas menus are its first festive additions.
The Christmas Eve dinner
The dinner on Thursday, 24 December, opens with a welcome glass of Champagne to toast the season. The first course is a char-grilled rock lobster tart, followed by a confit of Hokkaido scallop. Tea-smoked duck breast is the main course, and the meal closes on a pandan and coconut dessert.
It is a fixed menu rather than a choice of dishes per course, so anyone in your group who avoids shellfish will want to ask the restaurant before booking, since two of the four courses are built on lobster and scallop.
Small plates on a Tanica table, the image the restaurant uses for its Christmas Brunch. Image: Tanica
The Christmas Brunch
The brunch, on Friday, 25 December, takes the restaurant’s weekly brunch ritual and serves brunch classics as small plates, brought to the table without limit. Joining those classics, the festive specials are beef striploin, porchetta, roasted fish and truffle mac and cheese.
There are three drinks tiers:
• S$128++ with juices, soft drinks, coffee and tea
• S$198++ with flowing wines, selected cocktails and spirits
• S$228++ with flowing Champagne
What Tanica has not yet published is the seating times for either meal or a price for children, and no parking arrangement has been given for the Christmas meals. Tanica has also not named the Champagne for either Christmas meal; the regular Sunday Table pours Louis Roederer Collection 246 NV, alongside red and white wines and selected cocktails.
The dining room at Tanica, inside The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road. Image: Tanica
Tables are booked through the reserve link on Tanica’s site, by phone on +65 6329 5000, or by email at tanica.sgedition@editionhotels.com. The restaurant is at 38 Cuscaden Road, and its regular dinner service runs from 6pm to 10pm on Mondays to Thursdays and to 10.30pm from Friday to Sunday.

Third Floor Singapore has opened on the rooftop of Design Orchard at 250 Orchard Road. It is an all-day neighbourhood bar from the team behind award-winning No Sleep Club, with cocktails, wine, coffee, food and music in a relaxed, living-room-inspired setting.
Image: Third Floor
Third Floor Singapore: a casual take on No Sleep Club
Overlooking Orchard Road, Third Floor brings the creativity and technical precision of No Sleep Club, which ranked No. 8 on Asia’s 50 Best Bars 2021 and No. 26 on The World’s 50 Best Bars 2021, into a more everyday space. Think comfortable seating, an open kitchen and bar, and a pace that suits morning coffee, casual lunches, afternoon drinks and evenings with friends.
Image: Third Floor
Founder Juan Yi Jun, who was born and raised in Singapore, says the name comes from her teenage years hanging out around Orchard. “The location became the name, and more importantly, it became ours,” she says. Her career took her through Tippling Club and Operation Dagger before she co-founded No Sleep Club.
Image: Third Floor
Cocktails worth ordering
Drinks start with a memory, an observation or a familiar ritual rather than a spirit. Jun’s graphic design training shapes how ideas are developed, with distillation, fermentation and clarification used to serve the idea, not to show off. Three drinks to look out for:
• Jolly Shandy: a beer-and-lime shandy poured over frozen house-made lime sherbet made from leftover citrus shells and peels, which you stir with a spoon.
• 3 Lime Vodka Soda: calamansi, kaffir lime leaf and Thai sweet lime with a citrus-hop distillate.
• Blue Cheese & Olive: a dirty martini with Stilton-infused gin, fino sherry, vermouth and a house-made tomato concentrate, finished with Gordal olives stuffed with blue cheese cream.
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
A place to return to
Beyond cocktails, Third Floor serves coffee, food, wine and beer through the day. Music and creative collaborations are part of the plan too. Events such as Void Deck Jam, which we covered when it stepped into Design Orchard on 4 October , bring DJs, independent food vendors and local collaborators together without losing the informality of a neighbourhood bar.
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
As Jun puts it: “We take what we do seriously, but that doesn’t mean our guests have to.”
Third Floor Singapore: details
Image: Third Floor / Juan Qian
• Where: Rooftop, Design Orchard, 250 Orchard Road, Singapore
• Reservations: via BistroChat
• Follow: @thirdfloorsg on Instagram for opening hours, events and updates
Looking for more places to eat and drink around Orchard? See how Tan Ser Seng opened its first mall outlet at Great World .
Images: Third Floor, with photography credits to Juan Qian where shown.

A new local fusion Western hawker has officially landed in Little India ! Opened and run by an ex-restaurant chef, Botak Western has set up shop at 638 Veerasamy Road . It boasts an extensive menu composed primarily of hearty Western fare with an innovative local twist, and has already caught the attention of neighbourhood foodies.
Credit – Chen Melvin via Google Reviews
Chef Gino, the talented ex-restaurant chef behind the grill, pairs his work experience in Italian fine dining with bold Asian influences to create original recipes. He shared that opening a hawker stall was a longtime dream and is driven by a straightforward philosophy. “Having worked in restaurants previously, I’ve always believed that good-quality food shouldn’t have to come with a high price tag.”
Chef Gino’s ultimate mission with Botak Western remains clear — “to bring restaurant-quality food to the heartlands at affordable prices, so that everyone can enjoy a good meal without spending too much.” With Chef Gino at the helm, you can expect nothing less than professional cooking techniques and high-quality ingredients. The menu punches way above its price tag, with generous portions and great taste.
Credit – Botak Western
The Pan Seared Barramundi (S$16.80) comes beautifully crispy with white, perfectly flaky flesh served over roasted potatoes and vegetables in a creamy white wine and butter cream sauce. The fillet portion looks generous and hearty, with the dish reminiscent of something you’d find in an upscale restaurant setting.
Credit – Botak Western
If you’re in the mood for a truly unique fusion dish, check out their signature Sarawak Chicken Curry Shepherd Pie (S$10.80) . Underneath the crispy baked mashed potato crust lies a bed of deeply savoury and aromatic Sarawak-style chicken curry. The curry is traditionally prepared with santan — coconut milk — to produce a velvety and smooth texture while imparting a light fragrance to the gravy. The dish is topped off with shavings of mozzarella and parmigiano cheese for added umami .
Credit – Botak Western
Sides lovers, skip the plain fries and grab the Har Cheong Pork Belly (S$8.50) , fried till crisp and golden brown and paired with a punchy cincalok dipping sauce to cut through the unctuousness.
Whether you’re popping in for a quick lunch or a casual weekend treat, this spot proves you don’t need air-con or a fancy setting to enjoy serious restaurant-quality Western eats.

Casa Vostra’s fourth Singapore restaurant is open on level two of Wisma Atria, and it is the first of the chain’s outlets to take reservations. Opening hours are 11.30am to 10pm daily.
A limited number of tables can be booked online , opening 14 days ahead, and most tables are kept for walk-ins. The other three outlets, at Raffles City, Jem and Tampines Mall, take walk-ins only.
The dining room at Casa Vostra Wisma Atria, #02-02/03. Photo: Casa Vostra
Casa Vostra belongs to the Mission Group and is led by chef Antonio Miscellaneo, the chef-owner behind La Bottega Enoteca in Joo Chiat. The restaurant says La Bottega was named Asia’s No. 1 pizzeria in 2023 and 2024 by 50 Top Pizza. The house pizza is the Newpolitan, made with dough cold-fermented for 36 hours and fired at 450°C.
What is only at Wisma Atria

There are three, each S$15: Tomato Tarte Tatin with roasted heirloom cherry tomatoes; Zucchini and Sakura-Ebi with zucchini cream and chips; and Potato, Leek and Speck with ricotta and rosemary. Two white pizzas are new here too. Anchovy 2.0 is S$22, with fiordilatte, anchovies, pizzutello tomatoes and olive dust. Carbonara 2.0 is S$24, with Parmigiano Reggiano, pancetta, egg yolk and black pepper.

members.body:
Casa Vostra is opening at Wisma Atria with famous pizza
Fans of Italian food would likely already be familiar with Casa Vostra . When they first opened at Raffles City back in 2024, the queues stretched out the door—some waiting over an hour just to get a table. Since then, they’ve expanded to JEM and Tampines Mall , giving more diners a chance to try their offerings.
Image credit: Casa Vostra
If you still haven’t made the trip, good news: Casa Vostra is opening their fourth outlet at Wisma Atria , so those who work in the area can get a taste of their new outlet-exclusive menu items. Look forward to their trademarked Roman SquareCrunch Pizza , as well as mascarpone gelato served in a crunchy pastry cone, in collaboration with Mediterranean-Levantine restaurant Petra.
We Visited Casa Vostra Again To See If The Italian Restaurant Fared Better
For those unfamiliar, Casa Vostra is a casual Italian dining concept by Mission Group and Chef Antonio Miscellaneo, the same chef behind La Bottega Enoteca, which is widely regarded as Singapore’s top pizzeria.
What makes the food here different is how it’s made. The pizza dough is cold-fermented and the pasta hand-rolled, with ingredients either sourced directly from Italy or made in-house. Their pizzas come in three styles: Newpolitan Red , which has a San Marzano tomato base, Newpolitan White , featuring a cheese base, and the Doublecrunch , essentially a pizza-sandwich hybrid.
When we visited their OG outlet in 2025, we tried the Peposo ($22++) —braised beef cheek served with rosemary roasted potatoes and finished with black pepper. We also enjoyed the Crab Tagliatelle ($26++) , generously loaded with sweet crab flesh and tossed in a savoury mix of olive oil, garlic, and butter.
On the pizza side, the Tartufo e Funghi ($28++) is a must for truffle fans, topped with fresh black truffle, mushrooms, and a drizzle of truffle oil over a base of Fior di Latte and Taleggio. And if you’re in the mood for something sweet and savoury, the Prosciutto e Figura ($27++) —Parma ham, fig puree, rocket and walnuts on freshly baked dough—holds its own as one of the best pies on the menu.
The new outlet boasts an 85-seater open-plan space, perfect for date nights or a meal out with the fam. Do note that the restaurant operates on a walk-in only basis, so it’s best to head down early to beat the queue.
For more good food in the area, read our Orchard food guide or Somerset food guide . If you’re looking for more Italian food, our guide to the best Italian restaurants in Singapore has got you covered .
Address: 435 Orchard Road, Wisma Atria, #02-02/03, Singapore 238877
Opening hours: TBD

Casa Vostra is not halal-certified.
