Pompompurin + Starbucks collection
ICYMI, Starbucks recently sent Sanrio fans into a frenzy after teasing its upcoming Pompompurin collaboration on Instagram, and finally, the wait is almost over. Celebrating their 30th anniversaries this year, the coffee giant and everyone’s favourite golden retriever are coming together for a special collection featuring SG-exclusive merchandise and freebies.
The Pompompurin + Starbucks collection officially launches on 10th November 2026 , so mark your calendar, especially if you’re a Sanrio fan or know someone who is.
What’s in the collection?
Image credit: Starbucks
The Singapore-exclusive collection gives Pompompurin a Starbucks-inspired makeover, with the adorable character appearing across a range of merchandise and collectibles, and even donning the brand’s iconic green apron.
You can expect to shop a range of cute finds when the collection drops, from tumblers and mugs for your daily caffeine fix to plushies that Sanrio fans will want to kope .
Plush & Plush Keychain
Image credit: Starbucks
The star of the collection has got to be the Pompompurin + Starbucks Plush ($46.90) . Dressed in the green Starbucks apron and his classic brown beret, the huggable plush comes with a sling and 3 mini charms attached – a croissant, a Starbucks coffee cup, and a cookie.
We reckon it’ll be snapped up pretty quickly once the collection launches, so you’d better be ready to act fast if you want to bring one home.
If you’re planning to bring Pompompurin with you on your adventures, go for the smaller Pompompurin + Starbucks Plush Keychain ($29.90) , featuring the character holding a Starbucks cup.
Furry Pouch
Image credit: Starbucks
For something practical, there’s also the Pompompurin + Starbucks Furry Pouch ($29.90) . It has a soft, fluffy texture and comes in a handy size for keeping your little knick-knacks organised. Your AirPods, lipsticks, keys, and other small essentials will finally have a proper home, instead of getting lost in the depths of your bag.
Reusable Bag With Canvas Pouch & Large Reusable Bag
Image credit: Starbucks
If you always have barang-barang to lug around, consider getting the Pompompurin + Starbucks Reusable Bag With Canvas Pouch ($21.90) . The reusable bag can be folded neatly into a compact canvas pouch featuring a Pompompurin print, making it easy to stash in your handbag for your next shopping trip.
There’s also the Pompompurin + Starbucks Large Reusable Bag ($24.90) , with even more room for all your next haul.
Puffy Card Pouch
Image credit: Starbucks
Here’s another excuse to splurge: the Pompompurin + Starbucks Puffy Card Pouch ($20.90) is both cute and functional. You can use it to keep your cards in one place instead of digging through your bag for them. It even comes with a matcha latte charm for the finishing touch!
PVC Pouches (Blind Bag)
Image adapted from: Starbucks
Add a surprise to your shopping spree by getting the Pompompurin + Starbucks PVC Pouches (Blind Bag) ($10.90) . There are 2 designs to collect, but the catch is that you won’t know which one you’re getting until you open the packaging.
12oz Ceramic Mug
Image credit: Starbucks
Since we’re on the topic of Starbucks merch, you can expect a range of drinkware to add to your collection too. One of the cutest picks has to be the Pompompurin + Starbucks 12oz Ceramic Mug ($32.90) , just the right size for sipping your morning coffee or tea.
20oz Stainless Steel Tumbler
Image credit: Starbucks
But if you need caffeine to power you throughout your day, get the Pompompurin + Starbucks 20oz Stainless Steel Water Bottle ($52.90) instead. It keeps your drinks hot or cold, and you’ll get to take your time sipping on your coffee without worrying about it losing its temperature too quickly.
16oz Glass Cold Cup With Lid
Image credit: Starbucks
Can’t get enough of Pompompurin? The Pompompurin + Starbucks 16oz Glass Cold Cup With Lid ($42.90) comes with a Pompompurin straw topper, so you’ll have the golden retriever keeping you company with every sip.
24oz Water Bottle
Image credit: Starbucks
Or get the Pompompurin + Starbucks 24oz Water Bottle ($29.90) , a lighter option for getting your daily hydration in. This would make a great water bottle for little Pompompurin fans too; parents don’t have to worry about their kids lugging around a heavy tumbler or accidentally breaking a glass cup.
10oz Double-Wall Glass With Lid
Image credit: Starbucks
Rounding out the list of drinkware is the Pompompurin + Starbucks 10oz Double-Wall Glass With Lid ($34.90) – you can never have too many cups at home, especially when it’s a Sanrio-themed one.
Ceramic Plate Set
Image credit: Starbucks
The Pompompurin + Starbucks Ceramic Plates Set ($39.90) comes with 2 plates in different sizes, colours, and designs to spruce up your dining table. This is not something you see in Starbucks merch drops every day, but we’re glad they included it.
…

Yeah Gelato opens a new outlet at Jurong Point
Here’s a piece of good news for Westies: Yeah Gelato just launched its 7th outlet in Jurong Point , alongside three unconventional flavour releases. The Black Vinegar Gelato ($9.80++) , Mala Peanut Gelato ($9.80++) , and Misty Green Gelato ($7.80++) have soft-launched at the new outlet and will be available islandwide from 4 November 2026 .
Yeah Gelato: Viral Chinese Chain Opens At Plaza Singapura With Pistachio And Durian Flavours
The Beijing-born gelato brand first opened its doors in Singapore in June 2025 and has since exploded in popularity due to its fresh, daily-made gelato and premium ingredients. Curious about the bold new flavours, we headed down to give them a try.
The three new flavours came with Yeah Gelato’s signature peaks. The Mala Peanut was garnished with fried pieces of chilli, an interesting touch for a dessert.
I was most curious about the Black Vinegar, though I had my doubts about the unusual flavour combination. Surprisingly, it ended up being my favourite.
The tangy vinegar flavour was noticeable, yet subtle. The addition of cream cheese mellowed out its sharpness, resulting in unexpected caramel-like notes.
The Mala Peanut was another interesting number. It ended up tasting like peanut butter-flavoured gelato, with a mala aroma in the background. It reminded me of a thick, nutty, peanut-sesame dipping sauce that I would enjoy alongside a spicy bowl of mala, but in gelato form.
Of course, I had to try it with the fried chilli—it turned out to be crunchy and sweet with barely a hint of spice. The crunch and slight savouriness added a nice contrast to the creamy, sweet gelato.
The Misty Green Gelato is the most familiar flavour, made with matcha and green tea, which sets it apart from other matcha products. Personally, I could pick up on both flavours, though subtly. The green tea added a roasted, nutty flavour profile that complemented the earthy matcha notes.
We also tried out some of Yeah Gelato’s existing signatures. If you’re new to the brand, its Pistachio Gelato ($9.80++) is a fan favourite. While I’m not a pistachio fan, I immediately understood the hype. The pistachio flavour was rich and pronounced, with just the right amount of sweetness to balance its nuttiness.
Another best-seller worth trying is the Premium Rice Gelato ($7.80++) .
We also tried the Vanilla Gelato ($7.80++) , which is a staple in every gelato store. This one was speckled with real vanilla beans, giving it a rich, fragrant flavour. And the Hawthorn Gelato ($7.80++) hit me with a wave of nostalgia, as it tasted just like the hawthorn flakes that I’d snack on as a child.
The cafe in Jurong Point had a nice, calming ambience, with wooden furniture and beige walls, designed to mirror the serenity of a Chinese rice field.
To celebrate the new launch, Yeah Gelato is offering a 1-for-1 promotion at the Jurong Point outlet from 6 November to 8 November 2026, and 50% off a second cup from 9 November to 12 November 2026 .
On the topic of gelato, check out CHAGEE’s new gelato series , with eight new tea-inspired flavours. While you’re in Jurong, here’s a guide to some Jurong East food gems worth trying.
Address: Jurong West Central 2, #01-58/59 , Jurong Point, Singapore 648886
Opening hours: Daily 10:30am to 10pm
Tel: 9622 9676

The tangy vinegar flavour was noticeable, yet subtle. The addition of cream cheese mellowed out its sharpness, resulting in unexpected caramel-like notes.
The Mala Peanut was another interesting number. It ended up tasting like peanut butter-flavoured gelato, with a mala aroma in the background. It reminded me of a thick, nutty, peanut-sesame dipping sauce that I would enjoy alongside a spicy bowl of mala, but in gelato form.
Of course, I had to try it with the fried chilli—it turned out to be crunchy and sweet with barely a hint of spice. The crunch and slight savouriness added a nice contrast to the creamy, sweet gelato.
The Misty Green Gelato is the most familiar flavour, made with matcha and green tea, which sets it apart from other matcha products. Personally, I could pick up on both flavours, though subtly. The green tea added a roasted, nutty flavour profile that complemented the earthy matcha notes.
We also tried out some of Yeah Gelato’s existing signatures. If you’re new to the brand, its Pistachio Gelato ($9.80++) is a fan favourite. While I’m not a pistachio fan, I immediately understood the hype. The pistachio flavour was rich and pronounced, with just the right amount of sweetness to balance its nuttiness.
Another best-seller worth trying is the Premium Rice Gelato ($7.80++) .
We also tried the Vanilla Gelato ($7.80++) , which is a staple in every gelato store. This one was speckled with real vanilla beans, giving it a rich, fragrant flavour. And the Hawthorn Gelato ($7.80++) hit me with a wave of nostalgia, as it tasted just like the hawthorn flakes that I’d snack on as a child.
The cafe in Jurong Point had a nice, calming ambience, with wooden furniture and beige walls, designed to mirror the serenity of a Chinese rice field.
To celebrate the new launch, Yeah Gelato is offering a 1-for-1 promotion at the Jurong Point outlet from 6 November to 8 November 2026, and 50% off a second cup from 9 November to 12 November 2026 .
On the topic of gelato, check out CHAGEE’s new gelato series , with eight new tea-inspired flavours. While you’re in Jurong, here’s a guide to some Jurong East food gems worth trying.

deals.body:
Tokyo’s iconic dessert sensation, Mr. CHEESECAKE , is officially debuting in Singapore with an exclusive pop-up at ION Orchard from 11 Nov to 30 Dec 2026 . Founded by acclaimed Chef Koji Tamura, the cheesecake brand has achieved legendary status — selling over 1 million whole cakes globally.
Prior to establishing Mr. CHEESECAKE, Chef Tamura built a distinguished career at world-renowned fine-dining establishments, including Mirazur and Restaurant ES in France. He also served as head chef at Tokyo’s TIRPSE, which is famous for receiving a Michelin star in the shortest time in the world.
Despite his impressive resume, Chef Tamura was most inspired by childhood memories of his mother’s home-baked treats and his own experience of baking a cake for a high school friend’s birthday. He began crafting cheesecakes late at night and sharing them on social media. The overwhelming online response eventually led him to depart from fine-dining kitchens and launch Mr. CHEESECAKE.
What sets Mr. CHEESECAKE apart from other cheesecake brands is its signature dual-layer construction that consists of a delicately baked top layer paired with a velvety, near-rare bottom layer. This unique construction is deliberate, allowing the flavours, aroma and mouthfeel of the cake to evolve with temperature changes and provide different sensory experiences with the same cake:
Frozen: Enjoyed straight from the freezer for a refreshing, ice-cream-like bite.
Half-Thawed (1–1.5 hours): Offers a dual texture with a frozen centre wrapped in a creamy outer coat.
Fully Thawed: Unlocks rich sweetness and aroma with a silky consistency akin to creme brulee.
We got to sample Mr. CHEESECAKE Matcha (S$69) , RICH TIRAMISU (S$69) and Mr. CHEESECAKE Sakekasu Coconut (S$69), served fully thawed. Do note that cakes are only sold whole and portions pictured in my article are tasting samples.
My favourite cake by far was Mr. CHEESECAKE Sakekasu Coconut , which carried sweet and floral tropical notes. This unusual combination pairs sake kasu with rich coconut and uplifts it with a touch of lychee puree. The sake kasu , which is the leftover pressed lees from sake production, brings a mildly yeasty and tangy flavour — akin to yoghurt — to the cake.
This gentle acidity pairs well with the smooth, buttery profile of the coconut and pleasant floral aroma of lychee, making for a complex and layered profile with depth without feeling too heavy or sweet.
Another offering that I thoroughly enjoyed was Mr. CHEESECAKE Matcha (S$69) . It might be too intensely earthy for casual drinkers like me, but dedicated matcha lovers are bound to adore it. It also features light, creamy mascarpone and a dash of vanilla to balance the richness and slight bitterness of the matcha. Despite the bold flavours of this cake, it remains remarkably light and enjoyable with just the right level of sweetness.
Finally, we moved on to the RICH TIRAMISU (S$69). Rather than a purely traditional tiramisu, Mr. CHEESECAKE’s version incorporates Japanese ingredients like hojicha , which imparted an earthy, roasted aroma.
Building on that roasted aroma, the addition of browned butter lends more depth and a slight nuttiness to the overall profile. In the middle sits a thin, crisp almond dacquoise layer to provide a textural variation from the mousse-like interior. However, for a tiramisu, I found it rather lacking in coffee flavours.
Driven by Chef Tamura’s humble ethos — “Not the world’s best, but we make your days the best” — this limited-time pop-up brings one of Japan’s most coveted pastries to local dessert enthusiasts. Make sure to head down between 11 Nov and 30 Dec 2026 to get a taste of his renowned cheesecakes.

deals.body:
Tiger Remix is here, and Singapore gets it first. Tiger Beer has launched the flavoured lager range globally in Singapore and Malaysia, starting with two Asian-inspired flavours: Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime.
Image: Tiger Beer
What is Tiger Remix?
Tiger Remix keeps the crisp, balanced character of the brand’s premium lager and adds a fruit-and-tea twist. Peach Oolong pairs juicy peach with aromatic oolong tea for a smooth finish, while Yuzu Lime combines zesty yuzu and tangy lime for a brighter, citrus-led sip. Both are described as low in bitterness, which should make them an easy first step for drinkers who find regular lager too sharp.
Both variants contain 4.2% ABV and come in 320ml cans.
Image: Tiger Beer
Street-culture design, local roots
The packaging leans on Asian street culture, with signboard-inspired typography, shophouse forms and motifs that reflect the region. Tiger was born in Singapore in 1932, and Magdalene Tan, Head of Marketing of Asia Pacific Breweries, said the debut here carries special significance: Singapore is shaped by cultures from around the world yet remains distinctly Asian at heart.
Sam Fielding, Tiger Global Brand Director, framed the range as a new flavour platform for the brand, with Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime as the first two releases.
Where to buy Tiger Remix in Singapore
Tiger Remix is available now in single-can and 3-pack formats at 7-Eleven stores islandwide and on RedMart. A progressive rollout to major supermarkets, including FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and Giant, follows this November.
If you are stocking up for the festive season, our guide to FairPrice’s current in-store voucher offer may help. For more drinks news, see how Third Floor is pouring creative cocktails at Design Orchard, and the Pompompurin + Starbucks collection arriving on 10 November.

House of Spells , a UK-based multi-fandom store, is opening its first outlet in Asia at 118 Mall KL , on 1 Dec 2026 , bringing collectibles inspired by Harry Potter , The Lord of the Rings and more to local fans.
Credit – House of Spells
Founded in 2016, the retailer brings together officially licensed merchandise from popular film, television and fantasy franchises. Potterheads can look forward to items inspired by Harry Potter and Fantastic Beasts , while fans of Game of Thrones , The Hobbit , Stranger Things , Marvel, DC Comics and Studio Ghibli will have plenty to browse too.
Credit – House of Spells
The collection includes magic wands , character figurines , themed apparel , jewellery , stationery , mugs , posters and other collectibles . You might find something to add to your display shelf, a souvenir featuring your favourite character or a gift for that friend who can recite the entire film from memory.
Credit – House of Spells
Beyond the merchandise, House of Spells aims to make the shopping experience part of the attraction. Its stores feature fantasy-inspired interiors, atmospheric lighting and interactive displays designed to evoke the fictional worlds behind the products. Staff who share an enthusiasm for these franchises are also available to help visitors explore the collections.
Credit – House of Spells
The brand operates several stores across the UK, including in London, Liverpool and Stratford-upon-Avon, as well as an outlet in New York City. Its Kuala Lumpur opening marks its first move into Asia, giving Malaysian fans a new place to discover officially licensed merchandise without travelling overseas.
Do note that the exact look and layout of the KL store have yet to be revealed.
Situated at 118 Mall within the Merdeka 118 precinct in KL, the opening House of Spells could be a fun addition to your next shopping trip , even if you only intend to browse. After all, resisting a collectible featuring your favourite character is one thing; having an entire store of them in front of you is another.

Best Japanese buffets in Singapore
If someone told me I could pick only one cuisine to eat for the rest of my life, I’d choose Japanese cuisine in a heartbeat. I love how Japanese dishes can seem so simple, yet taste incredibly satisfying, which is why the idea of having unlimited servings of them feels even more irresistible. Few things compare to indulging in endless plates of sushi, sashimi, and grilled delights.
My love for Japanese fare has led me to compile a list of the 20 best Japanese buffets in Singapore, featuring spreads of sushi, sashimi, and other Japanese favourites across a wide range of price points. If you are looking for even more buffet suggestions, we also have guides to cheap buffets starting from $7 , as well as the best hotel buffets in Singapore .
Best Japanese buffet spots, in a nutshell:
• Cheap Japanese buffet in Singapore : Shabu Sai – Lunch buffet starting at just $18.99++
• Most Instagrammable buffet: Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant at Orchard Central – Popular buffet overlooking Orchard
• Most unique buffet: Maguro Samurai – Singapore’s first omakase buffet at Robertson Quay
• For special occasions : Gyu-Kaku – All-you-can-eat premium Japanese Wagyu cuts
<$40++ per person
1. Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant – Popular buffet in Orchard Central
Cheap Japanese buffet from $30.90++
Image credit: Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant
What is Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant? One of the more popular Japanese buffet restaurants in Singapore is Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant , located on the eighth floor of Orchard Central, which offers a wonderful view of the bustling Orchard Road. Lunch will set you back at $30.90++ while dinner is priced at $49.90++ per person . You can find a range of tempura, sushi, teppanyaki, and skewers here. For a broader selection with premium dishes, it’s highly recommended to go during dinner, which includes rotating items such as snow crab legs , oysters , robatayaki crayfish and more.
Expect to pay: $30.90++ per person (Lunch), $49.90++ per person (Dinner)
What to order: Aburi Salmon , Snow Crab Legs, Maguro Sashimi
Address: 181 Orchard Road, #08-01/02/03, Orchard Central, Singapore 238896
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 3pm, 6pm to 10pm
Tel: 9817 5259
Website
Kiseki Japanese Buffet Restaurant is not halal-certified.
2. SUKI-YA – Iconic all-you-can-eat hotpot chain
Authentic Japanese broths at affordable prices
What is SUKI-YA? A popular choice among hotpot lovers, SUKI-YA is one of the few restaurant buffets in Singapore that specialise in Japanese-inspired sukiyaki and shabu-shabu. There’s no need to be afraid of burning a hole in your wallet here as their lunch buffets are going at just $23.90++ , every Monday to Thursday, and $28.90++ on Friday to Sunday. Choose from six different broths, including a hearty pork-based broth and fresh soya miso, a nutritious and milky broth. This meaty feast gives access to chicken, pork, and beef, and you get to pick from three different dips: ponzu , sesame , and fresh egg .
Expect to pay: $23.90-$28.90++
What to order: Mala Miso, Shabu-Shabu, Sukiyaki
Website | Full list of outlets
SUKI-YA is not halal-certified.
3. Tenkaichi – Award-winning BBQ restaurant at Marina Square
Japanese BBQ buffet overlooking the Marina Bay skyline
What is Tenkaichi? For the best meat and sashimi Japanese buffet in Singapore, Tenkaichi is a strong contender. Choose from three choices of buffet starting from $29.80++ on Mondays to Thursdays, and $35.80++ on Fridays to Sundays: Standard , Deluxe , and Premium . There are quite a few cuts of meat to choose from at their Deluxe Buffet , including thin-cut Wagyu shabu shabu and Angus ribeye steak. Make sure to leave room in your tummy for sashimi, of which you can choose from fish such as salmon, tuna, and sea bream.
Expect to pay: $29.80-$94.80++ (Mon-Thur), $35.80-$99.80++ (Fri-Sun)
What to order : Ton Toro, Miso Buta Kata Rosu
Address: 6 Raffles Boulevard, #03-129, Marina Square, Singapore 039594
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11:30am, to 2:30pm, 5:30pm to 10pm, Sat-Sun 11:30am to 10pm
Website
Tenkaichi is not halal-certified.
4. Kiwami Ramen & Gyoza Bar – Ramen buffet in Tanjong Pagar
Free-flow ramen with over 25 sides at Guoco Tower
What is Kiwami Ramen & Gyoza Bar? Available at their Guoco Tower and VivoCity outlets, Kiwami offers one of the more unique Japanese restaurant buffets in Singapore: an all-you-can-eat ramen galore. From just $28.80++ per person , you get to try eight kinds of ramen, sides and more, all at unlimited portions! You can find their signature ramen offerings here, such as the Premium Kiwami Tonkotsu Ramen , made with a 10-hour pork bone broth that’s rich and creamy. You can even try variations of this dish, such as with black garlic oil, mala, and yuzu. You can also get 10 different side dishes to fill your belly, and end your meal with various ice cream flavours.
Read our Kiwami ramen buffet feature .
Expect to pay: $28.80++ per person

deals.body:
Tiger has two new cans in the fridge, and Singapore gets them first. Tiger Remix is a new range of flavoured lagers in Peach Oolong and Yuzu Lime, and the brand is giving it a global debut here and in Malaysia before anywhere else.
Both flavours are built on the crisp Tiger lager most of us already know from hawker centre tables and kopitiam fridges. The twist is in the fruit and the tea: Tiger describes the range as its signature taste paired with distinctive Asian-inspired flavours, drawing on the energy and self-expression of Asia’s street culture.
Two flavours, two moods
Peach Oolong mixes Tiger beer with juicy peach and aromatic oolong tea. Tiger pitches it as effortlessly easy to drink, and it is the softer, rounder of the two on paper, with the tea there to stop the peach going too sweet.
Yuzu Lime is the sharper one. It pairs the crisp lager with zesty yuzu and tangy lime, a citrus combination built for group nights out rather than a quiet can at home.
Both come in 320ml cans at 4.2 per cent ABV.
Yuzu Lime is the sharper of the two; Peach Oolong leans softer. Image: Tiger Beer
Where to buy Tiger Remix
Tiger Remix is on shelves now at 7-Eleven stores islandwide and on RedMart, in single cans and 3-packs. Supermarkets follow through November, with a progressive rollout at FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and Giant.
FairPrice already has both flavours on its online store. A 3-pack of 320ml cans carries a usual price of S$9.95, and an offer price of S$9.50 runs until 30 November. The BCRS container deposit is charged on top and refunded when the empty cans go back to a return point.
Good to know
Tiger Remix is an alcoholic drink, and FairPrice’s online store tells shoppers under 18 to remove alcohol from their cart before checkout.
For a first can, Peach Oolong suits drinkers who like things on the gentler side, while Yuzu Lime is the pick for anyone who wants more citrus bite with their supper.

HANDO is a new izakaya with affordable Japanese fare
Image credit: HANDO
A Japanese izakaya has just opened in Bendeemer , offering affordable bar snacks and other small plates. Soft-launched on 30 October 2026, HANDO has a modern concept, with a dimly lit interior and laid-back atmosphere designed for friends to gather and hang out.
20 Bendemeer Food Places For KL Ban Mian, Orh Nee Puffs And More
The restaurant’s signature is its handrolls, made in front of you across the counter, so you can enjoy them fresh. Each handroll is customisable, with your choice of red or white vinegar, rice portion, and wasabi.
Image credit: HANDO
Prices start from $8++ with the Tai handroll . For a more indulgent option, the Uni Bomb ($28++) is loaded with fresh uni and uni cream. Other options include Seared Anago ($10++) , made with grilled eel, and Engawa ($10++) , an incredibly rich, buttery fish.
If you’re torn between choices, they offer sets such as The HAND-Some One ($45++) , which includes five rolls, and The Full HANDO ($78++) , which has seven rolls, including the Uni Bomb.
For a full lunch, the Quick HANDO ($28++) comes with three rolls, miso, pickles, and cold tea. You can top up with the More Fun ($18++) set, which offers two off-menu rolls on top of an existing set.
Image credit: HANDO
Beyond hand rolls, the izakaya also serves grilled food, bar bites and more. This includes Chicken Thigh skewer ($4.50++) , Shiitake skewer ($8++), and Mix Fish ($14++) , a selection of sashimi dressed in sesame sauce and seaweed tempura.
Image credit: HANDO
If you’re with friends, the HANDO Karaage ($12++) , Fish Skin (8++) , and Corn Tofu ($9++) are suited for sharing. For something heartier, the HANDO Uni Udon ($28++) has udon with uni cream, topped with more uni and ikura.
For more new Japanese eateries opening in Singapore, check out these Japanese F&B openings in 2026 for fried sando, hot stone gyukatsu and more. If you’re in Bendeemer looking for dessert, check out our Keong Saik Bakery review !
Address: 28 Cavan Road, Singapore 209855
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 2:15pm, 6pm to 9pm
Website
HANDO is not halal-certified.

Yup, you heard me right. Inspired by the success of his first Singaporean venture just months prior, Michelin-recognised Chef Shusaku Toba behind Sio Pasta in Raffles City has opened an upscale alternative among the colourful shophouses of Tanjong Pagar . While Sio Pasta focuses on fast and casual meals, the newly unveiled o/sio — which officially opens 4 Nov 2026 — pivots towards a complete dining experience while keeping prices reasonable.
With the original o/sio branch hailing from the affluent Marunouchi district in Tokyo, you can expect nothing short of impeccable standards from this new expansion. Additionally, a second branch of Sio Pasta is in the works and is slated to open in late 2026 to mid 2027.
Here’s what we tried ahead of o/sio’s official opening:
My personal favourite, the Snow Crab Genovese (S$26.80) struck a perfect balance between fresh, herbaceous flavours and rich umami from the G rana Padano . The rustic pesto sauce was a little coarse and had a nice mouthfeel. It leaned more towards being bright and less salty than a typical pesto, which was a great move considering the mountain of fresh snow crab meat crowning the pasta. The crab was slightly sweet and naturally briny, which added the subtle saltiness that the dish needed to shine.
The noodles had a unique texture, where they were slightly chewy and QQ , almost like udon noodles — rather than purely al dente . To me, this dish was exemplary of the fusion between Japanese ingredients and Italian techniques that o/sio specialises in.
Moving onto another classic Italian dish, we tried their Maple Quattro Formaggi (S$16.80) . It features an ooey-gooey mascarpone cream base, with melted Fior di Latte on top. The pizza is speckled throughout with crumbled G orgonzola and freshly grated G rana Padano , giving it a sharp, intense flavour every few bites.
The pizza dough at o/sio goes through an arduous fermentation process, which yields a light, flavourful crust in the final product. All the pizzas are then baked in a wood-fired oven for under 2 minutes, demonstrating complete mastery of heat control.
To really elevate the pizza to a whole new level, be sure to add a drizzle of the provided maple syrup. It’s a creative alternative to the more traditional honey pairing and adds even more to the dish with its subtle woody undertones which complement the funk of the gorgonzola better than I could have imagined.
Considering the quality and attention to detail of the dishes, the quality-to-price ratio here is more than decent.
If you’re looking for your next budget-friendly date night spot, be sure to check out o/sio, which officially opens its doors on 4 Nov 2026.

Bookworms rejoice, especially if you reside in the north! Frasers Centrepoint Trust has partnered up with the National Library & Archives Board (NLB) to open The HomePage @ Causeway Point . Labelled as “Singapore’s first-of-its-kind” in a media release by Frasers Property, the hub is slated to open in 2028 as a brand-new reading and social destination. Spanning over 32,000 sq ft across parts of the mall’s sixth and seventh floors , the space will bring together books, community activities and family-friendly experiences.
Credit – Frasers Property
The name and design of The HomePage @ Causeway Point are inspired by the concept of home. Just as a home offers comfort, the hub will welcome visitors into a warm and inviting space. The design draws inspiration from familiar parts of Singapore’s architectural history, including the iconic Teck Whye HDB estates, the former NLB library at Stamford Road and the geometric forms of Brutalist architecture in the 1970s.
Credit – Frasers Property
One of Singapore’s largest publicly accessible assemblages of pre-loved books from NLB will also be available here for browsing. The collection of books includes both English and Mother Tongue languages. Look through the pre-loved books and bring them home without having to borrow them! There’s no return-by date; instead, we are encouraged to pass on the books to others to share the joy of reading.
Credit – Frasers Property
#Supportlocal; there will also be a dedicated showcase of Singapore Literature (Sing Lit) and local authors. NLB will curate the space alongside the National Arts Council . Through their wide variety of Sing Lit titles, thematic exhibitions and programmes, you can look forward to celebrating Singapore’s literary heritage.
Credit – Frasers Property
Beyond the books, it will also serve as a social hub for all ages. You’ll be able to enjoy food and beverages while relaxing with a book. The space also includes family-friendly amenities such as children’s play zones, an indoor theatre and a screening space. One key feature of The HomePage is The Social Steps , a multi-purpose terraced public living room where visitors can gather, unwind or participate in community activities.

Pokémon fans in Singapore, good news — PokéXciting! has arrived at Changi Airport and Jewel , until 3 Jan 2027 . This special Asia tour celebrates the 30th anniversary of the beloved pocket monsters with exciting events such as parades, meet-and-greets, and more.
The wider festivities last until 3 Jan 2027 , but there are highlights you won’t want to miss on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , including a thrilling parade with many, many Pokémons. Keep an eye out for the exclusive PokéXciting! Pikachu , sporting a fluffy blue hairstyle. This rare Pikachu can be caught around Changi Airport and Jewel using the Pokémon GO app.
Credit – The Pokémon Company
Over at Jewel , there will be a Pokémon Parade featuring all 27 starter Pokémon from 9 generations of the video game series, alongside not 1 but 2 Pikachus. This adorable spectacle will take place at Jewel’s Level 1 Forest Valley on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , 3pm and 6pm daily .
As the Pokémon march in sync with the music during the parade, it’s bound to be a heartwarming sight. Admission is free with registration required on-site prior to entry. Do note that each session operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
Don’t miss out on redeeming free Pikachu sun visors and Pokémon 30th Anniversary stickers . Grab ’em at Level 1 (opposite Porsche) on 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , 12pm – 9pm daily , on a first-come, first-served, while stocks last basis.
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Be sure to catch the PokéXciting! Special Night Sho w at Terminal 3 Departure Hall (Level 2, in front of Departure Immigration) on 7 and 8 Nov 2026, with shows daily at 4.30pm and 7.30pm . During the show, Pikachu dances to thrilling EDM beats under dazzling lights. Do note that you’ll also have to register prior to entry, with the queue opening an hour before each session.
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Besides watching the Pokémon, you can get up close with them during the various meet-and-greet sessions. On 7 and 8 Nov 2026 , meet Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander, and Squirtle at 12pm , 2pm , 8pm and 9pm .
There will be other sessions on 14, 15, 21, and 22 Nov 2026 as well as on 5, 6, 12, 13, 19, and 20 Dec 2026 at 2pm , 3pm and 6.30pm for each date. You can expect to see Pikachu alongside other characters like Eevee, Snorlax, Gengar, Piplup and Mimikyu. The 2pm and 3pm sessions are at T3 Departure Hall , while 6.30pm sessions are at T3B2 ST3PS .
Credit – Changi Airport Group
Be sure to snap Pokégenic photos across 4 themed zones at Jewel’s Forest Valley, which has more than 30 installations . There’s even an enormous Pikachu! The wider festivities last until 3 Jan 2027, so don’t worry if you can’t make it on certain days — there are many more activities for you to explore.
More information, including operating hours for individual events, is available HERE ; go catch ‘em all!

City Hall food guide
City Hall MRT Station is right smack in the middle of the East-West Line and North-South Line, making it one of the more convenient places to meet up with friends. Peppered with malls, there is no shortage of City Hall food places to choose from. Look below for our round-up of food gems to check out when in the area.
1. Ureshii
Korean-Japanese restaurant Ureshii is nestled away at The Arts House , a convenient eight-minute walk from City Hall MRT Station . Naturally, the menu is heavily influenced by a blend of Korean and Japanese flavours, such as the Kurobuta Udon Kimchi Soup ($28++) : a spicy-tangy kimchi soup with udon and pork meat. Alternatively, the Truffle Oil Tsuyu Pasta ($28++) is a great choice for those who enjoy oil-based pasta. This dish features fragrant truffle oil, aged tsuyu, and black tobiko.
Read our Ureshii review .
Address: 1 Old Parliament Lane, #01-02, The Arts House, Singapore 179429
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 11:50am to 2:50pm, 6pm to 11pm, Sun 11:50am to 2:50pm, 6pm to 10pm
Website
Ureshii is not halal-certified.
This Korean-Japanese Restaurant Has Jeju Abalone Porridge And Cheese Tonkatsu In City Hall
2. Alice Boulangerie
Popular cafe Alice Boulangerie has a second branch at Raffles City , and what sets this outlet apart from the OG is the addition of Fine Crumbs Bakery . There are more than 15 buns available every day, and some of our favourites are the Black Sesame Peanut Mochi Bun ($4.80++) , which nods to muah chee, Matcha Nama Bun ($6.50++) , and Pistachio Cream Bun ($6.80++) .
If you’re dining with friends or colleagues, we recommend the incredibly flavourful Chargrilled Chicken ($38++ for half) , featuring seasonal vegetables on the side. There’s also Smoked Black Cod($39++) , served with a tomato and olive stew.
Read our Alice Boulangerie review .
Address: 252 North Bridge Road, #01-22A, Raffles City Shopping Centre, Singapore 179103
Opening hours: Daily 9:30am to 10:30pm
Website
Alice Boulangerie is not halal-certified.
Alice Boulangerie Opens At Raffles City, Get Fresh Buns With Matcha Nama And Pistachio Cream
3. Broth & Beyond
Many think that CHIJMES only houses fancy restaurants, but that’s not true. Broth & Beyond is a value-for-money hotpot spot offering fresh, locally sourced ingredients from Yunnan. Their Flavour Discovery Set is priced at $39.90++ per person , which includes one broth flavour, a portion of meat, a veggie basket, a portion of rice or la mian, and access to the Market Table, which is essentially a huge condiment and dessert station. If you can’t decide which broth to get, consider the Black Truffle Assorted Mushroom Broth that’s simmered for eight hours using chicken fat and Yunnan mushrooms to achieve a rich, robust flavour.
Read our Broth & Beyond review .
Address: 30 Victoria Street, #B1-01/02, CHIJMES, Singapore 187996
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 11:30am to 11:30pm, Fri-Sat 11:30am to 2:30am
Website
Broth & Beyond is not halal-certified.
We Ate At This New Yunnan Hotpot Restaurant In The CBD That Opens Till 2:30AM Daily
4. Daily Beer
Another CHIJMES gem is Daily Beer , a popular Korean fried chicken restaurant that’s perfect for your chimaek (chicken and beer) night. You can’t go wrong with the classic Angry Bird (from $29++) , but if you want to take it up a notch, the Angry Bird Crunch (from $31++) , seasoned with corn flakes and garlic, is a better choice.You must get their craft beers to pair with your chicken; there are 10 beer flavours on the menu, such as K-Ginseng Lager ($13++) , K-Red Lager ($14++) , and the outlet-exclusive Chijmes Hazy IPA ($15++) .
Read our Daily Beer feature .
Address: 30 Victoria Street, #01-04, CHIJMES, Singapore 187996
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 11:30am to 11pm, Fri-Sat 11:30am to 12:30am
Website
Daily Beer is not halal-certified.
Daily Beer: Popular Korean Fried Chicken And Craft Beer Chain Opens In SG
5. Mensho Tokyo
If you’re after quality Japanese ramen and don’t mind splurging, Mensho Tokyo is the perfect spot. The restaurant currently has 18 outlets worldwide, with its San Francisco outlet even being/getting featured in the Michelin Guide.
The Singapore location has also grown in popularity since its opening in 2024. Some must-gets include the Signature Toripaitan ($28++) , with A5 Wagyu, house-made wheat noodles, and other premium noodles in a rich chicken broth. You can also go all in with the A5 Wagyu Shoyu Aburasoba Ramen ($41++) , featuring two types of Miyazaki A5 Wagyu and noodles drenched in an aged shoyu sauce.
Read our Mensho Tokyo review .
Address: 252 North Bridge Road, #03-43, Raffles City Shopping Centre, Singapore 179103
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 9pm
Tel: 8380 8467
Website
Mensho Tokyo is not halal-certified.
Mensho Tokyo Review: Michelin-Approved Ramen With Duck Matcha And Famous Chicken Broth
6. Hopscotch
Image credit: Hopscotch Bar

Three Bowls serves kolo mee at Whampoa Makan Place
Image credit: T greensake via Google Maps
If you want a Din Tai Fung-quality meal without its price tag, this hawker stall is worth checking out. Helmed by former Din Tai Fung chef Robin Lee, Three Bowls serves up East Malaysian fare at Whampoa Makan Place .
Paying homage to his roots, Chef Robin offers Sabah-style kolo mee, less com mon in Singapore than the Sarawak-style. The key difference lies in the darker, savoury soy sauce base, which gives Sabah-style noodles a richer, more robust flavour compared to the lighter, shallot oil-based Sarawak version.
Image credit: Wilfred Loy Yong Kang via Google Maps
Signature dishes are the Pork Chop Kolo Mee ($6.90) and Pork Chop Mee Soup ($6.90) , both featuring a Din Tai Fung-style fried pork chop.
Image credit: Patricia Lim via Google Maps
Alternatively, you can keep it simple with the Home Taste Kolo Mee ($4.50) and Home Taste Mee Soup ($4.50) , served with slices of char siew.
Other kolo mee options include Chicken Chop Kolo Mee ($6.50) , Fish Roll Fish Ball Mee ($4) , and Wanton Kolo Mee ($4) , available soup or dry.
If you opt for dry noodles, you can also customise your sauce. Choose from three options: White, a savoury shallot oil sauce; Black, a dark soy sauce with a hint of sweetness; or Red, a sweet char siew oil sauce.
Image credit: Zoey W via Google Maps
Another specialty of Three Bowls is the Homemade Knife-Cut Noodles ($6.90) , featuring chef Robin’s hand-pulled noodles—said to have a chewy texture and topped with fish balls and meat balls.
While the store is relatively new, it’s already built a solid fanbase with long queues every day. If you love the iconic Ding Tai Fung pork chop, then you need to give this a go.
If you found this story interesting, check out our Nomad Kitchen review , featuring a hawker stall opened by an ex-hotel and F&B manager. For more Malaysian food recommendations, check out our guide to the best Malaysian food places in Singapore.
Address: 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-14 Whampoa Makan Place, Singapore 320090
Opening hours: Mon, Wed-Sun 1pm to 4:30pm, 5pm to 9pm
Three Bowls is not halal-certified.
Ex-Hotel Manager Opens Stall With Lesser-Seen Dishes From 7 Countries: Here’s Our Review
Feature image adapted from Kevin and Lin Eva

deals.body:
I’ve heard of food and music festivals all my life, but never have I come across a festival dedicated entirely to celebrating and honouring Jejudony Pork . That was until I travelled to Jeju Island to attend the 2-day 2026 Jeju Dosaegi Festival that took place at Saebyeol Oreum area , Aewol-eup from 17 to 18 Oct 2026 .
If you’re wondering what an oreum is, it’s that volcanic cone rising in the background.
Every year, Koreans from all over the country travel to Jeju just to attend this prestigious festival. In Korea, pigs are highly-regarded and considered the ultimate sacrificial offering when praying to the gods and ancestors. They are also slaughtered at weddings and funerals purely for culinary purposes.
White, circus-like tents fill up the vast festival grounds with retail shops peddling products like honey, soju , sausages, mechanical keyboard accessories, and much more.
Farmers receive VIP treatment here, complete with a dedicated seating area set aside in their honour. There are tons of activities happening all day long, including games, a roaming karaoke-on-wheels contest, and performances by the Marine Corps Military Band and Sori Punggyeong Children’s Choir . On Day 2, the legendary South Korean hip-hop duo, Dynamic Duo , made a guest appearance to fire up the crowd — see how big of a deal this is?
Stroll through the festival grounds to try your hand at darts, or browse the flea market to pick up a unique souvenir. Got little ones in tow? Let them bounce their energy away at the kids’ play area or craft adorable critters out of pipe cleaners!I even spotted a dedicated zone where kids can unleash their artistic talent by doodling on the ground with chalk.
A long, snaking queue had formed in front of the Jejudony Pork Booth with throngs of people relishing on cooked pork samples, immediately catching my attention. When I spotted the 25% discount on 500g packets of Pork Neck and Pork Belly, each priced at just ₩10,000 ( ≈ S$9.65) — that’s equivalent to below S$10 per meat — I finally understood what the appeal was.
Need a quick fuel-up amidst all the festivities? No sweat. Check out the outdoor food truck cafeteria where you’ll find plenty of street food options to choose from like skewers, corn dogs, and tornado potatoes. Need your daily caffeine fix? You’ll find fresh coffee available alongside a selection of refreshing fruit juices. October is considered one of the best times to visit Jeju, so rest assured the weather will be nice and cool.
Wait, I know some of you may be thinking, “I need proper food. This won’t even fill me up!” Fret not, there are makeshift restaurants and we visited one that was run by the Jeju Pig Farming Cooperative Women’s Club . You’ll be taken care of by a bunch of warm and friendly ahjummas . The place served hearty meals and soju (if you fancy a tipple).
You can enjoy a scrumptious Seafood and Green Onion Pancake (₩10,000 , S$9.57) or slurp on a hot bowl of Meat Noodles ( ₩5,000 , S$4.79) . The Meat Noodles come with freshly-steamed Jeju pork — you’ll soon realise that the meat has such a clean taste and possesses a perfect meat-to-fat ratio. For an extra touch of decadence, share a plate of Boiled Pork ( ₩15,000 , S$14.36 ). Just dip it in soy sauce, pair it with kimchi , and you’re good to go!
We had a clearer glimpse of Jejudony Pork’s versatility over at Kang Chef’s Kitchen. Chef Kang took us on a culinary journey through Jeju pork, highlighting the many creative ways this prized meat can be prepared right here in Singapore.
We started off with the Pork Jowl Sushi , where Chef Kang replaced the usual fish with tender pieces of grilled pork jowl, served with a vibrant chives salad. Next up was the Boiled 5-Layer Pork Belly Noodles — it was impressive how beautifully this dish came together with simple accompaniments like seaweed, cucumber, and lettuce.
One of my favourites was the lip-smacking Traditional Jeju-Style Seasoned Pork Skewers , which Chef Kang served with asparagus, oyster mushrooms, and peppers. Since it was a Singaporean-themed night, he intentionally replaced the usual onion, big leek, and carrots with bok choy for his Spear Squid w/ Stir-Fried Black Pork Shoulder dish. Both the pork and squid were cooked to tender perfection.
One of the specialities of Kang Chef’s restaurant is his tangsuyuk (Korean sweet and sour pork) and it was the perfect opportunity to showcase it for the Loin Tangsuyuk , Pig Trotter w/ Chilli . Korean restaurants in Singapore typically use lean cuts for the tangsuyuk . Chef Kang’s loin rendition had more fats that made it extra creamy and juicy — hands down, one of the best I’ve had in my life!
I also had the chance to visit the Jejudony Pork Meat Processing Plant , gaining firsthand insight into the advanced quarantine and bio-security protocols that supply their partner farms with premium breeding pigs.

We started off with the Pork Jowl Sushi , where Chef Kang replaced the usual fish with tender pieces of grilled pork jowl, served with a vibrant chives salad. Next up was the Boiled 5-Layer Pork Belly Noodles — it was impressive how beautifully this dish came together with simple accompaniments like seaweed, cucumber, and lettuce.
One of my favourites was the lip-smacking Traditional Jeju-Style Seasoned Pork Skewers , which Chef Kang served with asparagus, oyster mushrooms, and peppers. Since it was a Singaporean-themed night, he intentionally replaced the usual onion, big leek, and carrots with bok choy for his Spear Squid w/ Stir-Fried Black Pork Shoulder dish. Both the pork and squid were cooked to tender perfection.
One of the specialities of Kang Chef’s restaurant is his tangsuyuk (Korean sweet and sour pork) and it was the perfect opportunity to showcase it for the Loin Tangsuyuk , Pig Trotter w/ Chilli . Korean restaurants in Singapore typically use lean cuts for the tangsuyuk . Chef Kang’s loin rendition had more fats that made it extra creamy and juicy — hands down, one of the best I’ve had in my life!
I also had the chance to visit the Jejudony Pork Meat Processing Plant , gaining firsthand insight into the advanced quarantine and bio-security protocols that supply their partner farms with premium breeding pigs.

Good news for anyone who has been eyeing those Korean burgers from afar. Lotteria is now halal certified in Singapore, with both outlets at Jewel Changi Airport and Jurong Point listed on the MUIS HalalSG directory. The brand announced it on its official Instagram on 3 November 2026, a day after rolling out a new Teriyaki burger series.
When the South Korean chain opened at Jewel in February 2026, it was pork-free and lard-free but carried no halal cert. That kept a lot of Muslim diners at the window instead of the counter. Nine months on, that gap is closed.
Lotteria halal certified: what the MUIS listing shows
We checked the MUIS HalalSG establishment search on 6 November 2026. Two Lotteria outlets appear under the Eating Establishment scheme, restaurant category:
• 63 Jurong West Central 3, #01-47/48/87/88/89/90/91, Jurong Point (certificate EERT26100000119)
• 78 Airport Boulevard, #B1-248, Jewel Changi Airport (certificate EERT26100000120)
In plain terms: this is a MUIS halal-certified restaurant, not just a “no pork, no lard” kitchen. Halal certification in Singapore is issued per outlet, so if Lotteria opens a third branch, check the HalalSG listing for that address before you go. The Lotteria Singapore website now carries the Singapore halal logo too.
Source: Lotteria Singapore
What to order at Lotteria, with prices
Lotteria does not publish its a la carte prices online, and counter prices can shift, so the figures below are the deals the brand has posted on its official Instagram. Burgers are the main event here, and the Ria’s range is the one Koreans grew up with.
• Student Deal: any 2 burgers for S$10 (Double Bulgogi Beef Burger excluded), weekdays only, valid till 30 November 2026. Show a valid photo student pass and order at the counter.
• Add 2 regular soft drinks and 1 large fries to the Student Deal for S$3.50 more.
• Breakfast Burger Combo at Jewel: S$5 for a Beef Burger, K-Omelette Chicken Sausage or K-Omelette Turkey Bacon with a Milo, daily 10am to 12pm.
• Breakfast for two at Jurong Point: 2 K-Omelette Chicken Sausage plus Tater Tots for S$10.50, weekdays 9am to 11am.
• Coffee at Jurong Point: any 2 cups for S$5.80, daily till 12pm.
Without a deal, these are the ones to go for:
• Ria’s Beef Bulgogi Burger, the sweet soy-glazed patty that made the brand’s name in Korea (there is a double version if you are hungry)
• Ria’s Shrimp Burger, a thick prawn patty and a cult favourite
• the new Teriyaki series: Teri Egg Beef, Double Teri Egg Beef and Teri Egg Crispy Chicken, all with a fried egg, for a limited time
• Gangjung Chicken, coated in a sweet-spicy Korean glaze, sold by the piece or as a burger
• Shake Shake Fries for the seasoning-bag drama, and the Mango Peach Bingsu if you still have space
Source: Lotteria Singapore
Lotteria Jewel Changi Airport: address, hours and MRT
• Address: 78 Airport Boulevard, #B1-248, Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore 819666
• Opening hours: daily, 10am to 10pm (last order 9.30pm)
• Nearest MRT: Changi Airport (EW29/CG2), then walk through Terminal 2 or 3 to Jewel’s basement level
Jewel is the more touristy of the two, so expect a queue around lunch on weekends. It works well as a pre-flight meal, or as the bribe that gets the kids to the Rain Vortex without complaint.
Lotteria Jurong Point: address, hours and MRT
• Address: 63 Jurong West Central 3, #01-47/48/87/88/89/90/91, Jurong Point, Singapore 648331
• Opening hours: Monday 9am to 10.30pm (last order 10pm); Tuesday to Sunday and eve of public holidays 9am to 12.30am (last order 12am)
• Nearest MRT: Boon Lay (EW27), linked to Jurong Point via the bus interchange
Jurong Point opened in August 2026 and keeps much later hours, which makes it the better bet for supper. Westies, this one is yours. If you need a refresher on the outlet itself, our earlier Lotteria Jurong Point guide covers the layout and launch details.
Is it worth the trip?
For Muslim families who have been asking Korean friends to bring Lotteria back from Seoul, yes, finally. The burgers are fast-food burgers, not atas smash patties, but the bulgogi sauce and the shrimp patty taste different from anything at the big American chains. Go on a weekday afternoon with a student in tow and two burgers come to S$10, which is quite the lobang.
We first flagged Lotteria back in June with its S$5 Jewel breakfast combo . For a sit-down halal option with more variety, J65’s halal buffet at Hotel Jen Tanglin is another one we have covered. Deals and limited-time items change often, so check @lotteriasg before heading down.

Planning a beach day at Sentosa just got tastier. Palawan Hawkers has officially launched at The Palawan @ Sentosa , and brings a vibrant cluster of 8 food trucks dishing out everything from decades-old heritage recipes to modern fusion bites.
Brought to you by the team behind Cosford Container Park, famous for being Singapore’s largest F&B container park, this pet-friendly open-air space serves up wallet-friendly bites starting at just S$5.90 .
Amongst the myriad offerings, look out for nostalgic heritage brands like Qing Heritage Hainanese Chicken Rice . They are known for their Hainanese Kampung Chicken Rice (price TBD) with tender steamed kampung chicken and their signature ginger paste, made from a secret recipe passed down since the 1940s. With its original outlet stationed all the way in Dover, Palawan Hawkers lets you can enjoy a taste of tradition by the beach.
Nearby, Boon Tat Street BBQ Seafood brings nearly 38 years of history to the shore, firing up smoky grilled BBQ Sambal Stingray (price TBD) , BBQ Prawns (price TBD) and Sotong (price TBD) . The seafood is then dressed in signature sambal chilli sauce — which was refined by its founder through years of trial and error — before being served on banana leaves to impart extra fragrance into the dish.
If you’re in the mood for something on the more experimental side, look out for Palawan Beer House , evolved f rom the popular Cluny Toast at the Singapore Botanic Gardens. They offer modern, elevated twists on local classics such as Sourdough Peanut Butter Toast (price TBD) and other innovative dishes created from collaborations with various Singapore dining brands. Some such dishes include Bacon & Egg Pizza by YOUNGS Restaurant & Bar (price TBD) and Authentic Signature Laksa (price TBD) by Nyonyas & Gentlemen at Village Katong Hotel.
To round things off, Urban Truck hits the spot with spicy, cheese-stuffed Indian fusion creations like Stuffed Parathas (price TBD) and Cheesy Kola Meatballs (price TBD) , while Creamy Duck Milkshake Bar cures sweet tooth cravings with a trendy Kunafa Pistachio Waffle (price TBD) and a thick, creamy Triple Chocolate Milkshake (price TBD) .
Operating daily from 11am to 9pm , it is an ideal pitstop to fuel up without breaking the bank after splashing around Sentosa .

Cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers sorted by area
Frankly, cafe-hopping in Singapore is an expensive hobby to have. Order one main and a drink, and there goes $30. But it’s a different story when you’re making use of your CDC Vouchers, which, by the way, aren’t just for grocery shopping or hawker meals. Check out our list of the best cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers for your next coffee run or WFH day.
66 Best Cafes In Singapore You Must Try
CBD cafes
1. The Better Half
Run by a young couple, The Better Half is a cosy nook at Everton Park selling drinks and fresh bakes. Almost everything is on display here, so take your time to pick what you’d like.
If you don’t know what to get, we recommend starting with their crowd-favourite Pistachio Raspberry ($8.50) : a pistachio cake with raspberry jam and the same tangy-zesty filling and buttercream. There’s also the lesser-seen Honey Kinako ($8.80) , featuring a wildflower honey cake with kinako buttercream and matcha glaze, finished with kinako crumble.
Read The Better Half review .
Address: 1 Everton Park, #01-43, Singapore 081001
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 10:30am to 4pm
Website
The Better Half is not halal-certified.
2. Bag Me Up Bagel House
Bag Me Up is another Everton Park gem that’s a stone’s throw away from The Better Half. This under-HDB cafe specialises in bagels and focaccia, all under $20!
If you prefer bagels, consider their Can Trust Chick ($14.50) , a simple combination of tender chicken patty and melted cheese. Something new on the menu is the Smash Bagel ($16.50) , which uses smashed beef patty as the key ingredient, alongside melted cheddar, caramelised onions, and a sunny-side-up.
Read our Bag Me Up Bagel House review .
Address: 2 Everton Park, #01-59B, Singapore 081002
Opening hours: Tue & Sat-Sun 9am to 3pm, Wed-Fri 9:30am to 3pm
Website
Bag Me Up is not halal-certified.
Bag Me Up Review: Unagi And Wagyu Beef Bagels At This Under HDB Bagel Shop Near Outram Park
3. Elijah Pies
If we had to introduce a cafe in Singapore known for pies, Elijah Pies would instantly come to mind.
Out of their nine flavours, the stunning Wild Berry Lavender Pie ($9++) is a bestseller. It features a crispy crust topped with fresh yoghurt infused with real berries and a hint of lavender, creating the perfect balance of tangy and creamy. Speaking of fruity flavours, the Yuzu Meringue Pie ($9++) and Lime Thyme Pie ($8.50++) are great alternatives. Otherwise, go straight for the Speculoos Hojicha Pie ($8.50++) or Pistachio Praline Pie ($9.50++) ; the former sees caramelised cookie butter and aromatic notes of roasted green tea.
Read our Elijah Pies review .
King George’s outlet
Address: 803 King George’s Avenue, #02-216, Singapore 200803
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 10am to 6pm, Sat-Sun 10am to 4pm
Tanjong Pagar outlet
Address: 7 Tanjong Pagar Plaza, #01-102, Singapore 081007
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 10am to 10pm, Fri-Sat 10am to 10:30pm
Website
Elijah Pies is not halal-certified.
Elijah Pies Review: IG-Famous Bakery Opens Chio Cafe With Mac N’ Cheese Pie, Matcha Latte Pie And More
4. Hello Arigato
Hello Arigato has six outlets at the time of writing, and their Everton Park, Joo Chiat, and Seng Poh Road branches accept CDC Vouchers. We recommend the former for a serene atmosphere, while the latter is great if you want to dine within a Scandinavian-esque space.
The cafe is known for sando, such as the crowd-favourite Porkatsu Sando ($26++) and the popular Gyu Sando ($28++) . The Gyu Sando is especially worth a try, comprising a thick beef tenderloin katsu paired with caramelised sweet onion jam. There are pastas too, including the creamy Hokkaido Milk Udon Carbonara ($22++) and flavour-packed Mentaiko Pasta ($22++) . FYI, the menu varies depending on the outlet you’re visiting.
Read our Hello Arigato review .
Everton Park outlet

Opening hours: Daily 9am to 5pm
Joo Chiat outlet
Address: 314 Joo Chiat Road, Singapore 427565
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 9am to 5pm, Sat-Sun 8am to 5pm
Tiong Bahru outlet
Address: 58 Seng Poh Road, #01-15, Singapore 160058
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 9am to 4pm, 5:30pm to 9pm, Sat-Sun 8am to 4pn, 5:30am to 9pm
Website

5. Pretty Good Muffins
ICYMI: Pretty Good Muffins went viral for their affordable muffins and matcha latte in early to mid-2025. After trying their goods, we can tell you that the Chinatown cafe’s hype isn’t dying down anytime soon because their muffins are, quite literally, pretty good .

Cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers sorted by area
Frankly, cafe-hopping in Singapore is an expensive hobby to have. Order one main and a drink, and there goes $30. But it’s a different story when you’re making use of your CDC Vouchers, which, by the way, aren’t just for grocery shopping or hawker meals. Check out our list of the best cafes in Singapore that accept CDC Vouchers for your next coffee run or WFH day.
66 Best Cafes In Singapore You Must Try
CBD cafes
1. The Better Half
Run by a young couple, The Better Half is a cosy nook at Everton Park selling drinks and fresh bakes. Almost everything is on display here, so take your time to pick what you’d like.
If you don’t know what to get, we recommend starting with their crowd-favourite Pistachio Raspberry ($8.50) : a pistachio cake with raspberry jam and the same tangy-zesty filling and buttercream. There’s also the lesser-seen Honey Kinako ($8.80) , featuring a wildflower honey cake with kinako buttercream and matcha glaze, finished with kinako crumble.
Read The Better Half review .
Address: 1 Everton Park, #01-43, Singapore 081001
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 10:30am to 4pm
Website
The Better Half is not halal-certified.
2. Bag Me Up Bagel House
Bag Me Up is another Everton Park gem that’s a stone’s throw away from The Better Half. This under-HDB cafe specialises in bagels and focaccia, all under $20!
If you prefer bagels, consider their Can Trust Chick ($14.50) , a simple combination of tender chicken patty and melted cheese. Something new on the menu is the Smash Bagel ($16.50) , which uses smashed beef patty as the key ingredient, alongside melted cheddar, caramelised onions, and a sunny-side-up.
Read our Bag Me Up Bagel House review .
Address: 2 Everton Park, #01-59B, Singapore 081002
Opening hours: Tue & Sat-Sun 9am to 3pm, Wed-Fri 9:30am to 3pm
Website
Bag Me Up is not halal-certified.
Bag Me Up Review: Unagi And Wagyu Beef Bagels At This Under HDB Bagel Shop Near Outram Park
3. Elijah Pies
If we had to introduce a cafe in Singapore known for pies, Elijah Pies would instantly come to mind.
Out of their nine flavours, the stunning Wild Berry Lavender Pie ($9++) is a bestseller. It features a crispy crust topped with fresh yoghurt infused with real berries and a hint of lavender, creating the perfect balance of tangy and creamy. Speaking of fruity flavours, the Yuzu Meringue Pie ($9++) and Lime Thyme Pie ($8.50++) are great alternatives. Otherwise, go straight for the Speculoos Hojicha Pie ($8.50++) or Pistachio Praline Pie ($9.50++) ; the former sees caramelised cookie butter and aromatic notes of roasted green tea.
Read our Elijah Pies review .
King George’s outlet
Address: 803 King George’s Avenue, #02-216, Singapore 200803
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 10am to 6pm, Sat-Sun 10am to 4pm
Tanjong Pagar outlet
Address: 7 Tanjong Pagar Plaza, #01-102, Singapore 081007
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 10am to 10pm, Fri-Sat 10am to 10:30pm
Website
Elijah Pies is not halal-certified.
Elijah Pies Review: IG-Famous Bakery Opens Chio Cafe With Mac N’ Cheese Pie, Matcha Latte Pie And More
4. Hello Arigato
Hello Arigato has six outlets at the time of writing, and their Everton Park, Joo Chiat, and Seng Poh Road branches accept CDC Vouchers. We recommend the former for a serene atmosphere, while the latter is great if you want to dine within a Scandinavian-esque space.
The cafe is known for sando, such as the crowd-favourite Porkatsu Sando ($26++) and the popular Gyu Sando ($28++) . The Gyu Sando is especially worth a try, comprising a thick beef tenderloin katsu paired with caramelised sweet onion jam. There are pastas too, including the creamy Hokkaido Milk Udon Carbonara ($22++) and flavour-packed Mentaiko Pasta ($22++) . FYI, the menu varies depending on the outlet you’re visiting.
Read our Hello Arigato review .
Everton Park outlet
Address: 4 Everton Park, #01-42, Singapore 080004
Opening hours: Daily 9am to 5pm
Joo Chiat outlet
Address: 314 Joo Chiat Road, Singapore 427565
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 9am to 5pm, Sat-Sun 8am to 5pm
Tiong Bahru outlet
Address: 58 Seng Poh Road, #01-15, Singapore 160058
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 9am to 4pm, 5:30pm to 9pm, Sat-Sun 8am to 4pn, 5:30am to 9pm
Website
Hello Arigato is not halal-certified.
Hello Arigato Everton Park Review: $13+ Tamago Sando, Matcha Cloud And More
5. Pretty Good Muffins
ICYMI: Pretty Good Muffins went viral for their affordable muffins and matcha latte in early to mid-2025. After trying their goods, we can tell you that the Chinatown cafe’s hype isn’t dying down anytime soon because their muffins are, quite literally, pretty good .

Nordic-inspired Christmas at Cedele
Pumpkin spiced latte season is out, and logcake season is in. This year, local favourite Cedele is celebrating the Christmas season, Nordic style, featuring wholesome ingredients and comforting flavours freshly made in Singapore, with a spread of new and returning hits that are sure to set the mood for sleigh bells jingling, ring-ting-tingling too .
First up, the savouries: Santa’s Surf & Turf Croissant Platter ($68) , a set of 12 buttery mini croissants sandwiching luxe crab mayo, as well as tender pulled beef.
You may recognise the platter from past editions, but here’s something new to 2026’s line-up━ Cheese & Spinach Brioche Wreath with Festive Dips ($48) . It’s the perfect grazing dish to kick off your Christmas feast, with your choice of Garlic Spring Onion or Pork Bacon Cream Cheese Dip .
Trust us when we say you’re missing out if you skip this. Think: warm, fluffy little cheese-speckled bread balls, dipped into creamy, umami-laden bacon cream cheese. You’re not drooling, we are.
Returning this year is the Truffle Mushroom Crown ($48) , another Christmas favourite at Cedele. You couldn’t ask for a better combi than this, with flaky, buttery pastry plus earthy diced forest mushrooms, elevated with truffle oil.
Rest assured, it’s not all about the finger foods, because Cedele’s bestselling Wagyu Beef Shepherd’s Pie ($79) is back on the menu this year!
Cedele fans will know the absolute treat this is, with a rich, tomato-based Wagyu braise below, and ultra smooth, fluffy mash on top, finished to golden perfection in the oven.
Balance this out with an order of Jolly Mesclun Salad ($48) , tossed in a bright, zesty yuzu vinaigrette that’ll have your palate refreshed before the sweets.
This year, the dessert spread is shaking things up with a Winterberry Banana Cake ($80) . As with all of Cedele’s bakes, it’s baked fresh daily right here in Singapore, with unrefined sugars or no trans fat .
If banana cake is your go-to sweet treat, this festive edition is layered with darling baby pink strawberry cream cheese, adding a bright, berry note to the rustic cake.
Then, there’s the all-new Winter Hearth Cheesecake ($60) , inspired by the warm hug of Nordic spices.
This cake starts with cardamon-infused cheese, poured over with toasty caramel apples, and given texture by a buttery walnut streusel. Don’t let the idea of cardamon sway you━this combi had us thinking of fireside cuddles on a snowy winter’s day.
Of course, Christmas ain’t Christmas without log cakes, and Cedele presents two of ‘em this year. There’s the classic Flourless Chocolate Log Cake ($78) that’s been a festive staple for every one the brand’s 29 years, crafted with the finest European butter, and gluten-free to boot.
On the same hug-in-a-dessert note, there’s the Spiced Apple Noel Log Cake ($82) , which we loved for its cinnamon-spiced apple filling, and brown butter chocolate ganache.
Another new item to add to your Christmas cart at Cedele is their Noel Tiramisu Tart , available in a set of four minis ($31.20) , or a 7-inch cake ($90) .
Their take on the Italian dessert sees a buttery tart shell filled with an utterly decadent, brandy-infused chocolate custard. For legit tiramisu vibes, this is piped over with mascarpone cream, before the tart is dusted in cocoa powder and cinnamon.
Whether you’re ordering the annual panettone for your fam or gifting, you’ll be happy to know that this year’s new creation is a Spiced Carrot Walnut Panettone ($48) , which reimagines Cedele’s signature Carrot Walnut Cake as the Italian sweet bread.
Yes, there is actual carrot baked into this panettone, as well as walnuts and chocolate chips, jazzed up with cinnamon, and dusted with a cinnamon streusel that had us coming back for seconds and thirds.
Otherwise, the classic Orange Jaffa Panettone is also available, both as a set of six minis ($25) , or a large 900g ($48) version.
For little treats to go along with those post-feasting cups of steaming hot tea, stock up your pantry with some cookies such as the new Assorted Christmas Cookies ($40) ━a tin of Almond Oat Long Black Cookies, alongside the brand new Cinnamon Nut Crunch, and Earl Grey Chocolate Chip flavours.
Alternatively, another new set is the Assorted Tea Cookies ($41) , with nine pieces each of Earl Grey Chocolate Chip, Classic Hojicha, and all-new Matcha Almond Shortbread.
Otherwise, the Assorted Espresso Cookies ($40) are their coffee-accented counterparts, with Almond Oat Long Black, Taro Latte Marble Shortbread, and Salted Walnut Espresso variants.
Here’s the best part: you can get two tins of these, or any of Cedele’s other Christmas cookies, at $75 , or four tins for $148 , which works out to be $37 a tin !

11.11 is easily one of the best times to snag the best travel deals in Singapore. The Skyscanner 11.11 Sale 2026 offers massive savings of up to 40% off flights . Running from 11am on 1 Nov to 11pm on 11 Nov 2026 , this limited-time Singles’ Day event brings together the best airline markdowns so you can lock in your next getaway for a fraction of the usual price.
Whether you’re eyeing a quick getaway or planning for 2027, here is an insider’s guide to navigating the sale to find the absolute best fares.
Credit – Skyscanner
Insider highlights: Skyscanner 11.11 Sale 2026 best fares
Skyscanner showed us their biggest price drops for the Skyscanner 11.11 Sale 2026.
• Seoul, South Korea: Save up to 32% on return flights for travel from 12 to 19 Nov 2026 , with prices starting from S$417
• Taipei, Taiwan: Save up to 37% on return flights for travel from 22 to 26 Jan 2027 , with prices starting from S$258
• Shanghai, China: Save up to 37% on return flights for travel from 7 to 12 Jan 2027 , with prices starting from S$258
Note, these offers apply exclusively to return flights departing directly from Singapore.
Participating airlines & exclusive savings
Credit – Skyscanner
Have a favourite airline? Skyscanner has partnered with major regional and international carriers to offer exclusive discounts of up to 15% off :
• Exclusive Partner Deals (up to 15% Off): Trinity Airways, Jin Air, Jeju Air and Cathay Pacific
• Featured Promotional Offers: Vietnam Airlines, Sun Phuquoc Airways, Jetstar Airways and more
How to spot & book the best deals
Sometimes, I get overwhelmed by the maze of options and shifting prices, and end up booking tickets that may not be the cheapest. On Skyscanner, you can get the best price in just 3 steps.
• Search Your Trip: Input your departure city (Singapore only), desired destination and travel dates
• Select Your Flights: Choose your preferred outbound and return flight times
• Look for the “On Sale” Tag: When selecting a provider or airline to book with, look out for the blue “On Sale” These flights are part of the Skyscanner 11.11 Sale 2026.
The secret weapon: Skyscanner’s app-exclusive drops
If you want to catch the biggest bargains during the Skyscanner 11.11 Sale 2026, download the Skyscanner mobile app to access DROPS . DROPS does all the hunting for you by constantly monitoring flight fares, then delivering them to you in an hourly feed.
To grab these limited-time deals before seats sell out, visit Skyscanner’s 11.11 Hub or check the app to explore DROPS today.

deals.body:
Beachgoers, ice cream lovers, and fitness enthusiasts have a common place to gather from now until 31 January 2027 . HIIT The Beach at Sentosa invites you to Move, Play, and Chill at a beachside playground .
Credit: Sentosa
And no, “HIIT” does not mean “High-Intensity Interval Training” here. Instead, it means “ High Intensity Ice Cream Training ”. This collaboration between The Magnum Ice Cream Company and Sentosa brings a playful experience that combines exercise , fun challenges, and sweet treats.
Credit: Sentosa
Located at Palawan Beach and open daily from 8am to 10pm is a fitness circuit unlike any other. You will find 8 interactive zones inspired by beloved ice cream brands like Magnum , Ben & Jerry’s , Wall’s , and Cornetto .
Credit: Sentosa
These include Cornetto Classic Climb , Ben & Jerry’s Pint Jumps (Burpee and Box Jump), Magnum BonBon Pusher , and more. Choose a pace, make your way through the course with family and friends, and have a full workout all the way to the finish line!
Credit: Sentosa
Once you’re done sweating it out, head down to the Cooldown Isle for a chill ice cream break you very much deserve. There is also limited-edition merchandise available for purchase here, along with big ice cream installations to take photos with.
If you’re looking for a free weekend activity with family and friends, or the coolest way to work out , consider heading to Sentosa to HIIT The Beach! For more activities and things to do this month, check out our latest monthly listicle here .
HIIT The Beach
Facebook | Instagram | TikTok | Website
Palawan Beach, Sentosa, Singapore 098233
8am–10pm (Daily)
Now till 31 January 2027
For more lifestyle updates like this, subscribe to our Telegram channel at @confirmgood .

Once you’re done sweating it out, head down to the Cooldown Isle for a chill ice cream break you very much deserve. There is also limited-edition merchandise available for purchase here, along with big ice cream installations to take photos with.
If you’re looking for a free weekend activity with family and friends, or the coolest way to work out , consider heading to Sentosa to HIIT The Beach! For more activities and things to do this month, check out our latest monthly listicle here .

Matchaya is taking 30 per cent off its Cloud Series kakigori at the Tiong Bahru flagship until 22 November 2026. The five bowls are exclusive to 82 Tiong Poh Road, #01-05 , and the Tiong Bahru menu prices them from S$18++ to S$22++ before the discount.
The line is part of Matchaya 3.0, under the name The Cloud Series. The ice is made by Kuramoto Ice in Kanazawa, Japan, and sourced through Kuramoto Ice Singapore, a family trade the brand traces to 1923. Each bowl is shaved into layers of sauce, cream and texture on that ice.
Five flavours on the Cloud Series
Five bowls sit on the kakigori menu, all marked as a Tiong Bahru exclusive:
• Signature Koicha Azuki: S$22++. Ceremonial matcha with azuki, red kidney beans, house-made granola and a delicate milk cream espuma.
• Burnt Butter Houjicha: S$18++. Roasted houjicha with brown butter cream, brown sugar jelly and a spiced Biscoff crumble.
• Chocolate Tiramisu: S$18++. Rich chocolate, ladyfingers and mascarpone cream with cacao chips, served alongside a double shot of espresso.
• Mango Coconut: S$20++. Mango compote and coconut cream espuma, with dried coconut and mango popping boba.
• Strawberry Yogurt: S$20++. Strawberry compote and fresh strawberries, with a tangy yogurt espuma and berry crisps.
Menu prices are subject to a 10 per cent service charge and GST. Matchaya’s homepage lists kakigori at 30 per cent off until 22 November. It does not set out further terms, so check in store before ordering.
How the bowls are built
Signature Koicha Azuki stacks koicha sauce with azuki paste and homemade matcha granola, then a Hokkaido milk espuma finished with koicha powder and red kidney beans.
Matchaya’s layer diagram for Signature Koicha Azuki. Image: Matchaya
Burnt Butter Houjicha holds houjicha sauce, brown sugar jelly and Biscoff crumble under a brown butter cream and a Hokkaido milk espuma. Chocolate Tiramisu uses a 73 per cent dark chocolate sauce with chocolate chips, ladyfingers and mascarpone cheese, and comes with a double shot of espresso on the side.
Matchaya’s layer diagram for Chocolate Tiramisu. Image: Matchaya
Strawberry Yogurt builds homemade strawberry sauce, strawberry compote, freeze-dried strawberry crumble and strawberry konjac balls under a yogurt espuma with lemon zest. Mango Coconut pairs mango sauce and mango compote with toasted coconut flakes and mango popping boba, then a coconut espuma with lemon zest and diced mango.
Matchaya’s layer diagram for Burnt Butter Houjicha. Image: Matchaya
Only at the Tiong Bahru flagship
The Tiong Bahru tea bar opens daily from 9.30am to 9.30pm. Havelock MRT is 7 minutes away, Outram 9 minutes and Tiong Bahru 13 minutes.
Matchaya’s menu marks the kakigori as a Tiong Bahru exclusive, and notes that the bowls are best enjoyed immediately.

Readers living in Punggol , especially Northshore, rejoice! FoodHub in Northshore Plaza I opened its doors on 6 Nov 2026 . The food court is located at #01-08/18 , directly opposite Koi and beside Giant. With 14 stalls under 1 fully air-conditioned roof, the residents get more food options.
To celebrate its opening, diners can get 80c Kopi O or Teh O for just 80 cents . There will also be budget meals such as traditional breakfasts for S$2.50. In this economy? Yes please.
Those residing nearby may know that there are many vacant stalls around Northshore Plaza, but the mall seems to be undergoing a revival with new food stalls. One of those is Hippopotato , which opened in Oct 2026. This new FoodHub is an addition to the food scene — the mall previously only had 1 food court — Bagus by Kopitiam.
Do note that some of the stalls were not operating when I visited on the morning of 6 Nov 2026, but they are expected to open within the next few days. Without further ado, here are the stalls available and some dishes you can savour.
Let’s start off on the left side of FoodHub. First, you’ll be greeted by a chain brand — Yuen Kee Dumpling . They serve dumplings and wantons with fillings such as pork and tobiko . There’s also Thai Tze Char , which sells Chicken Wing Rice (S$3) .
If you’re like me and can’t eat a meal without a drink, head to the Beverages & Desserts stall . Drinks , including Iced Calamansi start from S$2.10 . The Chicken Rice stall right beside the Beverages & Desserts stall offers Roasted / Steamed Chicken Rice at S$4.50 .
For those who love noodles, Wen Ji Noodle sells a variety of noodles starting from S$3 . You can’t go wrong with their signature Dry / Soup Fishball Noodle (S$5.60) . If you prefer duck over chicken, make a beeline for Taste Legend Charcoal Roasted Delights , with dishes such as Boneless Duck Rice (S$4) and Boneless Duck Noodles (S$5.50) .
Veggie lovers can try out Yuan Yang Spinach Soup , offering Spinach Sliced Food Porridge (S$6.50) and Spinach Seafood Soup (S$5.50) amongst others. You’ll be sure to have a warm, comforting meal at Ling Nan Claypot , where prices start at S$5.80 .
Get your mala fix at Wonderful Mala Hotpot ; ingredients are priced at S$2.28/100g — affordable in my opinion. Do note that there’s a minimum order value of S$7. Ruchulu declares itself the House of Flavours for South and North Indian food as well as Indo-Chinese delights.
For those who love Korean and Japanese cuisine, there’s a fusion stall you won’t want to miss. Choose from their range of bentos, curry rice and noodles . There’s even Fat Beef Sukiyaki (S$8.80) . Abang Gemuk sells mouth-watering burgers, Western grill, pasta, rice and finger foods starting at S$3.
844 Prawn Noodle has Sliced Pork Bee Hoon Soup for S$3 , while its prawn dishes start at S$6. It’s not a food court without the shiny caifan stall; the Mixed Vege stall sells a combination of 2Veg 1Meat for just S$3 .
10 best hawker stalls at the all-new One Punggol Hawker Centre you need to know about
