Bagel Chef is a new bakery at Sengkang Grand Mall
Image credit: Besharps via Google Maps
The bagel trend may have died down a little, but they’re still a pretty solid and IG-worthy treat from time to time. In the sea of good bagel spots , we’ve found another bakery that whips up the cult-favourite baked good. Bagel Chef has recently opened in Sengkang Grand Mall , giving bagel enthusiasts another spot to add to their rotation.
17 Best Sengkang Food Places For Cheap Korean Food, Popular Min Jiang Kueh And More
Image credit: SiDing Wang via Google Maps
The bakery currently offers an extensive selection of bagels, with over 20 flavours to choose from. Their Light & Wholesome range features the Plain Bagel for just $2 , alongside the Chia Protein Bagel ($2.80) and All-in-Nut Bagel ($3.80) for a healthier, guilt-free snack.
Image credit: Qing_ via Google Maps
What caught my eye is their Loaded Bagel series. As the name suggests, these are hefty bagels that are sure to fill your belly. Four flavours are up for grabs, including the must-try Pistachio Loaded Bagel ($9.80) , stuffed with pistachio cream, and the Blueberry Loaded Bagel ($8.80) for a fruity option. Matcha lovers can go for the Double Matcha Panna Cotta Bagel ($9.90) that’s filled with two kinds of matcha cream.
Image credit: Balyn Lim via Google Maps
There’s also the Rich Sweet line-up for those with a sweet tooth. Satisfy your cravings with their Milky Strawberry Bagel ($3.70) , which looks like a strawberry Pocky in bagel form. Caffeine junkies can opt for the Caramel Mocha Bagel ($4.20) or the Earl Grey Crunch Bagel ($4.80) . For something that’s not too sweet, the Sea Salt Lemon Bagel ($3.90) is worth a shot.
Locally inspired bagels are also available, such as the Pandan Coconut Crunch ($4.20) , Taro Mochi Floss ($3.90) , and Chestnut Pumpkin Bagel ($3.90) .
Image credit: jiaojiao song via Google Maps
Folks who like sweet and salty combos can go for the Raw Choco Butter ($4.20) , starring a thicc slab of butter atop a chocolate spread. If sweet bagels aren’t your thing, go for their savoury bagels instead, ranging from Seaweed Pork Floss ($4.20) to Bacon Kimchi ($4.20) for a heartier treat.
Image credit: jiaojiao song via Google Maps
Planning a potluck or party for the festive season? Consider picking up a Gift Box (price TBD) , a long box that fits around 10 bagels per box, perfect for sharing with the fam or gifting a bagel lover multiple flavours in one go.
Image credit: 博雅 via Google Maps
Their other bakes, such as toasts and buns, look just as interesting. Standouts include the Black Gold Pork Floss Toast ($8.60) , Hokkaido Pistachio Toast ($8.60) , and the Buttery Soft Bun ($3.20) . They also have the Buttery Sea Salt Roll , AKA shio pan, for $2 .
Image credit: SiDing Wang via Google Maps
Bagel Chef also offers a rotation of flavours that aren’t featured on the menu, such as Black Pepper Potato Sausage ($3.90) , Lemon Tea ($3.50) , and even Chocolate Cheese ($3.90) , so we recommend dropping by to see what’s on offer that day.
Bagel Chef is a five-minute walk away from Buangkok MRT Station .
Speaking of shio pan, check out our comprehensive ranked list of the best shio pan in Singapore . Alternatively, head to 365 Bakery in Johor Bahru for Swiss roll blind boxes and more bakes across the border.
Address: 70 Compassvale Bow, #01-73, Sengkang Grand Mall, Singapore 544692
Opening hours: Daily 10:30am to 9pm
Website
Bagel Chef is not halal-certified.
This Popular JB Bakery Has Swiss Roll Blind Boxes, Shio Pan And More: Worth The Hype?
Feature image adapted from 博雅/jiaojiao song and Qing_ via Google Maps.

deals.body:
BK Eating House is a 24-hour coffeeshop in AMK
Image credit: Stall.sg
Ang Mo Kio is no stranger to iconic hawker stalls; after all, it’s home to the famed Lao San Kway Chap , Dongsheng Cafe , and a slew of under-HDB coffeeshops. Adding to the mix is BK Eating House , which has recently opened a new coffeeshop at Ang Mo Kio Block 226F , offering a variety of affordable hawker eats. Better yet, it’s open 24 hours, so you can get your fill anytime.
Image credit: Kwong Fei Yee via Google Maps
The most enticing deal is from Hua Dee Hong Kong Style Roasted Delight , which is selling their plates of Soy Sauce Chicken Rice for just $1 as part of their opening promotions. Their soy sauce chicken is said to be succulent and tender, with a prominent soy sauce aroma. The rice is also said to be fragrant, savoury, and glossy. Their Char Siew Rice ($4) is another crowd-pleaser, with char siew that hits the sweet spot between fat and meat, and a satisfying smoky, charred finish.
Image credit: Heng Long Teochew Porridge via Google Maps
Heng Long Teochew Porridge is another popular stall here, serving up a plethora of side dishes alongside their signature Teochew porridge. Unlike Cantonese porridge, AKA congee, which is thick and creamy, Teochew porridge is thinner and more watery, designed to be eaten alongside stronger-flavoured side dishes.
As part of its opening promotions, you can select your preferred fish, steamed Hong Kong-style and drenched in a savoury soy-based sauce, for just $9.90 . Round it out with other side dishes, such as the Stewed Duck : tender duck slices simmered in a rich dark soy sauce base.
Image credit: Stall.sg
There’s also $6 Western , with menu items priced at $6 or less—a steal, considering Western food often goes up to $10 or more. Their Chicken Chop with Fries ($6) is a safe bet, comprising juicy, chargrilled chicken chop served alongside crispy shoestring fries, coleslaw, hamburger bun, and gravy. Their Chicken Cutlet with Pasta ($6) is also highly raved about: crispy, deep-fried chicken cutlet on a bed of pasta tossed in a tomato-based sauce, topped with a sunny-side-up egg.
Image credit: Jessie via Google Maps
If you can stomach innards, try Jalan Besar Pig’s Organ Soup ’s Pig’s Organ Soup (from $4.80) . Choose your preferred ingredients from a selection of pork slices, pork liver, meatballs, pork kidney, tofu and more. The whole medley is simmered in pork bone broth that’s best eaten with rice.
BK Eating House is located a 20-minute walk from Ang Mo Kio MRT Station .
For more eats in the area, read our Ang Mo Kio 628 Food Centre food guide . Otherwise, check out our review of Shared Table , a new garden cafe located at Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, located just a 14-minute walk away.

Opening hours: Daily 24 hours

The platter usually costs $18, so $1++ works out to about $1.20 nett after the 10% service charge and 9% GST. Peach Garden says there is no minimum spend and no limit on how many platters a qualifying table can order, it is dine-in only, and all six outlets are in: all day at Chinatown Point, Changi Airport T2 and The Heeren, lunch hours only at The Metropolis, OCBC Centre and Thomson Plaza. No end date is published and terms and conditions apply, so treat it like the launch discount before it and go early.

Sagye Lite, the casual sister of Orchard Korean pot rice restaurant Sagye, holds its grand opening at VivoCity on Wednesday 25 November with 1-for-1 sotbap for six days, to 30 November. The outlet is already in soft opening, so the doors are open now; the deal is what starts on Wednesday.
Spicy chicken with cheese sotbap at Sagye, Wheelock Place. Photo: Sagye
Sotbap is Korean rice cooked and served in its own pot, with the topping laid over the rice. At Sagye on Wheelock Place it is the centre of the menu, alongside stews and dishes to share. Sagye Lite keeps the pots and brings the prices down for everyday dining.
How the 1-for-1 works
Buy any eligible sotbap and a second eligible pot of equal or lower value is free. It is dine-in only and walk-in only, with no advance reservations for the promotion. A redemption is secured only when the order is placed in the restaurant, first come, first served.
• Lunch: 11am to 3pm, 150 redemptions
• Dinner: 5pm to 10pm, 150 redemptions
• Excluded: Signature Beef Short Rib and the F1 Japanese Wagyu Striploin sotbap
• Dates: 25 to 30 November 2026, while redemptions last
Because the free pot has to cost the same or less, two people ordering pots at the same price get the full value. Pair a cheaper pot with a dearer one and the free half of the deal is the cheaper one.
What the pots cost
Two pot prices have been shared ahead of the opening:
• Grilled Chicken Pot Rice: S$12.90
• Grilled Pork Belly Pot Rice: S$13.90
Under the 1-for-1, a grilled chicken pot paired with a grilled pork belly pot comes to S$13.90 for two. Rose yupdduk, rice cakes in a creamy rose sauce, is on the VivoCity menu too.
Inside Sagye Lite at VivoCity. Image: Sagye Lite / Instagram
Sagye at Wheelock Place
Sagye at Wheelock Place, 501 Orchard Road #02-19, serves beef short rib, scallop and dongpo rou sotbap, alongside Japanese Wagyu ribeye and army stew. It also takes walk-ins only and opens for lunch from 11am to 3pm and dinner from 5pm to 10pm daily. If the VivoCity queue is long on the first weekend, Orchard is another way to get sotbap from the same brand, at full menu prices and with no promotion. Sagye Lite also runs an outlet at Westgate.
Dongpo rou sotbap from the Wheelock Place menu. Photo: Sagye
Sagye Lite details
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #01-167/168, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Nearest MRT: HarbourFront (NE1/CC29)
Grand opening deal: 1-for-1 sotbap, 25 to 30 November 2026, dine-in only
Promotion sessions: 11am to 3pm and 5pm to 10pm
Reservations: walk-in only for the promotion
Instagram: @sagyelite_sg

members.body:
Sagye Lite to open at VivoCity on 25 November
Good news for sotbap fans: Sagye Lite is officially opening at VivoCity on 25 November 2026 ! To celebrate, the restaurant is giving out 1-for-1 sotbap , AKA Korean pot rice, for six days only.
Image credit: Sagye VivoCity via Google Maps
Sagye Lite is a more casual, affordable spin-off of the original Sagye, which served Korean pot rice and barbecue. At Sagye’s now-closed outlet in Tanjong Pagar, their sotbap was only served at lunch, with dinner focused on Korean barbecue, so Sagye Lite puts the pot rice front and centre instead.
The prices show the budget-friendly angle too. At Sagye Lite, you can get the Grilled Chicken Pot Rice ($12.90++) and the Grilled Pork Belly Pot Rice ($13.90++) . If you want something heartier, there’s also the Beef Bulgogi Pot Rice ($18.90++) .
You can also get their viral Rose Yupdduk (price TBD) at VivoCity, which is a good chance to order it alongside your sotbap. If you want more to share, consider ordering their Korean side dishes, including Bossam ($8.90++) , Korean Pancakes (from $12.90++) , Korean fried chicken (from $14.90++) , and Rose tteokbokki ($18.90++) .
To enjoy the 1-for-1 promo, simply buy any eligible sotbap, and you’ll get a second eligible sotbap of equal or lower value free. The 1-for-1 promo runs from 25 to 30 November 2026 , with two redemption sessions every day.
A few tips before heading down: up to 300 complimentary sotbap redemptions are available daily across lunch and dinner sessions, so it’s worth going early if you can. There are also no advance reservations required for the promotion, and your redemption is only secured when you place your order in the store, so you’ll need to be there in person.
In more food news, read our Yee3 feature on the viral Chinese coconut drink brand that has opened at ION Orchard, and our Age.3 feature on the Ginza-famous fried sando brand with 35 flavours from $4.80.
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #01-167-168, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 10pm
Website
Sagye Lite is not halal-certified.

deals.body:
Ang Mo Kio residents can rejoice as neighbourhood coffeeshop S-11 AMK 530 Food House has finally reopened following renovations. The refreshed kopitiam welcomes back several beloved hawker stalls alongside a fresh look for diners.
Credit – Piow Piow via Google Maps
To celebrate the relaunch, 178 Fish Head Steamboat is offering an opening promotion that regulars will not want to miss. Diners can enjoy their XO Fish Head Steamboat at S$23 instead of its usual price of S$33 . This limited-time deal makes it an ideal spot for hearty family dinners without breaking the bank.
Credit – William Lai & Jia Her Yong via Google Reviews
For herbal soup enthusiasts, Ju Xiang Bak Kut Teh has also returned to serve warming claypot dishes. It’s helmed by a chef hailing from Klang, Malaysia, so you know you’re getting the real deal.
You can order their Klang Signature Claypot Bak Kut Teh (S$8.60/16.80/32.20) which is intensely herbal and nourishing. If you’re in the mood for more addictively tangy and savoury flavours, order their Claypot Vinegar Pork Trotter (S$7.50) instead.
Supper lovers will be glad to see Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Porridge back in action at the coffee shop. The famous brand serves comforting bowls of its signature Frog Porridge (S$11/22/33) alongside smokey claypot goodies like Ginger Spring Onion Frog (S$11/22/33) .
Credit – Winston Ho & Soh Wee Kian via Google Reviews
Returning favourite Jin Long Wu Xiang Prawn Cracker is also back with crispy fried goodies starting from S$1.40 . Swing by for crunchy ngoh hiang and savoury sausages paired with a classic side of bee hoon .
Meanwhile, Auntie Jessie Rojak rounds up the line-up with plates of Traditional Rojak (S$5/7/9) and my personal favourite, Fruit Rojak ( S$5/7/9) , made with a generous heap of chopped cucumber, onions and pineapple dressed in a sticky-sweet sauce.
With its upgraded seating and strong line-up of stalls, this revamped coffee shop is ready for all-day dining. Head down soon to catch the XO Fish Head Steamboat (S$23) promotion while it lasts!

Returning favourite Jin Long Wu Xiang Prawn Cracker is also back with crispy fried goodies starting from S$1.40 . Swing by for crunchy ngoh hiang and savoury sausages paired with a classic side of bee hoon .

MODU, the samgyetang specialist from Mandarin Gallery and Amoy Street, opens its third Singapore outlet at Raffles City tomorrow, Thursday 19 November, and two of its soups will be sold nowhere else.
The new bowls are a Curry Laksa Samgyetang at S$40 and a Mugwort Samgyetang at S$37. The laksa one is MODU’s Singapore debut flavour, with the chicken in a rich coconut broth built on Southeast Asian spices. The same broth also comes as Curry Laksa Kalguksu, with handmade noodles, for S$34.
Curry Laksa Samgyetang, S$40, only at MODU Raffles City. Image: MODU
What is new at Raffles City
The Mugwort Samgyetang uses fresh Korean mugwort, or ssuk, in a light broth with a herbal edge. It is the gentler of the two Raffles City exclusives, and the one to pick if a laksa-flavoured ginseng chicken sounds like one idea too many.
Mugwort Samgyetang, S$37, another Raffles City exclusive. Image: MODU
Raffles City will serve 12 samgyetang. Classic Herbal is the cheapest at S$35. Perilla Seed is S$38, Black Garlic and Wild Mushroom are S$42, Truffle is S$46, and the Black Chicken and Premium Seafood bowl, with abalone and octopus, tops the menu at S$52. Every samgyetang there comes with unlimited herbal soup. If you order the Scorched Rice version at S$40, allow 20 to 30 minutes for it.
Classic Herbal Samgyetang, the cheapest bowl on the Raffles City menu at S$35. Image: MODU
Raffles City will serve organic chicken by the half, while Mandarin Gallery and Amoy Street use organic spring chicken. MODU says its chicken comes from halal-certified suppliers and every dish is pork-free and lard-free.
The grilled eel offer
Until 18 December, every two samgyetang ordered at Raffles City come with one Grilled Eel free. The eel is a S$34 sharing plate on the regular menu, served with two house sauces. The campaign is pitched at bringing your parents along, though that part is encouraged rather than required.
Order two samgyetang at Raffles City and the Grilled Eel is free until 18 December. Image: MODU
To claim it, show staff MODU’s campaign post on its @modu.singapore Instagram account when you order. The offer is dine-in only and valid at Raffles City only.
For two people, the 2-Gather Set at S$98 covers tea, an appetiser, two samgyetang, a sharing plate and dessert. Curry Laksa adds S$2 to the set and Truffle adds S$8.
Getting there
MODU Raffles City is at 252 North Bridge Road, #B1-06/07 Raffles City, Singapore 179103, in the basement of the mall at City Hall. From tomorrow it opens daily from 11am to 10pm. It is walk-in first, and groups can WhatsApp the outlet on 8087 0757. All prices are before the 10 per cent service charge and GST.

89 Carrot Cake sells handmade carrot cake in MacPherson
Image credit: MarilynC via Google Maps
Every time my friends and I discuss what to get for breakfast, the same few local dishes always pop up: kaya toast , economic bee hoon , and dim sum . However, I am a firm believer that fried carrot cake is the underrated GOAT of local breakfast dishes, and 89 Carrot Cake in Macpherson is one of the best. They even accept CDC vouchers , which is good news if you’re still looking for ways to spend them.
Which Is The Best Kaya Toast Franchise In SG? We Rank Ya Kun, Toast Box And More
Image credit: Hao Jun Chua via Google Maps
89 Carrot Cake was founded over 60 years ago by Uncle Zhang, who started off selling soon kueh and radish cake. Since his retirement in 2024, his daughter, a former childcare teacher, has taken up the mantle to continue his legacy with the same 60-year-old recipe.
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
What makes their dish stand out is that they make the radish cake fresh daily, lending a softer, smoother texture compared to store-bought variants, which tend to be denser and more starchy. It’s also said to have a subtle sweetness of radishes, with carrot chunks interlaced within the cake adding textural contrast.
Image credit: Chuan YEO via Google Maps
In the debate over whether black or white carrot cake is better, I’m on the latter team, and 89 Carrot Cake does their White Carrot Cake ($4) well. It’s said to be super garlicky and savoury, with a slight kick from the chilli paste. The scrambled eggs complement the soft, fluffy texture of the radish cakes, while the wok hei ties it all together.
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
For all Black Carrot Cake ($5) fans, theirs is equally good too. It features the same shebang of ingredients tossed in a sweet-savoury dark soy sauce that helps mellow out the chilli’s spice.
According to online reviews, wait times can stretch up to 20 minutes, so factor that in before you head down.
89 Carrot Cake is located at MacPherson Market & Food Centre , a nine-minute walk from Mattar MRT Station and a 14-minute walk from MacPherson MRT Station .
If you’re on a hunt for more hawker eats, check out our Three Bowls feature : a hawker stall run by an ex-Din Tai Fung chef selling kolo mee from only $4. Otherwise, read our Tampines hawker food guide for another hawker centre worth visiting on the Downtown Line.
Address: 89 Circuit Road, #01-102, MacPherson Market & Food Centre, Singapore 370089
Opening hours: Wed-Sun 6am to 11am
89 Carrot Cake is not halal-certified.

Sol & Manta is an aquarium-themed cafe in Joo Chiat
Image credit: Jay via Google Maps
I’ve always been fascinated by the sea, so dining at the aquarium restaurant in Sentosa has been on my wishlist for years. Unfortunately, it was always out of my budget, so I was happy to hear that Sol & Manta , Singapore’s first interactive aquarium-themed cafe, has just opened on Joo Chiat Road. Here, you can dine with marine animals for the price of a coffee.
Image credit: Lim Jaspar via Google Maps
Step into the cafe and you’ll notice large saltwater coral reef tanks that wrap around the dining area, along with floor projections that send “waves” rolling beneath your feet. The fun doesn’t stop there, because between bites, you can feed the goldfish or marine fish for $5 , or even pet a starfish.
Image credit: Mild Waranya via Google Maps
The food menu is more extensive than one might expect. For mains, highlights include the Charred Octopus ($37) , Duroc Porchetta ($33) , and Katsu Curry Don ($24) , while the pasta list features Uni Pasta ($32) , Cold Truffle Capellini ($27) , and Vongole ($25) , amongst others.
If you’re there for brunch, consider getting the Smashed Avocado Toast ($27) or Sol Garden Salad ($16) for something light. There’s also a kids’ menu with Spaghetti Bolognese ($14) and Fish & Chips ($16) , so it works for a family outing too.
The cafe offers a coffee menu too. We recommend the Ocean Dream ($10) , an espresso paired with coconut water, topped with a blue curacao cloud and coconut flakes to match the ocean theme. If you prefer the classics, get an Americano (from $6) or Latte (from $6.50) instead . Flavoured lattes are also available, including Hazelnut , Vanilla , Caramel and more.
Image credit: Mild Waranya via Google Maps
Matcha lovers will be spoilt for choice with Sol & Manta’s matcha-based signature drinks, which include the Violet Sea Cloud ($10) and Emerald Wave ($10) . The former comes with an ube cloud, while the latter features pistachio cloud foam and crushed pistachio
Image credit: Jay via Google Maps
Order some desserts to go with your drinks. A crowd favourite is the Chef Classic Tiramisu ($14) , along with the addictive Banana Fritters ($12) . Ice cream fans can go for a single scoop of Kapiti Ice Cream ($6) .
Sol & Manta is a 15-minute walk from Paya Lebar MRT Station .
For more cafes to visit, read our Bagel Chef feature on the new Sengkang bakery with over 20 bagel flavours from $2, or check out our list of CDC-friendly cafes , including a late-night gelato spot and more!
Address: 91 Joo Chiat Road, Singapore 427385
Opening hours: Tue-Fri 12pm to 9:30pm, Sat-Sun 10am to 9:30pm
Tel: 9191 5516
Website
Sol & Manta is not halal-certified.

deals.body:
Most of us grew up eating local fare. Over the years, we’ve grown so accustomed to the default ingredients that make up each dish that hanging one or two elements might seem like a mortal sin to purists. Take for example, nasi lemak , which is always paired with an open-faced omelette and chicken wings. So, when I found out through Google Reviews that Warmhouse Nasi Lemak at Chinatown Complex makes a couple of tweaks to this classic dish, curiosity got the better of me, and I had to swing by to try it for myself.
When we arrived, the inspiration behind the word ‘warmhouse’ became apparent. A quaint ceiling lamp cast a warm orange glow over the space, making it feel as though we had stepped into the kitchen of a welcoming household, awaiting for a humble home-cooked meal to be served.
We met Kenneth, a Singaporean ex-photographer, together with his ex-makeup artist wife, Cindy, a Taiwanese from Kaohsiung. Cindy shared that Kenneth enjoys cooking and loves to eat, while she’s obsessed over nasi lemak . Together, the couple decided to experience what it’s like to be a hawker and made the decision to combine the essences of both countries into their plates of nasi lemak . It also reminds them of their daughter, who is also a blend of 2 cultures.
What to order at Warmhouse Nasi Lemak
I fondly remember my first trip to Taiwan, where my ex-interns from my previous job had brought me to a pushcart stall near their university in Kaohsiung. An elderly uncle sold an assortment of deep-fried goodies, and that was where I first discovered my love for salt and pepper fried snacks. One bite, and I was hooked!
Thus, I was excited when we started off with the Set B Taiwanese Salt & Pepper Popcorn Chicken Nasi Lemak (S$5.50) — yes, I know, what a mouthful. I must say, for S$5.50 , to have at least 8 to 9 pieces of popcorn chicken was more than worth the price. They were accompanied by the usual peanut-anchovies combo, a fried onsen egg, sambal , and sliced Japanese cucumbers.
If you’re wondering whether this is the usual supermarket-bought frozen chicken nonsense, think again. Kenneth painstakingly marinates, breads, and deep-fries fresh chicken from scratch. As my molars sank into each crispy morsel, I was greeted by an almost-scalding gush of natural juices, accompanied by fragrant breading seasoned with salt, pepper, and five-spice powder, plus crispy fried basil leaves. Man, was it shiok !
Instead of the usual omelette or fried sunny-side up, the couple serves the dish with a lightly-fried whole ramen egg. I mean, who on earth would have thought that a flowy ramen egg would go so impeccably well with nasi lemak ? Soft, oozy, and melt-in-the-mouth — it was the perfect pairing. Cindy said the reason why they use ajitama eggs was because she dislikes how hard an omelette can get especially when it becomes cold.
The house-made sambal deserves a shout-out, too. Beyond its sweetness, it had a gritty texture and strong notes of sauteed onions and dried shrimp that gave it plenty of character. Mix copious amounts into the rice and thank me later!
Speaking of which, the rice wasn’t forgettable either, boasting a fluffy texture and rich coconut fragrance. I’m rarely blown away by every single component of a dish, but this was one of those rare occasions when everything just clicked with my palate.
We then moved on to the Set A Warmhouse Nasi Lemak (S$5) , which looked more like the default presentation that you see at almost every kopitiam or hawker centre stall. It came with a fried chicken wing, luncheon meat, and the same partners in crime as the previous dish.
The chicken wing was executed well, crispy and still maintained its juiciness. It also was seasoned properly — both skin and flesh — something that many other establishments fail to do. I’m rather icky whenever the skin and outer layer is flavourful, but the meat turns out bland and boring. It just goes to show that many of them didn’t marinate it long enough for the seasoning to penetrate thoroughly. As someone who drastically cut down on processed foods, that piece of luncheon meat felt like a little guilty pleasure. Simple, comforting, and thoroughly satisfying, it tasted like my childhood.
Who Warmhouse Nasi Lemak is best for
It’s perfect for nasi lemak traditionalists who love their default combinations. However, I’d recommend bringing a friend or two along so you can order one each to share, giving you the opportunity to savour both the traditional and more unique fusion versions.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT and alight at either Chinatown MRT Station (NE4/DT19) or Maxwell MRT Station (TE18) . Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Maxwell Stn Exit 2 and New Bridge Ctr .
Do we recommend Warmhouse Nasi Lemak?
…

So, when I found out through Google Reviews that Warmhouse Nasi Lemak at Chinatown Complex makes a couple of tweaks to this classic dish, curiosity got the better of me, and I had to swing by to try it for myself.
When we arrived, the inspiration behind the word ‘warmhouse’ became apparent. A quaint ceiling lamp cast a warm orange glow over the space, making it feel as though we had stepped into the kitchen of a welcoming household, awaiting for a humble home-cooked meal to be served.
We met Kenneth, a Singaporean ex-photographer, together with his ex-makeup artist wife, Cindy, a Taiwanese from Kaohsiung. Cindy shared that Kenneth enjoys cooking and loves to eat, while she’s obsessed over nasi lemak . Together, the couple decided to experience what it’s like to be a hawker and made the decision to combine the essences of both countries into their plates of nasi lemak . It also reminds them of their daughter, who is also a blend of 2 cultures.
What to order at Warmhouse Nasi Lemak
I fondly remember my first trip to Taiwan, where my ex-interns from my previous job had brought me to a pushcart stall near their university in Kaohsiung. An elderly uncle sold an assortment of deep-fried goodies, and that was where I first discovered my love for salt and pepper fried snacks. One bite, and I was hooked!
Thus, I was excited when we started off with the Set B Taiwanese Salt & Pepper Popcorn Chicken Nasi Lemak (S$5.50) — yes, I know, what a mouthful. I must say, for S$5.50 , to have at least 8 to 9 pieces of popcorn chicken was more than worth the price. They were accompanied by the usual peanut-anchovies combo, a fried onsen egg, sambal , and sliced Japanese cucumbers.
If you’re wondering whether this is the usual supermarket-bought frozen chicken nonsense, think again. Kenneth painstakingly marinates, breads, and deep-fries fresh chicken from scratch. As my molars sank into each crispy morsel, I was greeted by an almost-scalding gush of natural juices, accompanied by fragrant breading seasoned with salt, pepper, and five-spice powder, plus crispy fried basil leaves. Man, was it shiok !
Instead of the usual omelette or fried sunny-side up, the couple serves the dish with a lightly-fried whole ramen egg. I mean, who on earth would have thought that a flowy ramen egg would go so impeccably well with nasi lemak ? Soft, oozy, and melt-in-the-mouth — it was the perfect pairing. Cindy said the reason why they use ajitama eggs was because she dislikes how hard an omelette can get especially when it becomes cold.
The house-made sambal deserves a shout-out, too. Beyond its sweetness, it had a gritty texture and strong notes of sauteed onions and dried shrimp that gave it plenty of character. Mix copious amounts into the rice and thank me later!
Speaking of which, the rice wasn’t forgettable either, boasting a fluffy texture and rich coconut fragrance. I’m rarely blown away by every single component of a dish, but this was one of those rare occasions when everything just clicked with my palate.
We then moved on to the Set A Warmhouse Nasi Lemak (S$5) , which looked more like the default presentation that you see at almost every kopitiam or hawker centre stall. It came with a fried chicken wing, luncheon meat, and the same partners in crime as the previous dish.
The chicken wing was executed well, crispy and still maintained its juiciness. It also was seasoned properly — both skin and flesh — something that many other establishments fail to do. I’m rather icky whenever the skin and outer layer is flavourful, but the meat turns out bland and boring. It just goes to show that many of them didn’t marinate it long enough for the seasoning to penetrate thoroughly. As someone who drastically cut down on processed foods, that piece of luncheon meat felt like a little guilty pleasure. Simple, comforting, and thoroughly satisfying, it tasted like my childhood.
Who Warmhouse Nasi Lemak is best for
It’s perfect for nasi lemak traditionalists who love their default combinations. However, I’d recommend bringing a friend or two along so you can order one each to share, giving you the opportunity to savour both the traditional and more unique fusion versions.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT and alight at either Chinatown MRT Station (NE4/DT19) or Maxwell MRT Station (TE18) . Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Maxwell Stn Exit 2 and New Bridge Ctr .
Do we recommend Warmhouse Nasi Lemak?

members.body:
BB.Q Chicken Singapore opens at VivoCity’s Food Republic
Image credit: Hiro Nonoda via Google Maps
Calling all K-drama and Stray Kids fans: the chicken Felix keeps talking about is opening near you. BB.Q Chicken , which says it’s the world’s biggest Korean fried chicken chain, is set to open a food court stall at Food Republic , VivoCity on 27 November 2026 . Two more outlets will follow over the next couple of months.
17 Korean Fried Chicken In Singapore, Including Hawker And Halal Options
The VivoCity stall is a BB.Q Chicken Express, a smaller grab-and-go version of the brand. Next, another stall will open at Food Opera, ION Orchard in December 2026 . Then a second BB.Q Chicken Express opens at Food Junction, Junction 8 in January 2027 , which is good news for Bishan folks who’d rather not trek to HarbourFront for a chicken fix.
Image credit: BB.Q Chicken
If the name sounds familiar, you may have spotted it on screen. The chain has turned up in K-dramas such as Crash Landing on You and Guardian: The Lonely and Great God , better known as Goblin , and in variety shows Running Man and Knowing Bros .
Image credit: @felix.lee.00
It started in Korea in 1995, and the name stands for “Best of the Best Quality.” Today it has about 4,500 stores across 57 countries. It even has its own training school for franchisees, Chicken University, which has been running since 1999. Stray Kids member Felix was also a fan long before he became the brand’s global ambassador.
Image credit: Raymond Fu via Google Maps
The full Singapore menu and prices haven’t been released, but two signatures are confirmed for the VivoCity launch. Soy Garlic Chicken (price TBD) comes coated in a sweet-savoury soy glaze with plenty of garlic, the go-to pick if you don’t do spice. Heat-seekers should get the Red Chak Chak Seasoning Chicken (price TBD) , coated in a spicy red pepper seasoning instead of a sauce. From the opening promos, expect combos, boneless chicken, bone-in chicken, and burgers on the menu too.
Image credit: Ivonne Rivera via Google Maps
Now for the freebies. From 3 December to 17 December 2026 , every order comes with a free two-piece boneless chicken; orders of sides alone don’t qualify. The outlet picks the flavour, so there’s no choosing.
Felix fans get their own perk from 3 December 2026 . Buy any two items from the combo, boneless chicken, or bone-in chicken categories, or the burger category, and you’ll get a sealed surprise pack with two Felix photocards and one photo strip. There are four photocard designs and two photo strip designs, so collecting the full set could take a few visits.
Can’t wait till the 27th? Read our Lotteria review for another popular Korean fast food chain that’s recently set up shop in Singapore! Otherwise, read our guide to the best 1-for-1 buffet deals for 2026 for more affordable eats.
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #03-01, Food Republic, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Opening hours: TBD
Website
BB.Q Chicken is not halal-certified.

Global Korean fried chicken brand bb.q Chicken is opening 3 outlets in Singapore , with the first outlet at VivoCity’s Food Republic on 27 November 2026 – bb.q Chicken Express, a grab-and-go concept. bb.q Chicken will continue to bring its crunch to Food Opera at ION Orchard in December 2026 and Food Junction at Junction 8 in January 2027 .
Credit: bb.q Chicken US’s Facebook
What sets bb.q Chicken apart is the way it fries. According to the brand, each piece is hand-battered and fried at a lower temperature for longer, then tossed in its signature sauces and seasoning by hand.
Singapore Menu
Credit: bb.q Chicken US’s Facebook
Expect popular flavours in the menu, ranging from Soy Garlic for a perfect balance of sweet and salty flavours to Red Chak Chak Seasoning , fried till golden and coated with a special pepper powder for a fiery kick, and other exciting favourites.
Complimentary Chicken
bb.q Chicken is celebrating their opening with a promotion, running from 3 to 17 December . Free 2-piece boneless chicken will be distributed with every order , excluding sides.
Global Ambassador
Credit: bb.q Chicken US’s Facebook
Fans of Stray Kids or Felix in particular, take home exclusive bb.q Chicken x Felix merchandise with the purchase of any 2 items from these categories : combo, boneless chicken, bone-in chicken, or burger!
Each qualifying purchase comes with 2 Felix Lucky Draw photocards and 1 Felix Lucky Photostrip – sounds like a wonderful deal, right?
Whether it’s a fried chicken night or a potluck picnic session, bb.q Chicken is fitting for any occasion. See you there on 27 November!
bb.q Chicken Singapore

deals.body:
If your idea of a good bakery haul involves squeezing your purchases rather than eating them, Squishery’s latest pop-up might be right up your alley. Making its debut at KLGCC Mall , the brand has set up a bakery-themed space filled with slow-rising squishies inspired by bread, pastries and other sweet treats.
Credit – Squishery
Running until 22 Nov 2026 , the pop-up offers a playful shopping experience where you can grab a basket and fill it with squishy versions of bagels, cookies, chocolate bars and giant waffles.
There’s even a special interactive bakery experience for those who pick between 8 and 12 squishies , where the staff take on the role of little chefs to prepare your purchases before you bring them home.
Credit – Squishery
Among the collections to look out for is the Squishy Squad , featuring a lineup of charming characters such as Capy Red Bean Cake, Butter Cat, Mini Butter Cat, Cream Hug Roll, Capy Bread, Moozy Cheese, Little Piggy, Bear Swiss Roll and Pink Bean Squishy.
Bread lovers, meanwhile, will want to browse the Moozy Bakery Series . Expect plenty of familiar bakery-inspired designs, including Grandpa Toast, Butter Croissant, Butter Pineapple Bun, Pupu Milk Butter Crisp, Giant Waffle, Moozy Lava Pineapple Bun, Toasted Marshmallow Toast and Twist Bread, alongside other designs.
Credit – Squishery
Beyond their cute appearances, these squishies are fun to play with, thanks to their soft textures and slow-rising quality. The bakery-style gift boxes also make them a charming pick for anyone who enjoys collecting novelty toys or is looking for a quirky little gift.
There’s another reason to stop by KLGCC Mall while the pop-up is around. Shoppers who spend RM100 at any mall outlet in a single receipt can redeem a Polo Bun Squishy , while stocks last.
The Squishery pop-up is located at G-02-01 , in front of Jaya Grocer Signature at KLGCC Mall. You can drop by daily from 10am to 10pm until 22 Nov 2026 , so there’s still time to pick out a few squishy treats before the bakery closes.

deals.body:
Halal Food Friday goes to a name that has fed Kampong Gelam since 1992. Hjh Maimunah is a Malay and Indonesian restaurant serving halal nasi padang, where a beef rendang set costs S$10.70 on its delivery menu, and a Premium Ambeng platter for 2 to 3 people is S$47.
It is a Muslim-owned family business, founded by Mdm Mahiran Abdul Rahman with her late mother’s recipes, and now run by the second generation. The restaurant describes all of its food as halal-certified. We will come back to how to check that yourself.
Halal status: what we could verify
Hjh Maimunah states on its official website that its Malay and Indonesian cuisine is halal-certified, and that its kitchens are halal-certified. The business is also Muslim-owned, as the founding family’s own story on the site makes clear.
Halal certification is issued outlet by outlet, so do not assume that every stall carrying the name has the same certificate. Search the MUIS HalalSG directory for the specific address before you go, especially for the smaller outlets inside food courts.
Source: Hjh Maimunah
Where to find Hjh Maimunah and when it is open
The flagship is a pair of shophouses at Jalan Pisang, a short walk from Bugis MRT (roughly 8 minutes, going by the usual estimates). Joo Chiat is the second full restaurant, and there are smaller Mini outlets across the island.
• Jalan Pisang: 11 Jalan Pisang, Singapore 199078. Open 7.30am to 7pm, Monday to Saturday, closed on Sundays. Nearest MRT: Bugis (DT14/EW12).
• Joo Chiat: 20 Joo Chiat Road, Singapore 427357. Open 8am to 7pm, Tuesday to Sunday, closed on Mondays.
• Tampines Mall: Kopitiam, #04-27-29, 4 Tampines Central 5. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• City Square Mall: Food Republic, #B3-04, 180 Kitchener Road. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• Westgate: Food Junction, #B1-29, 3 Gateway Drive. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• Hong Leong Building: #B1-45, 16 Raffles Quay. Open 10am to 3pm, Monday to Friday, handy for the CBD lunch crowd.
The restaurant lists more Mini outlets, including Clementi Mall, Compass One, Yishun and Parkway Parade, on its locations page. Hours can change, so check the page before a long trip.
What to order at this halal nasi padang
You pick your own dishes from the counter and pile them over rice, so the order is yours to build. The restaurant says its menu runs past 100 items at the main restaurants, and the Minis serve at least 40.
• Beef Rendang, the slow-cooked dry curry the restaurant counts as its signature.
• Tahu Telur, a thick fried tofu omelette topped with vegetables, crushed peanuts and prawn paste sauce.
• Lemak Siput Sedut, sea snails in a spicy coconut gravy, for the adventurous.
• Ikan Bakar, grilled fish with a traditional rempah marinade.
• Sotong Hitam, squid in a spicy ink stew.
• Sayur Lodeh, a coconut vegetable stew that cools down the sambal.
• Kueh such as ondeh-ondeh, kueh lapis and kueh dadar to finish.
Source: Hjh Maimunah
Hjh Maimunah prices
The restaurant does not publish a dine-in price list online, but its delivery menu on Oddle gives a clear idea. Dine-in prices at the counter will depend on which dishes you pick, so treat the figures below as a guide only.
• Beef Rendang Set: S$10.70
• Ayam Lemak Cili Padi Set: S$10.20
• Asam Pedas Fish Set: S$10.70
• Beef, Chicken or Fish Deluxe Set: S$12.20
• Nasi Rawon Set: S$12
• Vegetable Set: S$8
• Original Ambeng Platter (2 to 3 people): S$44
• Premium Ambeng Platter: S$47
• Family Bundle (4 pax): S$58
Bring a group if you can. The Ambeng platters are made for sharing, and splitting a S$47 platter among three people works out to about S$16 each.
Planning your visit
Jalan Pisang is small and gets busy at lunch, particularly on weekends, so go early or aim for mid-afternoon. The restaurant also takes reservations through its website, which helps if you are a bigger group.
If you are making a day of it around Kampong Gelam, the Malay Heritage Centre has free admission and is close by. For this weekend’s other plans, see our things to do guide . Meal planning for the festive season? Here is the Holiday Inn Atrium 1-for-1 buffet .
Source: Hjh Maimunah

deals.body:
1-day Orchard itinerary on a budget
Orchard has always read as somewhere bougie to me, notorious for sky-high prices and luxury-brand outlets, which is probably why my friends and I tend to steer clear. After all, we don’t really have the money to splurge on a $50 meal at ION Orchard or a lavish hotel buffet .
However, after FOMO drove me down Orchard Road to admire the extravagant festive lights, I ended up putting together a full-day Orchard budget itinerary for under $30 that proves you can actually enjoy the heart of Singapore without burning a hole in your wallet.
BTW, if you’re willing to spend a little more, check out our 12-hour Orchard food itinerary instead!
How To Spend 12 Hours In Orchard: $22.80++ Porridge Buffet, $2 Thrift Stores And More
Breakfast: THE CITY BAKERY
As someone who can’t stomach a full meal during breakfast, THE CITY BAKERY is a good place to start the day with a small bite. It’s located at Mandarin Gallery , a 10-minute walk from Orchard MRT Station , offering a wide variety of pastries, bakes, and sandwiches.
ICYMI: This cafe-bakery started as a small neighbourhood bakery in New York City, founded by an ex-television producer with two Emmy Awards to his name. They’ve since expanded to Japan, with over 40 outlets at the time of writing, and recently opened their first Southeast Asian outpost in Singapore.
The bakery’s signature, and what put them on the map, is the Pretzel Croissant ($5) : a fluffy croissant with a savoury, pretzel-like crust. Inside, it’s just what you’d expect from a regular croissant—flaky with well-defined layers.
When we visited, we particularly enjoyed the Coffee Cinnamon Roll ($5) . It’s a spin on the classic breakfast pastry, zhnged up with a hit of coffee. The fragrance of the coffee brought out the earthiness and warmth of cinnamon, tying everything together.
Read our THE CITY BAKERY coverage .
Expect to spend : $5 for bakes
Address: 333A Orchard Road, #02-05 Mandarin Gallery, Singapore 238897
Opening hours: Daily 9am to 9:30pm
Website
THE CITY BAKERY is not halal-certified.
Japan-Famous Bakery Chain From NYC Opens At Mandarin Gallery—Here’s What To Try
Lunch: Maddie’s Kitchen
Image credit: Xin Hao via Google Maps
After breakfast, take some time to window-shop and soak up the atmosphere of Orchard Road before heading over to lunch at Maddie’s Kitchen in Far East Plaza . The walk from Mandarin Gallery to Far East Plaza takes about 17 minutes, which is plenty of time to jalan jalan.
Image credit: Ah Kay via Google Maps
Maddie’s Kitchen is a no-frills eatery selling affordable zi char. While most dishes are in large portions meant to be shared ‘round the table, their Hainanese Curry Rice is an item well loved by solo diners. The Pork Chop Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) features crispy pork cutlets served on a bed of rice, paired with a sweet-spicy Hainanese-style curry, said to be made with their house-made rempah. The set also comes with a pile of braised cabbage and a sunny-side-up fried egg, dressed with dark soya sauce.
Image credit: Glen Y via Google Maps
If deep-fried foods aren’t really your thing, their Curry Chicken Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) is a decent alternative, featuring the same rice and veggies, served with curried potatoes and tender chicken instead. You can also get their Braised Pork Belly Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) , topped with melt-in-your-mouth slices of braised pork belly.
Image credit: Snoop Ee via Google Maps
Alternatively, for something lighter, try their Batang Fish Soup or Fried Fish Soup , both priced at $7.80 . Both feature a clear, clean-tasting fish broth packed generously with a medley of ingredients: your preferred fish, tomatoes, cabbage, and silken tofu. It’s a comforting, protein-packed meal for your day’s activities.
Expect to spend : $6.80-$7.80 for mains
Address: 14 Scotts Road, #02-10/11/12/13, Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 9pm
Website
Maddie’s Kitchen is not halal-certified.
20 Far East Plaza Food Gems Including Popular Salted Egg Pork Rice And Fresh Shio Pan
Activity: Check out the events at *SCAPE
Image credit: Evelyn Yong via Google Maps
*SCAPE is one of my favourite activity spaces, and is usually chock-full of things to do. It’s a non-profit community space that supports youths’ interests in the creative arts, meaning there’s usually a wide variety of events, from arts festivals to workshops. While some require paid tickets, there are plenty of upcoming free events.
Image credit: *SCAPE
A current event running from now till 22 November 2026 is *SCAPE’s Singapore Youth Photography Awards 2026 Exhibition , which showcases the competition’s winning works, selected from over 500 submissions by a panel of distinguished judges. The collection is displayed at *SCAPE Whitespace Level 3 , free of charge. If you have an eye for photography and all things creative, take this opportunity to support Singapore’s photography talents.
Image credit: *SCAPE
…

deals.body:
Xiao Jiao Tian, the Sichuan-inspired chain that came to Singapore by way of Fujian, is now open at Wisma Atria. It is the brand’s second outlet here, after City Square Mall in Farrer Park, and it brings the same wok-fired menu to the third floor of an Orchard Road mall.
The headline dish at both is the Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, one of four signatures and the hottest of them, marked with two chilli symbols on the menu.
Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, one of Xiao Jiao Tian’s four signatures. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Who is behind it
Xiao Jiao Tian started in Fujian Province in 2013 and grew across more than 80 kitchens in China before it crossed over. The cooking is Sichuan in spirit but softened for a wider range of palates. Several dishes come with a spice-to-taste option, which helps if one person at the table wants it hot and another does not.
The kitchen’s own rule is that every dish is cooked once it is ordered, with nothing reheated and nothing made the night before. Rice is Wuchang rice from north-east China. The brand also promises that a dish which falls short of its standard is free.
What to order
The four signatures are a good first round for two or three people:
• Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, the spiciest of the four
• Chinese Sauerkraut Fish, sliced fish in a pickled mustard green broth, one chilli on the menu
• Honey Spicy Chicken Bites, also one chilli
• Crispy Roast Chicken, for anyone avoiding heat altogether
Chinese Sauerkraut Fish. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Beyond those, the best-seller section leans towards dishes that go with rice: Sizzling Beef, Golden Claypot Tofu, Steamed Pork Ribs with Rice Flour, Salted Egg Yolk Prawn and a Secret Recipe Grilled Frog. The Sweet and Sour Pork carries the Chinese name for lychee pork, the Fuzhou classic where the meat is scored so it curls up like the fruit, which is a quiet nod to where the brand began.
The full menu runs to 11 sections and more than 50 dishes, plus drinks, including a farmhouse section with Mapo Tofu and Country-Style Stir-Fried Pork, a cordyceps flower chicken soup, and shaved ices such as Golden Osmanthus Longan Ice and Fresh Fig Milk Ice. There is a separate kids’ section with crispy pork, chicken drumettes and fries, and the Steamed Egg with Minced Pork is labelled as a kids’ favourite.
Sizzling Beef, from the best-seller section. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
The menu includes pork and pork intestines, so it is not one for halal diners.
Getting there and booking
Xiao Jiao Tian Wisma Atria is at 435 Orchard Road, #03-32/33/34, Singapore 238877. From Orchard MRT, Exit 3 leads underground into Wisma Atria at Basement 1, and the lifts go up to level three.
It opens from 11.30am to 10pm on weekdays and from 11am to 10pm on weekends, with last orders at 9pm on weekdays and 9.30pm on weekends. The hours are the same at City Square Mall, 180 Kitchener Road, #04-37.
Wisma Atria is walk-in only. Reservations are taken at City Square Mall alone, and only for groups of eight or more, on WhatsApp at +65 8099 7139 or by phone on +65 6312 4698. Delivery is through GrabFood, Foodpanda and Chinatown Delivery.

Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, one of Xiao Jiao Tian’s four signatures. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Who is behind it
Xiao Jiao Tian started in Fujian Province in 2013 and grew across more than 80 kitchens in China before it crossed over. The cooking is Sichuan in spirit but softened for a wider range of palates. Several dishes come with a spice-to-taste option, which helps if one person at the table wants it hot and another does not.
The kitchen’s own rule is that every dish is cooked once it is ordered, with nothing reheated and nothing made the night before. Rice is Wuchang rice from north-east China. The brand also promises that a dish which falls short of its standard is free.
What to order
The four signatures are a good first round for two or three people:
• Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, the spiciest of the four
• Chinese Sauerkraut Fish, sliced fish in a pickled mustard green broth, one chilli on the menu
• Honey Spicy Chicken Bites, also one chilli
• Crispy Roast Chicken, for anyone avoiding heat altogether
Chinese Sauerkraut Fish. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Beyond those, the best-seller section leans towards dishes that go with rice: Sizzling Beef, Golden Claypot Tofu, Steamed Pork Ribs with Rice Flour, Salted Egg Yolk Prawn and a Secret Recipe Grilled Frog. The Sweet and Sour Pork carries the Chinese name for lychee pork, the Fuzhou classic where the meat is scored so it curls up like the fruit, which is a quiet nod to where the brand began.
The full menu runs to 11 sections and more than 50 dishes, plus drinks, including a farmhouse section with Mapo Tofu and Country-Style Stir-Fried Pork, a cordyceps flower chicken soup, and shaved ices such as Golden Osmanthus Longan Ice and Fresh Fig Milk Ice. There is a separate kids’ section with crispy pork, chicken drumettes and fries, and the Steamed Egg with Minced Pork is labelled as a kids’ favourite.
Sizzling Beef, from the best-seller section. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
The menu includes pork and pork intestines, so it is not one for halal diners.
Getting there and booking
Xiao Jiao Tian Wisma Atria is at 435 Orchard Road, #03-32/33/34, Singapore 238877. From Orchard MRT, Exit 3 leads underground into Wisma Atria at Basement 1, and the lifts go up to level three.
It opens from 11.30am to 10pm on weekdays and from 11am to 10pm on weekends, with last orders at 9pm on weekdays and 9.30pm on weekends. The hours are the same at City Square Mall, 180 Kitchener Road, #04-37.
Wisma Atria is walk-in only. Reservations are taken at City Square Mall alone, and only for groups of eight or more, on WhatsApp at +65 8099 7139 or by phone on +65 6312 4698. Delivery is through GrabFood, Foodpanda and Chinatown Delivery.

Tucked away in the bustling basement of Golden Mile Food Centre is Charr’d The Hawker , a vibrant Muslim-owned hawker stall run by 2 friendly young chefs. Don’t expect to find wagyu tomahawks at these hawker tables — despite the similar name, this modest Western stall is completely unrelated to Changi’s famous halal steakhouse.
Helmed by 2 young chefs who previously worked in fine-dining kitchens, their dream of running their own F&B business dates all the way back to their university days at The Culinary Institute of America under the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT). Prior to establishing Charr’d The Hawker, they ran a home-based venture called The Layered Brothers, where they served up lapis rempah , traditional spiced cakes.
Today, they bring expertise picked up from both university and professional kitchens to Golden Mile Food Centre, churning out comfort Western fare.
What to order at Charr’d The Hawker
For my main, I went straight for their bestselling Charr’d Chicken Chop (S$8.50) . It features a crisp chicken chop, a scoop of coleslaw, baked beans, a cup of BBQ sauce, a lightly toasted buttered bun and a choice between garlic butter rice, fries and mashed potato. I opted for the garlic butter rice. Visually, it’s a pretty plate as the colours of the garlic rice and purple cabbage in the coleslaw pop and make it look that much more appetising.
As the stall’s name suggests, I expected nothing less than a perfectly charred protein, and I’m glad to report it delivered. The chicken had a crisp, golden-brown crust that was absolutely delicious and well-seasoned.
The meat didn’t lean as salty as I would have preferred but when dipped in the provided BBQ sauce, it hit all the spots of tangy, spicy and salty. While the sauce was a little watery, I loved how tart it was and how the spice blend lent it a nice warmth.
The chicken fillet was a little thinner than other chicken chops I’ve had in the past, but the crispy skin and seasoning do make up for it.
Although the menu bills it as garlic butter rice, I didn’t pick up much of a garlicky aroma. To me, it tasted a lot more like traditional chicken rice. While it was still tasty, it wasn’t really what I had expected from garlic butter rice.
I appreciated that the rice was cooked nicely — the grains kept a pleasant bite without turning mushy or clumping together.
One of the best elements on the plate for me was the coleslaw. Sporting vibrant orange and purple hues from the shredded carrot and purple cabbage, it was visually appealing. It tasted fresh, helping to cut through the richness of the other components, while its crisp texture added a delightful crunch to every bite. The owner was even kind enough to top up extra coleslaw when I packed up my food to-go after the tasting.
The serving of baked beans was reminiscent of old-school Western hawkers and offered an elevated take on a familiar, old-school staple.
ATECOOKIES.SG: Are these $5.50 NY-style cookies on Beach Road actually worth it?
Next, I moved on to the 2-pc Chicken Wing (S$4) . These absolutely stole the spotlight for me, hitting every mark of what a great fried chicken wing should be. Marinated in yoghurt, the meat stayed wonderfully tender and juicy on the inside.
Outside, the crust boasted a super crispy finish packed with savoury seasoning. Honestly, it was a masterclass in fried chicken wings — flavourful enough that you don’t even need the accompanying chilli sauce.
Who is Charr’d The Hawker best for?
If you’re looking for a comforting, old-school Western-style meal with generous and thoughtfully executed sides, Charr’d The Hawker is well worth a visit. The chefs’ fine-dining background shines through in the little details, elevating familiar hawker staples like the vibrant, crunchy coleslaw. It’s an easy go-to for Muslim diners and groups hunting for hearty and affordable Western fare in the Beach Road area.
How to get to Charr’d The Hawker
Charr’d The Hawker is located on the basement level of Golden Mile Food Centre, which is a quick 7-minute walk from Nicoll Highway MRT Station . The station connects to the MRT Circle Line. Take Exit A and walk along Java Road before turning left onto Beach Road.
If you prefer to travel by bus, alight at Opp St. John HQ (01411) or St. John HQ (01419) along Beach Road. Do note that bus service 961M operates exclusively on Sundays and public holidays, while all other bus services operate daily.
Do we recommend Charr’d The Hawker?
Yes! I thoroughly enjoyed every element of the plate as each felt intentional and was done well. That said, on my next visit, I would opt for the chicken wing set instead of the chicken chop. While the chicken chop had a great crust, the fillet was slightly on the thinner side, whereas the wings were easily the star of the meal.

deals.body:
Base Gelato is a new gelato bar in Joo Chiat
If you’ve recently gone cafe-hopping in Joo Chiat , you’ve probably visited the usual hotspots such as Common Man Coffee Roasters and Elijah Pies . You might, however, miss an unassuming hole-in-the-wall shop that has recently opened right under everyone’s noses. Base Gelato is a new cafe in Joo Chiat by Creamier, selling specialty gelato flavours at nett prices.
How To Spend 12 Hours In Katong: Viral Matcha Cafe, Vintage Shopping And More
The space itself is very cosy and slightly dim. It boasts an industrial look, with natural light seeping in through the glass door.
Their menu is relatively straightforward: there are only six items to choose from. Each flavour of ice cream is specially curated, paired with its own unique accompaniments.
Their signature flavour is the Joo Chiat Heritage ($10) , which pays homage to the locale’s Peranakan history. It features a scoop of refreshing young coconut gelato topped with smoked gula melaka caramel and grated coconut, served alongside a skewer of QQ, house-made ondeh ondeh dango.
For those who prefer stronger flavours, order the Rum Raisin Vanilla Panna Cotta ($12) . The base is a layer of jiggly, silky vanilla panna cotta, made from locally grown Madagascar vanilla pods. It is topped with Jamaican rum-infused gelato and chewy sun-dried Xinjiang raisins for a nice textural contrast.
As a matcha addict, my personal favourite has got to be their Matchagato ($12) .
You can expect kinako, AKA roasted soybean powder, gelato encased in a chewy mochi wrapper and topped with azuki bean paste. Matcha is then hand-whisked right in front of you and poured over the whole shebang. I was pleased to know that their matcha is sourced from Wazakura, a prominent tea-producing region from Uji known for producing matcha that tastes rich with a smooth finish.
For something on the lighter end, the Yoghurt & Honey ($10) features triple-strained Greek yoghurt gelato similar to frozen yoghurt . It is topped with toasted honey fluff and garnished with wildflower honey and locally grown edible flowers.
This was my colleague’s favourite. The gelato was creamy with a slight tang from the yoghurt, while the honey fluff was similar to meringue, adding a nice airiness and sweetness to the dessert.
Image credit: Cindy Tan via Google Maps
We didn’t get to try all of their flavours, but the Black Forest ($12) will probably be a hit among chocolate lovers . This dessert consists of a bittersweet Valrhona Coeur De Guanaja 80% chocolate gelato topped with a dollop of cream and a wild Morello cherry, served alongside a dark chocolate sponge that’s soaked in cherry-infused kirsch.
Image credit: Cindy Tan via Google Maps
Alternatively, their Kaya Butter Toast ($9) is one flavour that nods to the classic Singaporean breakfast. It comprises butter-flavoured gelato and pandan coconut kaya jam sandwiched between two crispy brown toasts.
Overall, the price tag is a little steep for ice cream, but every item at Base Gelato earns its keep. Every flavour we tried was bold yet balanced, and exactly what you want in this sweltering heat.
Base Gelato is a 19-minute walk away from Marine Parade MRT Station . Do take note that it’s takeaway only.
For a full-fledged meal before your gelato treat, read our guide to the best food in Joo Chiat . If you’re not in the area but still craving a sweet treat, check out CHAGEE’s new gelato series .
Address: 198 Joo Chiat Road, #01-01, Singapore 427469
Opening Hours: Fri-Sun 12pm to 7pm
Website
Base Gelato is not halal-certified.
26 Katong And Joo Chiat Food Places: Chocolate Buffet, Legit Tonkatsu And More
Images taken by Chan Zi Xuan.
This was a media tasting at Base Gelato.

Bugis is a food mecca that draws all types of food and people. But sometimes, nothing beats a simple juicy burger. That’s why I can’t wait to sink my teeth into a smashed burger from LOBANG , a hole-in-the-wall joint that serves scintillating burgers at 17 Mohamed Sultan Road .
Their opening came as a surprise, much like their way of serving their burgers .
Credit – Instagram
Notice the shutters? Yeah, even when they’re open, the shutters remain closed. The spot is located in an alley with a tent and some seating for customers to eat. But bear in mind, this is a grab-and-go type of food, so there aren’t many seats.
The entire storefront has a minimalist, yet busy style that a lot of millennials and Gen Z would love. I hate to say this, but this spot is as Instagram-worthy as it gets.
You order by scanning the QR code next to their door. When your order is ready, the shutter will open ever so slightly. A mysterious hand will place your order on the metal table for you to grab. It feels like you’re doing some shady stuff.
Credit – Instagram
The colour palette reminds me heavily of Spider-Punk, one of the many variants of Spider-Man. The music posters are pasted haphazardly, creating a dense layer similar to wallpaper. The neon light buzzes and settles across the pavement. A part of me wishes I had just stumbled onto this place. The mystery and punkish ambience would make for a sick story to tell my friends.
Credit – Instagram
Now, enough about the decor and the vibes. Let’s talk burgers. They offer their normal Smash Burger (S$15) and an upgraded Double Smash Burger (S$18) . Simple and easy but wait till you read what’s in these bad boys.
The burger is made with a blend of beef short rib, brisket and wagyu. The blend of flavour, fat and texture is key to making the ultimate burger.
Credit – Instagram
On top of that, the burger contains caramelised onions and pickles. Those who need some heat (like me) can add their house-made lacto-fermented hot sauce.
A popular pairing with these burgers is a side of their French Fries (S$6) and their Calamansi Soda (S$6) . Personally, if I had to choose between their 4 drink options, I’d definitely go for the Calamansi Soda ; all that rich fat needs some acid to cut through it.
Do note that they only sell 88 burgers daily . While they’re open from 4pm to 12 am , they stop service for the day once they hit that 88-burger quota. I suggest coming earlier so you don’t miss this classic and succulent meal.
You can check if they’re sold out for the day on their Instagram . Also, for my fellow Muslims, all meat used in the burger is Halal-certified.
One Fattened Calf: What makes this burger extraordinary is the homemade potato bun

Now, enough about the decor and the vibes. Let’s talk burgers. They offer their normal Smash Burger (S$15) and an upgraded Double Smash Burger (S$18) . Simple and easy but wait till you read what’s in these bad boys.
The burger is made with a blend of beef short rib, brisket and wagyu. The blend of flavour, fat and texture is key to making the ultimate burger.
Credit – Instagram
On top of that, the burger contains caramelised onions and pickles. Those who need some heat (like me) can add their house-made lacto-fermented hot sauce.
A popular pairing with these burgers is a side of their French Fries (S$6) and their Calamansi Soda (S$6) . Personally, if I had to choose between their 4 drink options, I’d definitely go for the Calamansi Soda ; all that rich fat needs some acid to cut through it.
Do note that they only sell 88 burgers daily . While they’re open from 4pm to 12 am , they stop service for the day once they hit that 88-burger quota. I suggest coming earlier so you don’t miss this classic and succulent meal.
You can check if they’re sold out for the day on their Instagram . Also, for my fellow Muslims, all meat used in the burger is Halal-certified.

NoMad Singapore, the Orchard Road hotel from the New York brand, has opened reservations for all four of its restaurants and bars, and the first menus are out. The hotel itself is due to open in late 2026, with Hilton yet to name a date.
The four are NoMad Grill and Tropicana Club on level 19, Lù Bar by the pool on level five and Sticky Fingers on the ground floor. The menus mix locally inspired flavours with NoMad classics, from bak kut teh dumplings to a soft-serve take on mango sticky rice. LBRD first looked at NoMad Grill in August , before any menus were out.
Dry-aged rib eye at NoMad Grill. Photo: Hilton
NoMad Grill, the steakhouse on level 19
The flagship is a New York chophouse with in-house dry-ageing and live-fire cooking. The main room seats 65, and a private room takes up to 18 people around one table.
Steaks and chops lead the menu, with a raw bar and a seafood plateau that changes with the season. The local touches are grilled snail toast and fried frog legs with black bean, white pepper and curry leaf. On the seafood side there is wasabi yellowtail crudo, razor clams with escabeche and finger lime, and golden snapper in coconut leche de tigre.
The two big-table dishes are a suckling pig and the return of the NoMad Black Truffle Chicken, both served for two to four people. Dessert is a Baked Alaska, finished at the table.
NoMad Grill runs from breakfast to dinner daily: 6.30am to 10.30am, noon to 3pm and 5.30pm to 10.30pm.
Tropicana Club, cocktails and late nights
The name nods to two clubs: Havana’s Tropicana of 1939 and Singapore’s own Tropicana Club of 1968. This one is a cocktail bar with entertainment, also on level 19.
Cuban classics such as the daiquiri and El Presidente sit next to a long martini list, a pandan vesper and a passion fruit and tomato martini, with no- and low-alcohol versions too. The bar food is where Havana meets Singapore: chilli brown crab empanadas with bottarga aioli, bak kut teh dumplings with shiitake, pork belly and white pepper, and seabream ceviche with calamansi.
It opens 5pm to 1am on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, and 5pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday. It is closed on Monday and Tuesday.
Seabream ceviche at Tropicana Club. Photo: Hilton
Sticky Fingers, the soft-serve counter
The 20-seat ground-floor spot changes three times a day. Mornings are coffee from Singapore roaster PPP, house-made viennoiserie and New York-style breakfast sandwiches. Afternoons are soft-serve sundaes, including a Cacio e Pepe Sundae with pecorino, black pepper and olive oil, and the Sticky Mango, which pairs coconut ice cream with vanilla sticky rice and candied peanut. Evenings bring cocktails such as a pandan and coconut Negroni and a banoffee martini. Hours are 8am to 8pm daily.
The Sticky Mango at Sticky Fingers. Photo: Hilton
Lù Bar, by the pool
Lù Bar seats 35 beside the level-five pool, with drinks and small plates including black pepper crab pockets, prawn fresh rolls and a crispy pork belly bánh mì. It opens 9am to 10pm daily.
Prawn fresh rolls at Lù Bar. Photo: Hilton
Booking
Tables at all four go through the NoMad Singapore dining reservations on Hilton’s site. No prices have been published yet for any of the menus. The cocktail list is the work of Leo Robitschek of Sydell Group, a James Beard Award winner for bar programmes, while the food is led by Josh Harnden, a former Eleven Madison Park partner, with Lorenz Hoja, who spent more than ten years with Joël Robuchon, running the Singapore kitchens.

Carousel at Royal Plaza on Scotts started its Christmas buffet on Saturday, and it runs every day until New Year’s Day. Lunch starts at S$92++ a head and dinner at S$118++. Every kitchen in the hotel, Carousel’s open stations included, is halal-certified by MUIS, so the turkey, the roasts and the log cakes are all halal.
This year’s theme is Once Upon A Feast, a storybook Christmas. The festive additions sit on top of the usual Carousel spread: turkey, a log cake, Christmas pudding and stollen, plus a heavier hand with lobster after dark.
Once Upon A Feast, Carousel’s festive buffet, 21 November 2026 to 1 January 2027. Image: Royal Plaza on Scotts
Lunch or dinner: where the money goes
Both sessions share the same base. There is a seafood station with whole Atlantic salmon, blue swimmer crab, mussels, clams, half-shell scallops, tiger prawns and lobster claws. There is a live carving station with a slow-baked Christmas turkey in giblet sauce and BBQ beef striploin, plus teppanyaki, sushi and sashimi, a pasta station and a run of Indian dishes.
Dinner adds the expensive items. Hyogo Bay oysters, boiled Maine lobster and Snow Queen crab legs go on ice, and on weekends the crab legs also come hot and steamed. The dinner specials are a chilli crab chawanmushi, Japanese garlic butter baby lobster, and yuzu miso barramundi with a curry leaf furikake, and the dinner crab section includes tom yum chilli crab with golden mantou.
If the point of the evening is seafood, dinner is the session to book. If the group is mostly there for turkey, roast beef and dessert, lunch covers the same ground for less.
Seafood on ice at the Carousel buffet. Photo: Royal Plaza on Scotts
The festive rates
Prices are per adult and before service charge and GST.
• Monday to Thursday: lunch S$92++, dinner S$118++
• Friday: lunch S$92++, dinner S$128++
• Saturday: lunch S$102++, dinner S$128++
• Sunday: lunch S$102++, dinner S$118++
Carousel counts Sunday dinner as a weekday dinner, so Sunday night is priced like Monday.
The four special dates have their own rates, which replace the usual ones:
• Christmas Eve, Thursday 24 December: lunch S$92++, dinner S$168++
• Christmas Day, Friday 25 December: lunch and dinner both S$138++
• New Year’s Eve, Thursday 31 December: lunch S$92++, dinner S$168++
• New Year’s Day, Friday 1 January: lunch S$98++, dinner S$128++
Children aged 6 to 11 pay half the adult rate, and children under 6 eat free. Tables of 21 or more get 15 per cent off the buffet, except on public holidays or with other offers.
What changes on the big nights
The special dates bring extra dishes on top of the regular spread. On Christmas Eve dinner there is aburi Maine lobster with mentaiko, slipper lobster in a heritage curry with butter croutons, and Carousel’s signature laksa-spiced turkey, stuffed with otah and chestnut. Slow-baked prime ribs come with a truffle lobster risotto.
On New Year’s Eve dinner the headline is Maine lobster braised in Singapore chilli crab sauce, with golden mantou to mop it up. Christmas Day lunch has a golden tempura live station.
The special-date logs are a Chocolat Mochi Log with Valrhona dark chocolate and gula melaka mochi, a Nonya Emerald Yule Log with calamansi confit and caramel miso, and a burnt cheese log.
Taking it home instead
Royal Plaza on Scotts also does a festive takeaway range: whole roast turkey, beef sirloin, lamb, seafood, Nonya roast chicken, hampers and log cakes. Orders go through the hotel’s online shop, with delivery or self-collection from 21 November. Delivery is free on orders of S$120 or more after discounts, and orders of S$1,000 or more before discount take 15 per cent off with the code FESTIVE until 25 December. There is no delivery on 24 and 25 December, only self-collection.
Roasts from the Grand Carvery Hamper in the hotel’s festive takeaway range. Photo: Royal Plaza on Scotts
Getting there
Carousel is at Royal Plaza on Scotts, 25 Scotts Road, Singapore 228220. Bookings go through the hotel’s website, and the hotel’s number is 6589 7799. The hotel says its halal certification is under MUIS’s Eating Establishment Scheme (Food Station), under which alcoholic drinks can still be served with strict controls in place.

Sushiro says on its Instagram that its Great World outlet opens on Tuesday 24 November, with a rotating 1-for-1 sushi plate and S$6++ alcoholic drinks from then until 7 December. Great World lists the promotion as available while stocks last.
An artist’s impression of Sushiro Great World. Image: Sushiro Singapore
The new restaurant sits on the first floor of Great World at 1 Kim Seng Promenade, units #01-112/113/114. It is a Digiro concept store, the second in Singapore after Mandai, so the conveyor belt here is a screen rather than a moving track of plates.
The 1-for-1 plate, date by date
Each 1-for-1 runs for two or three days before the next plate takes over. Sushiro lists this run on its Instagram, with the opening price and the usual price for each plate:
• 24 to 26 November: Bluefin Fatty Tuna, S$5.20++ (usually S$10.40++)
• 27 to 28 November: Big Cut Fresh Tasmanian Salmon, S$3.20++ (usually S$6.40++)
• 29 to 30 November: Salmon Roe Wrap, S$4.20++ (usually S$8.40++)
• 1 to 3 December: Shio Koji Big Red Shrimp, S$3.20++ (usually S$6.40++)
• 4 to 5 December: Medium Fatty Tuna, S$4.20++ (usually S$8.40++)
• 6 to 7 December: Jumbo Scallop, S$5.20++ (usually S$10.40++)
The bluefin fatty tuna in the first three days and the jumbo scallop at the very end are the two dearest plates in the run, so those are the dates to aim for if you are choosing one visit. If salmon is what you order every time anyway, 27 or 28 November is the cheaper trip.
Sushiro says alcoholic drinks are S$6++ each for the full two weeks.
Fatty tuna nigiri. Image: Sushiro Singapore
Opening day only
On 24 November itself, Sushiro says a bill of S$50 or more earns one spin of a sure-win prize wheel, with prizes ranging from S$10 return vouchers to limited-edition merchandise. Terms and conditions apply.
How Digiro works
Instead of plates going round on a belt, a touchscreen panel at the table shows animated sushi plates moving across a digital conveyor. You tap a plate to order it, and the same screen doubles as the menu. Ordering also fills up a progress bar that unlocks mini games featuring Sushiro’s Dakkosushi characters, with a chance to win Dakkosushi merchandise.
If you have been to the Mandai outlet at Mandai Wildlife East, it is the same idea. If you like watching real plates go past before you commit, the screens are the trade-off.
Tuna, ikura, unagi and salmon from Sushiro’s regular menu. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Getting a seat
Reservations go through the Sushiro Singapore app. With a 1-for-1 on from the first day, booking ahead for a weekend dinner is the sensible move.
Great World is also not the last new Sushiro this year. Funan, also a Digiro concept store, is slated for early December at #02-16.
Sushiro Great World details
Address: 1 Kim Seng Promenade, #01-112/113/114, Great World, Singapore 237994
Hours: 11am to 10pm daily, last order 9.30pm
Opening deals: 24 November to 7 December 2026, while stocks last
Prices: before service charge and GST
Reservations: Sushiro Singapore app

World Christmas Market returns from 10 December 2026
Image credit: World Christmas Market
PSA: The Christmas market that drew more than 218,000 people to Marina Bay last year is moving house. World Christmas Market is back for a third edition, now called A Christmas Story by World Christmas Market . It runs from 10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 on the grounds of METT Hotel Singapore and Fort Canning Park . Even better, entry is free for everyone.
We Visited World Christmas Market 2025, A Festive Fair At Bayfront With Over 40 Stalls
The fair started in 2024 at The Promontory at Marina Bay. In 2025, it moved to the much bigger Bayfront Event Space as Togetherland by World Christmas Market .
We went last year and counted over 40 food and drink stalls, from Rollney’s ice cream-stuffed chimney cakes to chilled and grilled oysters at Slurp Your Oysters.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
This year the organisers, DareDreamer, are swapping the waterfront for something greener and more old-school, with the fair spread across the hilltop park and the grounds of the colonial-era hotel.
The fair is split into three zones. The first, The Story Terrace, has festive shopping, gifts, and hands-on workshops. It’s also home to The Long Table, a communal dining setup where you can share a meal with friends or end up chatting with strangers.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
Next is The Piazza, the main square. A 38-foot real Christmas tree stands in the middle, with smaller decorated trees all around it. The third zone, The Merry Grounds, is where the food is. Expect seasonal bites, festive drinks, and plenty of reasons to stick around. If you’re mainly going to eat, start here. The full vendor lineup is still TBD, since the festival is still taking applications from F&B, retail, and craft vendors. We’ll update this article once the stalls are confirmed.
Across the grounds, look out for giant nutcrackers and glowing reindeer, which make good photo backdrops. There’s plenty of music too. A 42-piece orchestra plays on opening weekend. Brass sextets, saxophone quartets, and choirs perform on other dates throughout the season.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
On opening night, 10 December 2026, the gates open at 5pm. The tree-lighting and opening ceremony starts at 7.30pm, so arrive early for a good spot. The fair also stays open until 1am on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve, so it works for a late-night date or a countdown with friends.
In other exciting food news, McDonald’s is launching new Maple BBQ Burgers for a limited time! If you’re watching your spending this month, check out our 12-hour Orchard budget itinerary .
Address: 11 Canning Walk, METT Hotel Singapore, Singapore 178881
Opening hours: Mon-Thurs 5pm to 11pm, Fri-Sun 4pm to 11pm (10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027); 24 and 31 December 4pm to 1am
Website
Orchard On A Budget: How To Spend A Day In Town For Under $30
Feature image adapted from World Christmas Market.
